{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-13T08:46:06.530666+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_bd85b932e1930bff171213fdd880d15813936b076776187f9c9d8a138639e1e6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let g be a norm on R^2 even in the first coordinate (every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm qualifies). Fix a transversal offset h and span length r, and for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) consider F(j) := g((h, j)) + g((h, r-j)) (the second leg g((0,r) - v) = g((-h, r-j)) equals g((h, r-j)) by evenness). F is convex in j (a sum of compositions of g with affine maps) and satisfies F(r - j) = F(j), so it is symmetric about j = r/2 and therefore minimized there: F(j) >= F(r/2) for EVERY real j, including j < 0 and j > r. Consequence: any lower bound on the dogleg excess assumed only for the MIDPOINT-displaced point (the enclosing-ball statement as classically printed) extends free of charge to every longitudinal position at the same transversal offset - for axis-aligned spans, the 'displaced point arbitrary at its distance' reading is a theorem, not an added assumption. For tilted spans the reflection symmetry fails and the extension is genuinely false (measured deficits up to 4.5 percent at small tilts), so this reduction is exactly the boundary of what symmetry buys. Verified: zero violations over 80,000 fresh trials on four norms (weighted p-norms and a polygonal norm), worst ratio 1 + 2e-12; independently verified by its originating referee at zero violations over 5 norms x 3 scales x 5 offsets x 1401 positions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:28.472350+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bd8e2a6eb5d89c2a1884460e74e64ed21ed28d432677308925b651e8638141ba","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 46 (Conditional one-leg recovery) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $2\le r<\infty$, let $\cH_0,D,R$ be Hilbert spaces, and let
$(e_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be a finite orthonormal system in $\cH_0$.
For $A_a\in\Sch_r(D,R)$, define
\[
 \operatorname{Col}(A)x:=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}e_a\otimes A_ax,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Row}(A)
 \left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\conj{e_a}\otimes x_a\right)
 :=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}A_ax_a.
\]
If $X=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_aA_a$, where the $g_a$ are independent
standard real Gaussians or normalized circular complex Gaussians, then
\begin{align}

 \norm{\operatorname{Col}(A)}_{\Sch_r}^2
 &\le\mathbb E\norm X_{\Sch_r}^2,
 \notag\\
 \norm{\operatorname{Row}(A)}_{\Sch_r}^2
 &\le\mathbb E\norm X_{\Sch_r}^2.
\end{align}
The inequalities remain valid pointwise, and hence conditionally, when the
$A_a$ depend measurably on an auxiliary variable independent of
$(g_a)_a$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:20:15.584932+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bda04e7f40323579d237bb825d0b41a752af6cdc3e28266bafa3f02e8bf1ab82","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:admissible-classes of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Suppose that $P\nmid rd$.  There is a set
$\mathcal R_{r,d}(Q)\subset\mathbb Z/d^2\mathbb Z$ such that
\[
\mathcal A_{r,d}(Q)
=
\left\{
N\in\mathbb Z_{>0}:
\mu^2(N)=1,\ P\nmid N,\
N\bmod d^2\in\mathcal R_{r,d}(Q)
\right\}.
\]
Every class in $\mathcal R_{r,d}(Q)$ is coprime to $d$, and
\[
\#\mathcal R_{r,d}(Q)
=
\begin{cases}
1,&(r,d)=1,\quad 2\nmid rd,\\
1,&(r,d)=1,\quad 2\mid r,\\
1,&(r,d)=2,\quad 2\Vert d,\\
2,&(r,d)=2,\quad 4\mid d,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
If $d$ is even, every integer represented by an admissible class is odd.
Writing
\[
s=\frac{N(r^2N-4Q)}{d^2},
\]
the parity information is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{case}&\text{parity of }s\\ \hline
2\Vert d,\ 2\Vert r&\text{even}\\
2\Vert d,\ 4\mid r&\text{odd}\\
4\mid d&\text{one even class and one odd class}.
\end{array}
\]
In particular, the number and parity type of these classes are independent of $k$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.755748+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bda7079c62c6c3aa27f6e01b86d25032fd0808ca4fe797e03db2e87e3c8dac83","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume conditions \((A)\) and \((B)\), and the positivity condition
\begin{equation}
        \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
        \mathbb Q\left(
        Z_N(\beta_N;\bar\omega)
        <
        \delta\,
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q}[Z_N(\beta_N;\bar\omega)]
        \right)=0 .
\end{equation}
Let \(k_N\) be as in \eqref{eq:kN-section2}.  If \(\alpha>3/H\), assume
\[
        \sup_{N\ge1}\beta_NN^{H/2}<\infty .
\]
Put
\[
        \kappa:=\frac{\alpha H}{2}-\frac32>0
\]
and define
\begin{equation}
A_*(\alpha, H) := \sup_{1/2 < p < \min\{1,\, 1/2 + \kappa\}} \min\left\{
\frac12 + \kappa - p\left(H - \frac12\right),\,
\frac14 + \frac{\kappa}{2} + p(1 - H)
\right\}

\end{equation}
Then, for every \(0<a<A_*(\alpha,H)\),
\[
        N^a\left|

        \log Z_N(\beta_N;\bar\omega)
        \right|
        \xrightarrow{\mathbb Q}0 .
\]
If \(2<\alpha\le3/H\), assume
\[
        \beta_N=\beta\, l(N^{3/2})^{-1},
        \qquad \beta>0,
\]
and set
\[
        a_N:=\beta_NN^{H/2}.
\]
Then
\[
        \frac{
        \log Z_N(\beta_N;\omega)
        -
        \log Z_N(\beta_N;\bar\omega)}
        {a_N}
        \xrightarrow{\mathbb Q}0 .
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:20:33.755725+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bdab94d6dc55189695d026f0ba5482683d76fc5a471b7f35270ed45a35685535","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 48 (\cite{Falk01}*{Theorem 3.7}) of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] \label[Thm]{prop:tensorreducedos}
    Let $M$ and $N$ be matroids and let us identify the symbol $f$ with an element in each.
    Then we have the graded $\QQ$-algebra isomorphism
    \[
        \rOS(P_{f}(M, N)) \cong \rOS(M)\otimes_{\QQ} \rOS(N).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        Let $E_0 = E(M) - \{f\}$ and $E_1 = E(N) - \{f\}$.
        We will prove the isomorphism 
        $$\OS(\mathbf{d}_f P_{f}(M, N)) \cong \OS(\mathbf{d}_f M)\otimes_{\QQ} \OS(\mathbf{d}_f N).$$
        Both sides are canonically quotients of the free exterior algebra 
        $A = \bigwedge(E_0 \sqcup E_1)$.
        We will show that the kernel ideals are equal.
        As discussed in \Cref{subsec:OS_algebras},
        $\OS(\mathbf{d}_f P_{f}(M, N))$ is the quotient of $A$ by 
        (i) the monomials 
        $e_D$ for subets $D \subseteq E_0 \sqcup E_1$ containing $f$ in their span
        and (ii) the elements $\partial e_C$ for all circuits of $P_f(M, N)\del f$.
        Since a subset of $E_0$ (or $E_1$) spanning $f$ still spans it in $P_f(M, N)$ and since every circuit of $M \del f$ (or $N \del f$) is a circuit of $P_f(M, N) \del f$, every relation in the defining ideal of 
        $\rOS(M)\otimes_{\QQ} \rOS(N)$ lies in the defining ideal of
        $\OS(\mathbf{d}_f P_{f}(M, N))$. The converse follows from the following two observations:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item If $D \subseteq E_0 \sqcup E_1$ contains $f$ in its span in $P_f(M, N)$, then so does at least one of $D \cap E_0$ or $D \cap E_1$.
            \item If $C \subseteq E_0 \sqcup E_1$ is a circuit of $P_f(M, N)$ then either $C \subseteq E_0$, or 
            $C \subseteq E_1$, or else both 
            $C \cap E_0$ and $C \cap E_1$ contain $f$ in their span.
        \end{itemize}
        The first observation shows that every element of type (i) in the defining ideal of $\OS(\mathbf{d}_f P_{f}(M, N))$ is a multiple of an element of type (i) in the defining ideal of 
        $\rOS(M)\otimes_{\QQ} \rOS(N)$. 
        The second observation shows that every element of type (ii) in the defining ideal of $\OS(\mathbf{d}_f P_{f}(M, N))$ is either equal, up to sign, to a type (ii) element for $\rOS(M)\otimes_{\QQ} \rOS(N)$ or else every term in its expansion into monomials is a multiple of an element of type (i) in the defining ideal of $\rOS(M)\otimes_{\QQ} \rOS(N)$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

	\[
	\zeta^T(t)\coloneqq\sum_{\boldsymbol{k}\in D_t} \prod_{v\in V(t)} \frac{1}{k_v^{n_v}},
	\]
	where $D_t$ is the set defined by:
	\[
	\left\{ (k_v)_{v\in V(t)}\in(\N^*)^{| V(t)|} \,\middle|\, \forall (v,u)\in  V(t)^2 , k_v<k_u \text{ if } u< v  \right\},

    \[

    \]
    where $\Delta_t\subseteq \interff{0 1}^{| V(t)|}$ stands for:
    \[ 
    \left\{ \left(t_{v_1},\dots, t_{v_{| V(t)|}}\right) \,\middle|\, \forall (i,j)\in\IEM{1}{| V(t)|}^2, t_{v_i}> t_{v_j} \text{ if } v_i < v_j  \right\},
    \] 

    where for any $(u,v)\in V(t)^2, u< v$ reading the tree as a Hasse diagram where the root is the minimum of the poset and 
    \begin{align*}
    	g_x:\left\lbrace\begin{array}{rcl}

    	\end{array} \right. &&
    	g_y:\left\lbrace\begin{array}{rcl}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:50:36.760796+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bdb8b93b90fdd83991c0d2b7b141ca95f2141f24a5f84c40bb1aef406ebdd65e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 58 of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $\ell_\eps: \RR^d \to [1,\infty)$ be a smooth function possibly depending on $\eps$. We say it is an admissible scale if for any multi-index $\beta \in \NN^d$ there holds 
$$
|\partial_\xi^\beta \ell_\eps(\xi)| \leq C_\beta \ell_\eps(\xi)^{1-|\beta|}.
$$
Furthermore, we call a smooth positive function $m_\eps(\xi)$ an admissible order function if there are constants $C,M>0$ so that 
$$
\frac{m_\eps(\zeta)}{m_\eps(\xi)} \leq C\left (1+\frac{|\zeta-\xi|}{\ell_\eps(\xi)^{1/2}} \right )^M \left (1+\frac{|\zeta-\xi|}{\ell_\eps(\zeta)^{1/2}} \right )^M,
$$
and there holds the estimate
$$
|\partial_\xi^\beta m_\eps(\xi)|\leq C_\beta m_\eps(\xi) \ell_\eps(\xi)^{-|\beta|}.
$$
We write $a_\eps(x,t,\xi,\lambda) \in S_\eps(m_\eps;\ell_\eps)$ if 
$$
\| \partial_\xi^\beta \partial_x^\alpha \partial_t^\gamma a_\eps(x,t,\xi,\lambda)\|_{L^\infty} \leq C_{\beta,\alpha,\gamma}m_\eps(\xi)\ell_\eps(\xi)^{-|\beta|}, 
$$
and set the corresponding seminorm 
$$
|a_\eps|_{m,\ell,K}=\max_{|\alpha|+|\beta|+|\gamma| \leq K}  \sup_{\xi \in \RR^d, \lambda \in K_\lambda}\ell(\xi)^{|\beta|}m(\xi)^{-1}\| \partial_\xi^\beta \partial_x^\alpha \partial_t^\gamma a_\eps(x,t,\xi,\lambda)\|_{L^\infty}.
$$
In the special case where $\ell_\eps=\langle \xi \rangle$, we simply write $a_\eps \in S_\eps(m_\eps)$.
Given a symbol, we may quantise it using the usual Kohn-Nirenberg quantisation on the torus. Indeed, given $f \in C^\infty(\TT^2)$, we define 
\begin{equation}

\Op_x(a_\eps) f=\sum_{k \in \ZZ^2}a_\eps(x,t,2 \pi k,\lambda)\e^{2 \pi ix\cdot k} \widehat f(k),
\end{equation}
where the frequency variable is $\xi=2 \pi k$.","status":"unverified"}

\[
  \rho_u=u^{-2/\alpha}
  \quad\text{in the stationary case and when }\alpha<\beta,
  \qquad

\]
and let \(E_u=[0,T]\ominus\rho_uF\).  Then the conclusions of
Theorems~\ref{thm:stationary_case} and~\ref{thm:main_theorem} remain valid after
replacing
\[
  \{\Gamma_{[0,T]}(\uu(\bm X-u\bm b))>L_u\}
  \quad\text{by}\quad

       >L\rho_u^{\lambda_\Gamma}\},

and replacing every local \(\Gamma_E\) in a limiting constant by
\(\Gamma_{E;F}\).  In particular, the powers of \(u\) in the main formulae
are unchanged; only the limiting constants acquire the fixed footprint \(F\).

If \(F\in\mathcal K_0^+\), the same transfer applies to

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.509121+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be0a6f667ff0970c536bbb39df4dc0315fc379b9e845ae9e00b87169547d3225","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:collapse of arXiv:2607.14266, 'The Swapping Mechanism for Interacting Diffusions: Framework, Comparison with Switching, a'] If we first let $s\to\infty$ (so that the fast-swap limit
		(equation eq:fast-rate of the paper) is attained) and afterwards let $t\to\infty$
		under the diffusive scaling
		\[
		\xi=\frac{x-(\frac{x_0+y_0}{2}+\bar\mu t)}
		{\sqrt{(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)t/2}},\qquad
		\eta=\frac{y-(\frac{x_0+y_0}{2}+\bar\mu t)}
		{\sqrt{(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)t/2}},
		\]
		with $\bar\mu=(\mu_1+\mu_2)/2$, then the two Gaussian clouds that form
		the fast-swap mixture merge into a single isotropic planar normal:
		\[
		p(x,y,t)\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y
		\;\longrightarrow\;
		\frac{1}{2\pi}\,e^{-(\xi^2+\eta^2)/2}\,\mathrm{d}\xi\,\mathrm{d}\eta.
		\]
		In this double limit the individual diffusivities are homogenised to the
		effective value $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}^2=(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)/2$, and
		the memory of the initial assignment is completely lost. A natural
		estimate for the collapse time is
		\[
		t_{\mathrm{coll}}\simeq \max\!\Bigl\{
		\frac{(x_0-y_0)^2}{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2},\;
		\frac{|x_0-y_0|}{|\mu_1-\mu_2|},\;

		\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:32:19.991063+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be291be9e788519bf3de8afb6521646e3894253da901b99221881f1d74ced760","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 (Markov kernel) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] A \emph{Markov kernel} on $(\XX,\XXA)$ is a map
\[
  T : \XXA \times \XX \longrightarrow [0,1], \qquad (A,x) \longmapsto T(A \mid x),
\]
such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]

The \emph{$n$-step kernels} are defined recursively by
$T^{0}(A \mid x) := \ind_{A}(x)$ and
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.576199+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be31b7c28ac42b0f6c8bc15337a14440a4424efdd8ef42e6e1029c44519f285b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $(\xi_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ be independent random variables such that $\E \xi_i=0, \Var(\xi_i)=1$, and for some $M>0$

	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^n w_iw_i^\top\succeq I_m,

	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the cleaners compared are consistent for the population covariance (sample, eta-RIE without floor, LW2020, NERCOME)","the ensemble error covariance is rank-deficient in practice (members near-collinear), so the unconstrained plug-in has near-null sample directions"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T07:07:18.954358+00:00","domain":"ensemble learning / covariance estimation","id":"claim_be3490f4cbcedf62ac943e2d6db3d9c77b884a50d5bcd0fb5f57c27a6283efd2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Read the ladder result (every consistent cleaner ties inside the long-only stack; floors and linear shrinkage lose) through the entrywise bound. Unconstrained minimum variance depends on $\\hat\\Sigma^{-1}$, so its error is governed by the SPECTRUM of $\\hat\\Sigma$: the ratio $q = M/n$, the bulk edge, the near-null directions - the territory of random-matrix cleaning, where the Ledoit-Peche oracle, its analytical estimate and NERCOME differ from the sample covariance by design. The long-only plug-in's excess risk is bounded by twice the ENTRYWISE error $\\varepsilon = \\max_{ij}|\\hat\\Sigma_{ij} - \\Sigma_{ij}|$, which is $O(\\sqrt{\\log M/n})$ for the sample covariance and of the same order for every consistent estimator (a consistent nonlinear shrinkage moves the eigenvalues by $O(n^{-1/2})$ relative, hence the entries by the same order) - so all of them obey the same bound and, on the well-conditioned active submatrix, produce the same weights. A fixed floor $f\\sigma^2$ on the small eigenvalues, or a linear shrinkage $\\rho(\\mu I - \\hat\\Sigma)$, is a BIAS of size $f\\sigma^2$ (or $\\rho|\\mu - \\Sigma_{ii}|$) in the entries spanned by those directions that does not vanish with $n$; it cannot tighten the bound and it displaces the plug-in wherever an active member has weight in a floored direction. With case weights $s_i$ (the per-sample relative metric $s_i = 1/\\|y_i\\|^2$) the bound holds with $n$ replaced by the effective sample size $n_{\\mathrm{eff}} = (\\sum s_i)^2/\\sum s_i^2$, which a few tiny-norm cases can make much smaller than $n$: that is why the relative-metric fit overfits without the constraint and why the long-only form still pays a little at very small $n$. Measured on the EMIT pool (2026-09-05, seed 101): the bound holds on every output of Y1/Y2/Y4 at n = 932 and of Y2/Y4 at n = 60, and is loose by one to three orders of magnitude (median $2\u000barepsilon$ over the oracle risk 10-1000 against a realised excess of 0.02-0.5 at full calibration) - it delivers finiteness and the right dependence, not a tight number; the unconstrained plug-in on the same matrices carries weights of median absolute size 68,000 on Y1 and 1,800 on Y2; the effective sample size of the $1/\\|y\\|^2$ weighting is 150 of 932 rows on Y2 (615 on Y1) and 8.7 of 60 in the $n = 60$ arm.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.677433+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be37c35dd8e8626d6e81d895300bd851c3840c0ce9e91ed55947f6e3741fa678","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 16 (Equivalence of lossless response charts) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let, for $i=1,2$,

restrict to mutually inverse homeomorphisms

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. summands with mean zero and finite variance","the constant sqrt(2) inside the normalisation is not adjustable; it is the correct almost sure envelope"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:40.781780+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be6c233b3f80b2ad7b180f07b82c12b5a10e4b84732b718a58c52d3c3540a594","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, X_2, ... be i.i.d. with E[X_1] = 0 and E[X_1^2] = sigma^2 < infinity, and let S_n = X_1 + ... + X_n. Then almost surely limsup_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) = sigma and liminf_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) = - sigma. Consequently the set of limit points of S_n / sqrt(2 n log log n) is exactly the interval [-sigma, sigma], and the sequence oscillates: it comes arbitrarily close to both endpoints infinitely often and does not converge. STRASSEN'S CONVERSE: if limsup_n |S_n| / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) < infinity with positive probability, then E[X_1] = 0 and E[X_1^2] < infinity, so the two-moment hypothesis is exactly right and not merely convenient. The theorem sits strictly between the strong law, which says S_n/n -> 0, and the central limit theorem, which describes S_n/sqrt(n) in distribution but says nothing about the almost sure oscillation; in particular the CLT does NOT imply that S_n/sqrt(n) is almost surely bounded, and indeed it is not - the iterated logarithm is the correct almost sure envelope. [Hartman and Wintner (1941); Strassen (1966); see Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 8.5.2]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:20.964338+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be9b1fb39d6c7713f063f10f6e9f0b7d92dcb7d0d9ad019434d8b95f969bab76","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 32 (Limit Theorems for the edge count) of arXiv:2605.28776, 'Limiting distributions of triangle counts in linear preferential attachment models'] The following convergences hold as $\lambda\to\infty$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:29:14.981580+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_be9d0e08793ebc333766b42715a8672010ee862c2274792e4c465b0f770cc81c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theo of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $(\mathcal{T}_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a sequence of size-conditioned simply generated trees of

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.985052+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bea4fd85ba321d8d7e0e90b6f3b495ae071c8ef7af75a2d829117486a75b4ab8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:gluing_good of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Suppose that $d=3\alpha$ and that the modified hydrodynamic condition does \emph{not} hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item If $\liminf_{r\to \infty} r^{-\alpha}\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K|<\infty$, then 
 there exist constants $\delta>0$ and $C<\infty$ and an unbounded set $\mathscr{R} =\{r_1,r_2,\ldots\} \subset [1,\infty)$ 
with $r_{i+1} \geq 32r_i$ for every $i \geq 1$ such that  $\sup_{r\in \mathscr{R}} r^{-\alpha}\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K|<\infty$ and

for every $n,N \geq 1$, $r \geq r_{n+N}$, and $y\in \mathbb Z^d$ with $\|y\|\leq r_{n+1}$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.333789+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bea75eccc5ca175e75dc4cbc9b5eeb06b53fb671db990a23f8d44d43142545f2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2512.05466, 'Stochastic Flows and Marked Stable Processes'] (\cite[Proposition 2.10]{AWYskew})
 Let $\overline{\delta}\colon \bR \to \bR$ be a drift function, $\cS$ be a general $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow
 and $\cS^*$ be its dual as in \eqref{def:dual}. The following statements hold almost surely.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For any $r<x$, $b\ge 0$ and $a\ge \cS^*_{-x,-r}(b)$,  we have $\cS_{r,x}(a)>b$ and 
\begin{equation}
    \cS_{r,y}(a)\ge \cS^*_{-x,-y}(b),\qquad  y\in [r,x].

Moreover  $\cS_{r,y}(a)> \cS^*_{-x,-y}(b)$ if $y\in (r,x)$ and $\cS_{r,y}(a)>0$.

\[
\cS_{r,y}(a')\le \cS^*_{-x,-y}(b),\qquad  y\in [r,x].
\]
 Moreover $\cS_{r,y}(a')< \cS^*_{-x,-y}(b)$ if  $y\in (r,x)$  and $\cS^*_{-x,-y}(b)>0$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.565635+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bea97aca44702c78b2ce673462417cc878740b9d196c18c89a96b92f3baac5ac","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian...'] We construct and characterize the one-parameter family of real-valued processes that allow to recover the law of a Brownian loop-soup of any intensity on the real line conditionally on its occupation time field. These processes generalize the Brownian burglar constructed by Warren and Yor (that corresponds to our process in the limiting case where the intensity vanishes and there is just one Brownian motion). These processes are closely related to the Bass-Burdzy flow and recent work of A\\\"id\\'ekon, Hu and Shi on the stochastic Jacobi flow. Our approach uses a formalism, building on the notion of driver processes, where one considers the evolving object to be the line that we ``stretch\", instead of the burglar itself and its remaining occupation time. This leads to a characterization of these (generalized) Brownian burglars by simple natural axioms. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:25:44.986324+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_beaecea872195873154b0fad3849e46fe9612847e86ace3fa25155ff8fadaee8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 (mass control of compensator measures) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let $X$ and $\{X^n\}_{n\ge1}$ be c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,t]$ with jump measures

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.686226+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bed4cbe665408f418a1960f3f2128acde96f4b12d6be79fdd452ec4031e4ba61","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 (Entire parameter dependence) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $q,r\geq1$ and $T_0>0$, write $I=I_q$, let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r:[0,T_0]\to\C$ be continuous bounded-variation paths, and let $K_1,\ldots,K_r:[0,T_0]\to M_q(\C)$ be continuous. Write
\[
\norm{K_j}_{\infty}=\sup_{0\leq s\leq T_0}\norm{K_j(s)}.
\]
For $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)\in\C^r$, let $V^u$ solve
\[
\dd V_s^u
 =V_s^u\sum_{j=1}^r u_j K_j(s)\dd\xi_j(s),
\qquad
V_0^u=I.
\]
Then $u\mapsto V_{T_0}^u$ is entire on $\C^r$.
Its Picard series converges absolutely and locally uniformly, and
\begin{equation}
\norm{V_{T_0}^u}
 \leq
 \exp\!\left(
   \sum_{j=1}^r
   \abs{u_j}\,\norm{K_j}_{\infty}\,
   \Var(\xi_j;[0,T_0])
 \right).
\end{equation}
All mixed derivatives may be computed term by term from the Picard series.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.367411+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bee1edf13eced449987f9cb2c5cf074c3c0bbb93f875b46f5f9e8d9ed640a840","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:antiHN of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] An \textbf{ascending-phase filtration} of an object $E\in\cA$ is a filtration 
    \[
    0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\cdots\subset E_n=E
    \]
    such that $0\neq A_i\coloneqq E_i/E_{i-1}$ are semistable for $i=1,\ldots,n$ with strictly ascending phases $\phi(A_1)<\phi(A_2)<\cdots<\phi(A_n)$. We write $E_{\leq\phi}\coloneqq E_k$, where $k=\max\left(\{0\}\cup\{i\mid\phi(A_i)\leq\phi\}\right)$ and regard the collection $(E_{\leq\phi})_\phi$ as an ascending $[0,1]$-filtration of $E$.

    If $E,F\in\cA$ are equipped with ascending-phase filtrations $(E_{\leq\phi})_\phi$, $(F_{\leq\phi})_\phi$, then a morphism $f\colon E\to F$ is said to be \textit{compatible} if it is filtration preserving, i.e.\ $f(E_{\leq\phi})\subseteq F_{\leq\phi}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.349683+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bef4771e153a1f5e86b37a54bbe4a60748ab9c190eab12bc6913e7cd9c207f24","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 172 (eighth moment bounds for $X^{\RomII}$, $X^{\trunc,\RomII}$, and $X^{\frozen,\RomII}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $(a(q_d):0\le d\le \dmax)$
and $(a^\frozen(q_d):0\le d\le \dmax)$
be sampled as in Definition~\ref{d:rerand}.
For $N$ large enough, we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[\bigg(
	\sum_{\ell=a}^{b-1} 
	\Delta X^{\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))
	\bigg)^8\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4
	\]
for all $0\le a\le b\le \dmax$. The same bound holds 
with $\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$
or $\Delta X^{\frozen,\RomII}(q_d,a^\frozen(q_{d+1}))$
in place of $\Delta X^{\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$.

\begin{proof}
Let $\Delta_d$ be as in Remark~\ref{r:fourth.mmt}. We first define the (high probability) events
	\beq
	E_d\equiv \bigg\{
	\frac{\|\bar{\bg}(q_d)\|^2}{N} \le 2
	\bigg\} \in \cFt(q_d)\,,\quad
	E_\star=\bigcap_{d=a}^{b-1} E_d\,.
	\eeq
It follows using Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} (with $\cFt(q_d)$ in place of $\cG(q_d)$, as discussed above) that, for any $\vartheta\in\R$,
	\[
	\ind\{E_d\}
	\E\Big[ \exp(\vartheta \Delta_d) \,\Big|\,\cFt(q_d)\Big]
	\le \ind\{E_d\}
	\exp \bigg\{ L^{O(1)} \delta
	\vartheta^2 \frac{\|\bar{\bg}(q_d)\|^2}{N} 
	\bigg\}
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} \delta\vartheta^2\Big)\,.
	\]
Recall that $\Delta_{a,b} \equiv \Delta_a + \ldots + \Delta_{b-1}$. Then
	\begin{align*}
	&\E\Big[ \exp( \vartheta \Delta_{a,b})
		\ind\{E_\star\} \,\Big|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\Big]
	=\E\bigg[ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-1} \Delta_d\bigg)
		\ind\{E_\star\}
		\,\bigg|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\bigg] \\
	&\qquad=
	\bigg\{ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-2} \Delta_d\bigg)
	\prod_{d=a}^{b-2} \ind\{E_d\}\bigg\}
	\cdot
	\ind\{E_{b-1}\}
	\E\Big[ \exp(\vartheta \Delta_{b-1})
		\,\Big|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\Big]\\
	&\qquad\le
	\bigg\{ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-2} \Delta_d\bigg)
	\prod_{d=a}^{b-2} \ind\{E_d\}\bigg\}
	\cdot \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} \delta\vartheta^2\Big)\,.
	\end{align*}
Applying the same argument recursively gives
	\[
	\E\Big[ \exp( \vartheta \Delta_{a,b})
	\ind\{E_\star\}\Big]
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} (b-a) \delta \vartheta^2\Big)
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a) \vartheta^2\Big)
	\]
It follows by a Chernoff bound (using only $\P(E_\star)\ge1/2$)
	\[
	\P( |\Delta_{a,b}| \ge y \,|\,E_\star)
	\le 2 \exp\bigg( -\frac{y^2}{4 L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)}\bigg)\,,
	\]
and integrating this bound gives (cf.\ \eqref{e:subgaus.mmt})
	\[
	\E\Big[ (\Delta_{a,b})^8 \,\Big|\, E_\star\Big]
	\le \int_0^\infty 8y^{7}
	\P( |\Delta_{a,b}| \ge y \,|\,E_\star)\,dy
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4\,.
	\]
On the event $(E_\star)^c$ we can use the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality to bound
	\[
	\E\Big[ (\Delta_{a,b})^8 ; (E_\star)^c\Big]
	\le \Big( \E[(\Delta_{a,b})^{16}] \P(( E_\star)^c) \Big)^{1/2}
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4}{\delta^{O(1)}\exp(\Omega(N))}\,,
	\]
where the bound on $\E[(\Delta_{a,b})^{16}]$ follows very similarly to \eqref{e:weak.fourth.mmt.bound}. This is negligible since we assume  $\delta\gg 1/N$ (see Assumption~\ref{a:params}), and the claim follows.  It is straightforward to verify that the same argument applies with $X^{\trunc,\RomII}$ or $X^{\frozen,\RomII}$ in place of $X^{\RomII}$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:51:12.741713+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_befae574d8016467a297e0df9d0f01df39466d0f8c891870209547f4a30247d4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 26 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{Real trees}) 
Let $(T, d)$ be a metric space; it is a {\it real tree} {if and only if} the following holds true.

\smallskip

\noi
\textbf{(a)} For any $\sigma_1, \sigma_2 \! \in\!  T$, there is a unique isometry 
$f:[0,d(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)] \! \rightarrow \! T$ such
that $f(0)\!=\! \sigma_1$ and $f(d(\sigma_1,\sigma_2))\! =\! \sigma_2$. Then, we set 
$\lgeo \sigma_1,\sigma_2\rgeo \! :=\! f([0,d (\sigma_1,\sigma_2)])$. 

\smallskip

\noi
\textbf{(b)} For any continuous injective function 
$g: [0, 1] \! \rightarrow \! T$, such that $g(0)=\sigma_1$ and $g(1)=\sigma_2$,  $g([0,1]) \! = \! \lgeo \sigma_1,\sigma_2\rgeo$. \cq","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543499+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bf1628660619b55d7ec07f62522563b7d539708a5746d597fc84c4bf7fb10937","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The PROBABILISTS' Hermite polynomials He_n are defined by He_n(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2/2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2/2}, equivalently by the generating function exp(t x - t^2/2) = sum_{n >= 0} t^n He_n(x)/n!. Hence { He_n / sqrt(n!) } is an ORTHONORMAL BASIS of L^2 of the standard Gaussian measure on R, and the normalised basis satisfies the derivative relation d/dx ( He_n/sqrt(n!) ) = sqrt(n) ( He_{n-1}/sqrt((n-1)!) ). The PHYSICISTS' Hermite polynomials H_n(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2} are orthogonal with respect to the weight e^{-x^2} instead, and the two families are related by H_n(x) = 2^{n/2} He_n( sqrt(2) x ), equivalently He_n(x) = 2^{-n/2} H_n( x / sqrt(2) ). Use the displacement coordinates

\[
\widehat H_{\mathfrak h}\in BV_c(\R^{2d})
\]
holds.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:53:51.332475+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bf41b71fd053fffc3f9c7aed494319fa28083c3081e8755d2cc9d839aae9902c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:A5 of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Suppose Assumptions~(A1)--(A4) hold but (A5) is dropped.
Define
\begin{equation}
\rho_{12} := \frac{\lambda_1^{1/\alpha_1}}{\lambda_2^{1/\alpha_2}} \in (0,\infty),
\end{equation}
so that $\varepsilon_T^1/\varepsilon_T^2 \to \rho_{12}$ as $T\to\infty$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textbf{Modified cross-kernel.}
The renormalized cross-kernel $\tilde h_T$ (introduced in Section~(sec:cross-kernel of the paper), eq.~(equation eq:hT-def of the paper)) converges in
$L^2(\mathbb R_+)$ to
\begin{equation}
L_{12}^{(\rho)}
:= b_\infty^{12}\|\psi^{12}\|_1 \cdot (K_1 * K_2^{(\rho_{12})}),
\end{equation}
where $K_2^{(\rho_{12})}(t) := \rho_{12}^{-1}\,K_2(t/\rho_{12})$ is the
Mittag-Leffler kernel of the second component time-rescaled by $\rho_{12}$.
Under (A5), $\rho_{12}=1$ and $L_{12}^{(\rho)}=L_{12}$.

\item \textbf{C-tightness.}
The bivariate C-tightness of Proposition~(prop:tightness of the paper) remains valid
without (A5), with $L_{12}$ replaced by $L_{12}^{(\rho)}$.
The Hölder exponent of the cross-term is still $2(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)-1>2\alpha_2-1$,
since time-rescaling by $\rho_{12}$ does not change the singularity exponent.

\item \textbf{Modified limit system.}
The limit $(V^1,V^2)$ satisfies the limiting system~(equation eq:main-limit1 of the paper)--(equation eq:main-limit2 of the paper)
with $L_{12}$ replaced by $L_{12}^{(\rho)}$.
All subsequent results (Theorem~(thm:ALP-extension of the paper), uniqueness,
and Corollary~(cor:rho of the paper)) hold with this replacement, with the
decorrelation constant $C_\varrho$ modified by the factor $\rho_{12}^{\alpha_2-1}$
in the prefactor of $K_2^{(\rho_{12})}$.

\item \textbf{Reduction to (A5).}
Condition~(A5) is imposed for notational simplicity.
Without it, the same argument yields a time-rescaled cross-kernel
as described in part~(i); the parametric reparametrisation
$\lambda_2 \leftarrow \lambda_2\,\rho_{12}^{\alpha_2}$
(corresponding to a deterministic time-change of the second component's
near-criticality rate) recovers the form stated under (A5).
The restriction is therefore one of parametric normalisation, not structural content.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:25:41.601600+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bf50b17597c7e1217a3aa2bf875ac677ca675e087fe0615086a73f11279a9ea1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 66 of arXiv:2608.12947, 'Branch-stationary max-stable fields on rooted trees'] For \(v\in K\), define

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593770+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bf5c9207a7fe4d256725406cf68ff6894d76aad2bf0a98de44f2e7999b604320","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02711, 'Differentiability of the Leading Lyapunov Exponent \\\\ of a linear differential equation...'] The study of evolution in temporally fluctuating environments often relies on the analysis of Lyapunov exponents, which quantify the exponential growth of populations. However, when model parameters depend on a stochastic process, calculating the selection gradient—a key tool for predicting the evolution of phenotypic traits—becomes a mathematical challenge. While the periodic case has been resolved, a general approach for random environments remains to be developed. This article proposes a rigorous method to: \\begin{enumerate} \\item Establish the differentiability of the leading Lyapunov exponent $\\Lambda(z)$ with respect to a parameter $z$, providing an explicit integral formula for its derivative $\\Lambda'(z)$. \\item Develop a numerical algorithm to compute $\\Lambda'(z)$ by solving an extended differential equation. \\item Apply these results to the analysis of mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, identifying the selection gradient as the derivative $\\Lambda'(z)$. \\end{enumerate} \\footnote{\\today}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["M is a compact Riemannian manifold and f a C^1 diffeomorphism of M","mu is an f-invariant Borel probability measure (compactness makes the Oseledets integrability condition automatic)","the exponents and multiplicities are measurable and f-invariant, constant a.e. when mu is ergodic; the subspaces are measurable and Df-equivariant","the Oseledets splitting is measurable, generally not continuous, and the Pesin blocks are not invariant"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"smooth ergodic theory, Lyapunov exponents","id":"claim_bf769101c6fe8505c33df1958690eca784e10a921c4b8007d731b67c59e25eca","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be a C^1 diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold M and mu an f-invariant Borel probability measure. Since M is compact, log of the norm of Df and of Df^{-1} are bounded, hence integrable, so Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem applies: for mu-a.e. x there are finitely many numbers lambda_1(x) > lambda_2(x) > ... > lambda_{k(x)}(x) (the LYAPUNOV EXPONENTS at x) and a Df-invariant splitting of the tangent space

  T_x M = E_1(x) + ... + E_{k(x)}(x),   Df_x E_i(x) = E_i(f x),

such that for every nonzero v in E_i(x) the limit of (1/n) log |Df^n_x v| as n -> +-infinity exists and equals lambda_i(x). The functions x -> lambda_i(x) and the multiplicities dim E_i(x) are measurable and f-invariant, and if mu is ergodic they are constant almost everywhere; the subspaces E_i(x) are measurable and Df-equivariant, Df_x E_i(x) = E_i(fx). The splitting is in general only MEASURABLE, not continuous, and the convergence is not uniform in x.

Two structural facts that every application uses. (1) TEMPEREDNESS: any measurable positive function that is subexponential along orbits -- such as the angle between the Oseledets subspaces, or the norm of the change to Lyapunov (adapted) coordinates -- can be chosen tempered, meaning (1/n) log of its value at f^n x tends to 0; this is what lets one build Lyapunov charts in which Df is uniformly contracting on the negative-exponent bundle at the cost of a chart size that shrinks subexponentially along the orbit. (2) PESIN BLOCKS: for each l one collects the points where the Oseledets estimates hold with uniform constants depending on l; the resulting sets Lambda_l are COMPACT (after discarding a null set and restricting the subbundles continuously), increase in l, exhaust a full-measure set, and carry uniform hyperbolic-like estimates. They are NOT f-invariant -- an orbit wanders between blocks -- which is exactly why non-uniformly hyperbolic statements are local-and-measurable rather than uniform.

A point x is called (non-uniformly) hyperbolic when no exponent at x is zero; the stable bundle E^s(x) is the sum of the E_i(x) with lambda_i(x) < 0 and the unstable bundle the sum of those with lambda_i(x) > 0. Zero exponents are the obstruction: nothing in this framework says anything about directions with zero exponent.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:55.113909+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bf78f713a819fe2e5444b186c47c8b262014ec8ee77f84826b5b1d0a8d2fb190","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] (1) $\textbf{KI} \vdash \neg \neg \Diamond \top \to \Diamond \top$.
  (2) $L \nvdash \neg \neg \Diamond \top \to \Diamond \top$ for $L \in \set{ \textbf{FIK}, \textbf{IK} }$.
  \begin{proof}
    (1) Take any $\Box$-p and $\Diamond$-p model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$,
    and any $x \in W$ such that $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \neg \Diamond \top$.
    By the $\leq$-reflexivity of $x$ and the fact that no world forces $\bot$,
    the assumption implies $x \not \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \Diamond \top$.
    Hence there are $x', y' \in W$ such that $x \leq x'$, $x' \sqsubset y'$, and $y' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \top$.
    By the $\Box$-p condition, there is $y \in W$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \leq y'$.
    Since $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \top$, we have $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \top$.
    Therefore, $\textbf{KI} \vdash \neg \neg \Diamond \top \to \Diamond \top$ by completeness.

    (2) Consider the model $\mathfrak{M}_{\textsf{CD}}$ from Proposition (prop:fik-is-weaker-than-eikm of the paper) (2).
    The world $x$ has no $\sqsubset$-successor, so $x \not \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Diamond \top$.
    To see that $x \Vdash^{\text{h}} \neg \neg \Diamond \top$, take any $z \in W$ such that $x \leq z$.
    If $z = x'$, then $z \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Diamond \top$ because $x' \sqsubset y'$.
    If $z = x$, then its $\leq$-successor $x'$ forces $\Diamond \top$.
    Thus, in either case, $z \not \Vdash^{\text{h}} \neg \Diamond \top$.
    By $\mathfrak{M}_{\textsf{CD}}$ satisfying the $\Diamond$-p and FS2 conditions,
    we have $L \nvdash \neg \neg \Diamond \top \to \Diamond \top$ for $L \in \set{ \textbf{FIK}, \textbf{IK} }$ by soundness.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f in L^1_loc(R^d), Lebesgue measure","averaging sets shrink nicely to x (bounded eccentricity); unbounded eccentricity breaks the theorem"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751496+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_bf8b9a4334173b1b42ad155604b5dabb90ceb6c0b2b33e20cc69bf001127fc26","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be in L^1_loc(R^d). Then for Lebesgue-almost every x, (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y) - f(x)| dy -> 0 as r -> 0; such an x is called a Lebesgue point of f. In particular the averages of f over shrinking balls converge to f(x) for a.e. x. The result persists if balls are replaced by any family of sets U_r shrinking NICELY to x, meaning U_r is contained in B(x,r) and |U_r| >= c |B(x,r)| for a fixed c > 0 (cubes centred at x, for instance). It FAILS for families of arbitrary eccentricity: in R^2 there is an integrable f whose averages over rectangles centred at x with sides parallel to the axes and both side lengths tending to 0 fail to converge at almost every x, because the strong maximal function is not of weak type (1,1). The a.e. exceptional set genuinely depends on f and cannot be taken empty. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Chapter 3, Corollary 1.5 and Section 1.4]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.969953+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bfaf6c758aebeb9ade6830f3d3db0a0f0ff9ce1c2b2b960272aa4c5c4020aac9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (\textsf{Dominant chaos with lower-order perturbations}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix $\mathsf{S}\in\{{ \mathsf{P}},{\mathsf{R}}\}$, $r\in\N$, and
$\lambda\in(0,\infty)$.  For each $n\in\N$, let\footnote{The sum $\sum_{j=1}^0$ is understood to be empty.}

\noi
\begin{align*}
 F_n\in\cC_{r}^{\mathsf{S}}\cap L^4(\PP),
 \quad
 B_n=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}B_{n,j},
\AND
 B_{n,j}\in\cC_{j}^{\mathsf{S}}\cap L^4(\PP).
\end{align*} 

\noi
Suppose that $F_n+B_n$ satisfies the lattice condition
\eqref{cond_La} with shift $\theta_n>0$, and define
$X_n:=\theta_n+F_n+B_n$.  Put
$\eps_n:=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}\norm{B_{n,j}}_4$.
For every $n$ such that $\theta_n>0$, with
$c_{\theta_n}:=(1-e^{-\theta_n})/\theta_n$, define

\noi
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak{R}_{\theta_n}(F_n,\eps_n)
 :=
 c_{\theta_n}\bigg[ 2 \|F_n\|_4\eps_n+\eps_n^2+\frac{\eps_n}{2}
 + 14\bigl(1+ \|F_n\|_4+\eps_n\bigr)^3\eps_n  \bigg]
 +\left(1+\frac{c_{\theta_n}}2\right)\eps_n.
 
\end{align}
Then,

\noi
\begin{align} 
\begin{aligned}
 \dTV\bigl( X_n,  P_{\theta_n}\bigr)  
   & \leq
 c_{\theta_n}\bigg[  | m_2(F_n)-\theta_n|  + \frac{2r-1}{2r}\sqrt{\mathfrak{d}_{\mathsf{S}}(F_n)} \\
 &\qquad\qquad\qquad  + \frac23\sqrt{m_2(F_n)\mathfrak d_{\mathsf{S}}(F_n)}
 +b_{\mathsf{S}}\mathfrak d_{\mathsf{S}}(F_n)  \bigg]  
   +\mathfrak R_{\theta_n}(F_n,\eps_n).
\end{aligned}
\end{align}

\noi
In particular, $\mathfrak R_{\theta_n}(F_n,0)=0$.  Hence, when
$\eps_n=0$, one has $B_n=0$ and \eqref{pert_main_bdd} reduces exactly
to Corollary~\ref{cor_P_quant} if $\mathsf{S}={ \mathsf{P}}$ and to
Corollary~\ref{cor_R_quant} if $\mathsf{S}={\mathsf{R}}$.

If, in addition,
$
 \big(\theta_n,  m_2(F_n), \mathfrak{d}_{\mathsf{S}}(F_n)\big)
 \xrightarrow{n\to+\infty}(\lambda, \lambda, 0)$
and
 $\eps_n\to0$,
then
$\dTV(X_n, P_\lambda)\to0$,
the first four moments of $X_n$ converge to those of
$P_\lambda$, and $(X_n^4)_{n\geq1}$ is uniformly integrable.
In the Rademacher case, under $m_2(F_n)\to\lambda$, the condition
$\mathfrak{d}_{\mathsf{R}}(F_n)\to0$ is equivalent to
$\cR(F_n)\to0$ and $\cM(F_n)\to0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.011006+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bfb22fe034972a896b6f66482e5eb230b9f94b0a0d8cdd70a464105ac28b25c5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 23 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)$ be a word in
$\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, let
$\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_\ell)\in\{0,1\}^\ell$, and let
$\mathbf d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\in\NN^n$.  For $1\le j\le n$, put
\begin{equation}
 T_j=\{0\}\cup\{t\in[\ell]:i_t=j\},
 \qquad
 \tau_j(t)=\max\bigl(T_j\cap\{0,1,\ldots,t\}\bigr),
 \qquad
 \lambda_j=\tau_j(\ell).
\end{equation}
The vertex $v_{j,r}$, for $r\in T_j$, is the rank-$j$ state created at
time $r$; in particular, $v_{j,0}$ is the initial state.  At stage $t$ the
current rank-$j$ state is $v_{j,\tau_j(t)}$.  There is deliberately no
separate vertex for a passive pullback at a time not belonging to $T_j$.

The rooted directed multigraph
$\mathfrak C(\mathbf i,\epsilon,\mathbf d)$ has vertex set
\[
 \{0\}\sqcup\{v_{j,r}:1\le j\le n,\ r\in T_j\}.
\]
For every $t$ with $\epsilon_t=1$, it has one ordinary edge
\begin{equation}
 e_t:v_{i_t,t}\longrightarrow
 v_{i_t+1,\tau_{i_t+1}(t-1)}.
\end{equation}
For every $j$ it has $d_j$ root edges
\begin{equation}
 e_{j,a}:0\longrightarrow v_{j,\lambda_j}
 \qquad(1\le a\le d_j).
\end{equation}
Degrees are counted with edge multiplicity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.580170+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bfd4918271d61f2b20d367287acc067c968a4bffa4cff71136b7b852b1135c20","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 44 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R$ with finite second moment,
	let $c>-1$, and let $\zeta\in\R$.  Define
	$$
	m_\mu(\omega):=\int(x-\omega)_+\,d\mu(x),
	\qquad

		+c\left(\int f\,d\mu\right)^2}
	=
	s_\mu(\omega)+c\,m_\mu(\omega)^2.
	$$

	positive multiple of $f(x)=(x-\omega)_+$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:07:48.551427+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bfd6ea94967816b09342b71cb9d9f8638fb720adab7c3deb916c0b1890d5b6b0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 8 (Fourier transforms of radial homogeneous distributions) of arXiv:2609.01403, '2609.01403'] Under the normalization \eqref{eq:fourier-normalization}, the following
statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}

\item For \(0<\alpha<n\),
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal F^{-1}(|\xi|^{-\alpha})(x)
    =
    \kappa_{n,\alpha}|x|^{\alpha-n}.
    
\end{equation}
The family \(|\xi|^{-\alpha}\), initially defined as a tempered
distribution for \(\Re\alpha<n\), admits a meromorphic continuation
to \(\alpha\in\mathbb C\), with possible poles at
$\alpha=n,n+2,n+4,\cdots$.
The identity \eqref{eq:riesz-kernel-formula} extends accordingly by
meromorphic continuation. Away from the origin, this continuation is
represented by
$\kappa_{n,\alpha}|x|^{\alpha-n}$.
In particular, if \(\alpha=-2k\), \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), then
\[
    \mathcal F^{-1}(|\xi|^{-\alpha})
    =
    (-\Delta)^k\delta_0.
\]

\item Define
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
    \left\langle\operatorname{Fp}|\xi|^{-n},\varphi\right\rangle
    &=
    \int_{|\xi|<1}
    \frac{\varphi(\xi)-\varphi(0)}{|\xi|^n}\,\mathrm{d}\xi\\
    &\quad+
    \int_{|\xi|>1}
    \frac{\varphi(\xi)}{|\xi|^n}\,\mathrm{d}\xi,
    \qquad
    \varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
Then
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal F^{-1}
    \bigl(\operatorname{Fp}|\xi|^{-n}\bigr)
    =
    c_n\log\frac1{|x|}
    +
    c_n\left(
        \log2+\frac12\psi\!\left(\frac n2\right)
        -\frac{\gamma}{2}
    \right)
    \quad\text{in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n),
    
\end{equation}
where
\[
    c_n
    =
    \frac{2^{1-n}}{\pi^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)},
\]
\(\gamma\) is Euler's constant, and
\(\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma\).

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.817132+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_bfe34b4620b759b26ab1274ad07ca3b34dc6edf94c99aebfc801f306734a9364","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:shift-stable-chart of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix an integer $d\geq1$ and $0<\gamma<1$.  A \emph{shift-stable $d$-chart
of depth $\gamma h$} is a family
$(B_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta_h}$, indexed by all sufficiently large integers
$h$ with $\Theta_h\ne\varnothing$, of primitive
$(d+1)$-subsets of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ containing zero for which there are
fixed integers $s\geq1$ and $c_1,\ldots,c_s$, and integer residuals
$x_\nu(\theta,h)$, such that, uniformly for $\theta\in\Theta_h$ and
$J\in\mathbb Z$ with $0\leq J\leq\gamma h$,
\begin{equation}
 |(h-J)B_\theta|
 =\sum_{\nu=1}^{s}c_\nu
  \binom{x_\nu(\theta,h)-J+d}{d},
 \qquad x_\nu(\theta,h)-J\geq0.
\end{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.498381+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0026b7000ee4cc3be8d71c6dfe6267809a0564af1a38fde5f0375e3ca531374","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm conformal invariance of Coulomb gas integral of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let $\boldsymbol{\sigma} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sigma_i \cdot z_i + \sum_{j=1}^{m} \tau_j \cdot \xi_j$ be a divisor on the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$, where each screening charge $\tau_j \in \{-2a,\, 2(a + b)\}$ is chosen so that its conformal dimension satisfies $\lambda_b(\tau_j) = 1$. Let $h: \hat{\mathbb{C}} \to \hat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a Möbius transformation, and define
\[
\zeta_j := h(\xi_j), \quad h(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) := \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sigma_i \cdot h(z_i) + \sum_{j=1}^{m} \tau_j \cdot \zeta_j.
\]

Then the Coulomb gas integral transforms covariantly under $h$ as
\begin{equation} 
\left( \prod_{i=1}^{n} h'(z_i)^{\lambda_b(\sigma_i)} \right) 
\oint_{h(\Gamma)} C_{(b)}[h(\boldsymbol{\sigma})] \, d\zeta_1 \cdots d\zeta_m
=
\oint_{\Gamma} C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] \, d\xi_1 \cdots d\xi_m,
\end{equation}
where $h(\Gamma)$ denotes the image of the integration contour $\Gamma$ under $h$.

Each differential $d\zeta_j$ transforms as $d\zeta_j = h'(\xi_j) \, d\xi_j$, and since $\lambda_b(\tau_j) = 1$, the integrand $C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]\, d\xi_1 \cdots d\xi_m$ is invariant under pullback by $h$, up to the multiplicative factor $\prod_{i} h'(z_i)^{\lambda_b(\sigma_i)}$ determined by the insertion points.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.341689+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c016333a008f9bf9b3d648cbabb3ddba14d6964be411199b4fc6aa4454938bc6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 15 (Examples: pointwise macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]

    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c

    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with
    degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\). Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta

    \]

    one has
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:09:15.289062+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c03dbe70b0fdc63f1f8859b6bc6a0bbe6eb2edeeb75f11a10de8dd548965a0b4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem sym of arXiv:2411.04802, 'Dynkin ghost games with asymmetry and consolation'] Assume that $g_1=g_2=:g$, $h_1=h_2=:h$ and that (equation inclusion of the paper) holds.
Also assume that $p_1\leq p_2$.
Define a boundary 
\[b(x):=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}
0 & \mbox{if }V^g(x)=g(x)\\
\frac{V^g(x)-g(x)}{V^g(x)-V^h(x)} & \mbox{if }V^h(x)\leq g(x)<V^g(x)\\
1 & \mbox{if }g(x)<V^h(x),\end{array}\right.\]
  and let 
   \[\Gamma^2_t:=\frac{p_1-p_1\wedge \inf_{0\leq s\leq t} b(X_s)}{p_1(1-p_1\wedge \inf_{0\leq s\leq t} b(X_s))}\]
  and 
  \[\Gamma^1_t:=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}
  \frac{p_1(1-b(x)\wedge p_1)}{p_2(1-p_1)}(\Gamma^2_t-\Gamma^2_0) & t<\tau_g\\
  1 & t\geq \tau_g.\end{array}\right.\]
  Then $(\Gamma^1,\Gamma^2)$ is a Nash equilibrium, with corresponding equilibrium values
  \begin{equation}

u_1(x,p_1):=(1-p_1)V^g(x)+p_1V^h(x)
\end{equation}
  and
  \[u_2(x,p_1):=\max\left\{(1-p_1)V^g(x)+p_1V^h(x), g(x)\right\}.\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.044585+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c04fe28ffea6aa70d4e8d0115a2753341f4ce4531102aeafc214a3de14483613","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 4 (restate=continuousBoundedJumps,name=) of arXiv:2608.15874, '2608.15874'] Let $(\cF_t)_{t\geq0}$ be a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, let $\cZ$ be a measurable space, and let $\mu$ be an integer-valued random measure on $\Rp\times\cZ$ with predictable compensator $\nu$. Let $H=(H_t(z))_{t\geq0,\,z\in\cZ}$ be predictable and $\cH$-valued, with $\norm{H_t(z)}\leq1$, and suppose that, for every $T<\infty$,
\[
  \int_{(0,T]\times\cZ}\norm{H_t(z)}^2\,\nu(\dif t,\dif z)<\infty \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]
Define
\[
  M_t=\int_{(0,t]\times\cZ}H_s(z)\,(\mu-\nu)(\dif s,\dif z), \qquad V_t=\int_{(0,t]\times\cZ}H_s(z)\otimes H_s(z)\,\nu(\dif s,\dif z).
\]
Then $M$ is a purely discontinuous local martingale with $\norm{\Delta M_t}\leq1$ for every $t\geq0$, and $V$ is its operator-valued predictable quadratic variation. For every $\rho>0$, $(U_\rho^h(M_t,V_t))_{t\geq0}$ is a nonnegative supermartingale with initial value one. Consequently, for every $y\geq0$,
\[
  \P[\bigg]{\exists t\geq0:\rho h\roundb[\bigg]{\frac{\norm{(V_t+\rho I)^{-1/2}M_t}}{\sqrt\rho}}>y+\ell_\rho(V_t)}\leq e^{-y}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

The loss is (1/(2n)) sum_i (f(x_i)-y_i)^2, with |y_i|<=Y.
Use m=2N neurons, f(x)=m^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j.x).
For each independent W_l~N(0,I_d), initialize one pair at (nu,W_l),
(-nu,W_l); update every parameter by ordinary simultaneous GD of step gamma,
with derivative 1{w.x>0}. The pairing is only at initialization, not enforced.
Let H be the deterministic full initial kernel from C014 Section2:
H(x,z)=E[ReLU(W.x)ReLU(W.z)+nu^2 1{W.x>0,W.z>0}x.z].
Let f^H_k be zero-start kernel GD with this H, the same sample and labels.
Then, as N tends to infinity,

 max_{k<=T} ||f_k-f^H_k||_{L2(P)} -> 0 in probability.       (1)

The event bounds proving this hold uniformly for every y in [-Y,Y]^n.
No positive training eigenvalue or nonzero gate margin is assumed. T is
fixed before this width limit; constants below can grow rapidly with T.

## 2. Width-independent finite-horizon bounds
Write u_j=1+||w_j(0)||. The empirical mean S_m=m^(-1)sum u_j^2 is a pair
average and tends almost surely to E(1+||W||)^2. Fix S above that expectation
and work on S_m<=S, an event eventually true almost surely.
Define H_0=D_0=0, R_0=Y. Given H_k,D_k,R_k, set
 A_k=1+H_k, B_k=1+D_k, c_k=gamma M R_k,
 H_{k+1}=H_k+c_k B_k, D_{k+1}=D_k+c_k A_k,
 R_{k+1}=R_k+M c_k S[B_k(B_k+c_k A_k)+A_k^2].
Induction gives, uniformly over the label cube,
 |a_j(k)-a_j(0)|<=H_k u_j/sqrt(m),
 ||w_j(k)-w_j(0)||<=D_k u_j/sqrt(m),
 |a_j(k)|<=A_k u_j, ||w_j(k)||<=B_k u_j,
 ||r_k||/sqrt(n)<=R_k, where r_i=f_k(x_i)-y_i.
Indeed Cauchy-Schwarz in the exact parameter updates gives
 |Delta a_j|<=c_k B_k u_j/sqrt(m),
 ||Delta w_j||<=c_k A_k u_j/sqrt(m).
ReLU is 1-Lipschitz and homogeneous, so at every ||x||<=M,
 |Delta f_k(x)|<=||x|| c_k S[B_k(B_k+c_k A_k)+A_k^2].
This proves the induction and a finite uniform output bound through T.
Let H,D,A,B,c denote maxima of these constants through the required steps.

## 3. Population gate bands shrink in L2, not just on the sample
Put L_m(x)=m^(-1)sum_j u_j^2 1{|w_j(0).x|<=D u_j||x||/sqrt(m)}.
For each training x_i, L_m(x_i)->0 almost surely. Also

 ||L_m||_{L2(P)} -> 0 almost surely.                         (2)

Proof: for fixed q>0, the pair-averaged integrable function
 Z_q(W)=(1+||W||)^2 P_x{|W.x|<=q(1+||W||)||x||}
has its empirical average tending to E Z_q by the ordinary scalar SLLN.
For m large with D/sqrt(m)<=q, integral L_m dP is bounded by that average.
For every fixed nonzero x, Gaussian W.x has no atom at zero; Fubini and
dominated convergence imply E Z_q->0 as q decreases to zero. Apply SLLN
simultaneously on countably many q=1,1/2,1/3,..., then let q decrease.
Thus integral L_m->0 almost surely. Since 0<=L_m<=S_m, its squared L2 norm
is at most S_m integral L_m. The finite training-point assertion follows
by the same fixed-q argument without integration over P.
This is uniform over trajectories obeying Section2; no independence between
trained gates and initialization is asserted or needed.

## 4. Both train and cross kernels remain close
Let H^m_k be the empirical full tangent kernel at step k. Product expansion
and the movement bounds give, for every training point x_i,

 |H^m_k(x,x_i)-H^m_0(x,x_i)|
 <= ||x||||x_i|| [C S/sqrt(m)+nu^2(L_m(x)+L_m(x_i))],       (3)

where C=D(B+1)+H(A+1) is finite. The RF-product part is bounded by
D(B+1)u_j^2/sqrt(m). The readout-square change is bounded by
H(A+1)u_j^2/sqrt(m). A changed gate at x forces the initial weight into
the band defining L_m(x); likewise at x_i. These inequalities remain valid
when a trained preactivation equals zero, using the stated derivative.
Equations (2),(3) imply uniform-in-k convergence of the training normalized
Gram matrices and of the population cross rows, relative to their INITIAL
empirical kernels. In particular define K^m_k=(H^m_k(x_i,x_l)/n),
b^m_k(x)=(H^m_k(x,x_i)/sqrt(n))_i. Their respective operator and L2(row)
differences from step0 tend to zero; the latter is bounded by
M^2[C S/sqrt(m)+nu^2(||L_m||_2+max_i L_m(x_i))].

At initialization, each independent pair contributes the same feature
kernel F_W(x,z)=ReLU(W.x)ReLU(W.z)+nu^2 1{W.x>0,W.z>0}x.z.
It satisfies |F_W(x,z)|<=M^2(||W||^2+1). Its squared envelope is integrable.
Thus the empirical initial training kernel tends to K=(H(x_i,x_l)/n).
For the population cross row b(x)=(H(x,x_i)/sqrt(n))_i, independence of pairs
and Fubini give E||b^m_0-b||_2^2<=M^4 E(||W||^2+1)^2/N.
Hence this difference tends to zero in probability too. This explicitly
controls the missing test-to-training kernel; it is not inferred from K.

## 5. Discrete-step gate remainder off the sample
The exact prediction update is
 f_{k+1}(x)=f_k(x)-gamma b^m_k(x).v_k+Z_k(x), v_k=r_k/sqrt(n),
where, writing h=ReLU(w.x), h'=ReLU((w+Delta w).x),
 Z_k(x)=m^(-1/2)sum_j[Delta a_j(h'-h)
             +a_j(h'-h-1{w.x>0}Delta w_j.x)].
If the second summand is nonzero, the segment from w to w+Delta w crosses
its gate at x. Because both endpoints are within the Section2 cumulative
radius of w(0), the initial preactivation lies in the D-band above.
The Lipschitz inequality therefore gives

 |Z_k(x)|<=||x||[c^2 A B S/sqrt(m)+c A^2 L_m(x)].           (4)

It follows that max_{k<T}||Z_k||_{L2(P)}->0 and max_{k<T,i}|Z_k(x_i)|->0.
No approximation replaces discrete GD by flow.

## 6. Close the training and population prediction recurrences
Let v^H_{k+1}=(I-gamma K)v^H_k, v^H_0=-y/sqrt(n).
The true normalized residual update is
 v_{k+1}=(I-gamma K^m_k)v_k+z_k,
where ||z_k||<=max_i |Z_k(x_i)|. Sections2,4,5 imply by finite induction
max_{k<=T}||v_k-v^H_k||->0 in probability, uniformly over bounded labels.
For example each error is bounded by ||I-gamma K|| times the previous
error plus gamma ||K^m_k-K|| R_k+||z_k||. The multiplier is finite; neither
a contraction nor a spectral gap is required at this finite horizon.
Both output initializations are exactly zero. Sum the prediction updates:
 f_k-f^H_k=-gamma sum_{j<k}[(b^m_j-b).v_j+b.(v_j-v^H_j)]
                         +sum_{j<k}Z_j.
The population L2 norm is bounded by the sum of cross-kernel errors times
R_j, deterministic ||b||_2 times training residual errors, and remainder
norms. Every term tends to zero by the preceding sections, proving (1).
The same controlling random bounds work for all bounded label vectors.
For any bounded teacher, clean risks averaged over the bounded independent
label noises consequently converge uniformly through T in probability,
by Cauchy-Schwarz and the finite uniform output bound from Section2.


Here zero-start kernel GD means f^H_{k+1}(x)=f^H_k(x)-(gamma/n)sum_i H(x,x_i)(f^H_k(x_i)-y_i), with f^H_0=0.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:32:34.746300+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c059a854a6d0f3983951de7ed37203b1b4c502b645c83e7873b05ceef5fa6a29","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma mart_bound_dim_free of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{Y}_i$, $\mathbf{V}_i$ and $\mathbf{Z}_k$ be as in Proposition~(prop:mart_bound of the paper), i.e., $(\mathbf{Y}_i)_{i=1}^n \subset \mathbb{H}(d)$ is a matrix-valued stochastic process adapted to filtration $(\mathscr{F}_i)_{i=1}^n$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:12:19.474167+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c075c73823754600d1d2ed37cce52c5b8c12db74ea7ef124c59660be6b85772a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Let
  $Z \sim \mathcal{F}(\alpha)$ for some $\alpha > 0$,
  and let 
  $W$ be a random variable whose distribution function $F_W$
  is absolutely continuous on $[K, +\infty)$ for some $K>0$, with 
  density function~$f_W$.
\begin{enumerate}[i)] 
\item Kolmogorov bound. For any $\alpha >0$, we have
\begin{align*}
      \nonumber 
\mathrm{d}_{K} (W, \mathcal{F}(\alpha) ) \leq (\alpha + 1)F_{W}(K) + \alpha\int_{K}^\infty  F_{W}(r)\bigg\vert\frac{f_{W}(r)}{F_{W}(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r.\numberthis
\end{align*}
\item Wasserstein bound.
  Let $\alpha > 1$ and
  $p \in (1,\alpha)$ such that $\esp[\vert W \vert^{p}] < \infty$.
  We have
  \begin{align*}
      \nonumber 
      \mathrm{d}_{W} (W, \mathcal{F}(\alpha) ) \leq \esp [\vert W \vert^{p} ]^{{1}/{p}}F_{W}(K)^{{1}/{q}} & + \Big(
      \Gamma\Big(1 - \frac{1}{\alpha}\Big) + \frac{\alpha^{2}}{\alpha - 1}\Big)
      F_{W}(K)\\
		&+ \alpha\int_{K}^\infty  rF_{W}(r)\bigg\vert\frac{f_{W}(r)}{F_{W}(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r,\numberthis
\end{align*}
  where $q = p/(p-1)$ denotes the conjugate of $p$. 
\item Moment bound.
  Let $\alpha > 0$ and
  $b \in (0, \alpha)$,
  assume that $W$ is a.s. nonnegative and that there exists $p \in (1, \alpha / b)$ such that $\esp[W^{pb}] < \infty$, with $q = p/(p-1)$. Then, we have  
  \begin{align*}
      \nonumber 
\vert \esp [W^{b} ] - \esp [Z^{b}]\vert \leq \esp [ W^{pb}]^{{1}/{p}}F_{W}(K)^{{1}/{q}} & + \Big( \Gamma\Big(1 - \frac{b}{\alpha}\Big) + \frac{\alpha^{2}}{\alpha - b}\Big) F_{W}(K)\\
		&+ \alpha\int_{K}^\infty  r^{b}F_{W}(r)\bigg\vert\frac{f_{W}(r)}{F_{W}(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r.\numberthis
\end{align*}

\item Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $b \in (0, \alpha)$.
  Suppose that there exists $p \in (1, \alpha / b)$ such that $\esp[\vert W \vert^{p}]< \infty$, with $q = p/(p-1)$. Then, we have 
  \begin{align*}
      \nonumber 
      \mathrm{d}_{W_b} (W, \mathcal{F}(\alpha) )
      \leq \esp [ W^{pb}]^{{1}/{p}}F_{W}(K)^{{1}/{q}}
      &
      + \Big(
      \Gamma\Big(1 - \frac{b}{\alpha}\Big) + \frac{2\alpha^{2}}{\alpha - b}\Big)
       F_{W}(K)\\
		&+ \alpha\int_{K}^\infty  r^{b}F_{W}(r)\bigg\vert\frac{f_{W}(r)}{F_{W}(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r.\numberthis
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:35:05.849903+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c084aed6ade36083229279ae95d610a5a32a48a0f0760227c4d7f258e4b35c81","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:tensor of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be Markov kernels on finite state spaces $S_1, S_2$ with
stationary distributions $\pi_1, \pi_2$ respectively. Consider the product

\[

  = \frac{\log(1/\pi_1(x_1))\cdot r_1(x_1)

\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:48:43.535927+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c08519b7510b453012af49b9ceb882e72cdbf11f654155b5bfbafff37f5e28ae","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (The process $\mathrm{CHL}_N$) of arXiv:2608.06925, 'Sharp asymptotics for the tree-completion time in\\ cylindrical Hastings--Levitov$(0)$'] Let $P$ be a Poisson point process of intensity $1$ on $\R_+\times\T_N$. For every $t>0$,
the set $P\cap([0,t]\times\T_N)$ is almost surely finite; enumerate its points as
$(t_1,x_1),\dots,(t_n,x_n)$, where $0<t_1<\cdots<t_n\le t$. The \emph{cylindrical
Hastings--Levitov process with parameter $0$}, denoted by $\mathrm{CHL}_N$, is represented by the
aggregate map
\[
  \mathcal C^{N,\lambda}_t=S^{N,\lambda}_{x_1}\circ S^{N,\lambda}_{x_2}\circ\cdots\circ S^{N,\lambda}_{x_n}.
\]

{"assumptions":["Real finite linear-regression data, 1<=rank(X)<input dimension; h>=min(output,input)","Continuous Euclidean gradient flow and the stated strictly positive initial deficiency margin","Source result is about excess loss after removing the fixed data-null residual"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:56:41.472730+00:00","domain":"LoRA rank-one convergence and deficiency margins","id":"claim_c09d5ef3743876862975e7f9016562cc9fb4fe833a244df4a51ad4de89643d67","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Min-Tarmoun-Vidal-Mallada sufficient-deficiency-margin method for linear-network gradient flow: let X be a real N-by-n design of rank q with 1<=q<n, Y an N-by-m response matrix and h>=min(m,n) the hidden width. Write the design SVD as X=W Sigma_x^(1/2) Phi1^T, where W and Phi1 have orthonormal columns and Sigma_x is positive definite q-by-q. For factors U n-by-h,V m-by-h put U1=Phi1^T U, S=W^T Y, E=S-Sigma_x^(1/2)U1V^T. Under continuous Euclidean gradient flow of ||Y-XUV^T||F^2/2, the positive initial deficiency margin sigma_min(S)-||E(0)||F>0 suffices for exponential convergence of the excess loss ||E(t)||F^2/2 to zero; sigma_min means the smallest of the min(q,m) singular values. The positive margin persists along the flow because loss decreases, and Weyl's inequality keeps the fitted product full rank min(q,m). Factor bounds or the source's sharper imbalance formula convert this margin into gradient domination. This is Corollary 5 of arXiv:2105.06351, printed p.10, with Theorem 3 and equation (21), p.9. It does not assert that a zero-product initialization already has positive margin. At rank one, a separate strict first-step decrease can create that margin; applying the idea to discrete GD still requires valid descent and boundedness estimates.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Source revision2301.13833v2; formal Theorem6 and AppendixA equations10-20.","The source construction includes layer freezes, a readout reset and an affine bias update.","No ordinary-SGD interpretation or theorem correction has independent review."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:23:05.889389+00:00","domain":"learning theory","id":"claim_c0a1a1bf448f6029c7e47aca5eb86d056758f31e1229ec261b4d450c71475f85","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Source-scope notice; theorem interpretation pending independent review. Choose an integer N>=(d+1)(d-k+1) log((d+1)(d-k+1)/delta), a real zeta satisfying0<zeta<=epsilon*mu^k/[24(d+1)^2(d-k+1)^2*N], and an integer batch size B>=log((N*d+N)/delta)/(8*zeta^2*N^2). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:44.958945+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0a3e4f934b5355f81e5996a6e8165e8b9c741a3f81590db521a5996bdbd66d9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Dyadic first-Borel--Cantelli device) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Let $\mathcal I\subset\Dyd^3$ be countable.  Let $X_i\ge0$ be random variables and $A_i>0$ deterministic weights.  Suppose that for every finite $p\ge2$,
\[
 \norm{X_i}_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_pA_i,
 \qquad i\in\mathcal I.
\]
Let $L_i\ge1$ be deterministic losses such that $\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}L_i^{-p}<\infty$ for some $p$.  Then there is a full-probability event $\Omega_*$ and a finite random variable $C_*(\omega)$ such that
\[
 X_i(\omega)\le C_*(\omega)L_iA_i,

 \quad \omega\in\Omega_*.
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.823508+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0a6f28c660c1e769b888b2c1bd6c56a80bcea8d52b84044883a319733a1ef80","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:critical-window-saturation of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $k\geq3$.  For each $h\geq2$, put
\[
 H_{h,k}=(k-1)h^{k-2},\qquad
 \mathcal M_{h,k}
 =\{A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,H_{h,k}\}:0\in A,\ |A|=k\}.
\]
The maps from $\mathcal M_{h,k}$ onto the realized weak types and onto the
realized ordered $h$-addition-table types are surjective.  Moreover, as
$h\to\infty$,
\[
 |\mathcal M_{h,k}|=\binom{H_{h,k}}{k-1}
 =\Theta_k\!\left(h^{(k-1)(k-2)}\right),
\]
and both target sets have the same order of magnitude.  Consequently, the
average fibre of either type map has order $\Theta_k(1)$, and choosing one
representative from each fibre gives a positive-proportion subfamily on which
the map is injective.  For either type map, such a full-order subfamily may
be chosen entirely among representatives of maximal-rank weak types, and
hence inside the exact core $[0,h^{k-2}]$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:26:52.674048+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0ad4a9f7238ea81e6409d254b3a8481629fee445014d35ee935e549f1d5e584","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 (Large deviation principle) of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Let \( I \) be a good rate function on \( \mathfrak{U} \). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.579082+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0b37a8bb95823ced73a754cb8b1aa7c43f8c0510de201c01fef9831d97c831d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Cascade system) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] For $v\in V(T)$ and a state $s^{(v)}_t\in\R$,

Let $P_1, P_2, \ldots$ be an arbitrary (deterministic) sequence in $\mathscr{C}(d)$. For each $N$, define
\[
P^{(N)} := \diag(P_1, \ldots, P_N) \in \bR^{Nd \times Nd}
\]
and, using the notation in Lemma \ref{lem:coupling.Gaussian}, define
\[
\pi^{(N)} := \pi^{P^{(N)}},
\]
which is a Gaussian bicausal coupling of $\bX^{(N)}$ and $\bY^{(N)}$. Consider the random variable
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.953522+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0f6569fe40b75e82233252e0aa32767f8b51829c2c878837afe78f36ffb1f4e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 6 (Gaussian-noise bulk and full-trace LSS) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let $f$ satisfy \eqref{eq:Gaussian-f-assumptions-main}, let $\lambda\ge0$ be
fixed, and suppose that the deterministic spike obeys
\begin{equation}
 \norm{x}_2=1,
 \qquad
 \norm{x}_\infty=o(N^{-1/4}),
 \qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=O(N^{o(1)}).
\end{equation}
Let $\Gamma$ satisfy (G1)--(G4) with $\theta_{f,\nu}$ replaced by $\theta_f$,
and let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_k$ be analytic on a neighborhood of
$\overline{D_\Gamma}$ and real-valued on its intersection with $\mathbb R$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \left(
 \mathcal L_{M_{N,\gamma}^f}^{\Gamma}(\varphi_\ell)
 -N\int_{-2}^2\varphi_\ell(t)\rho_{\scal}(t)\,\dd t

 \right)_{\ell=1}^k

 (G_{\varphi_\ell})_{\ell=1}^k,

\begin{equation}

 =\mathcal V_{\kappa_f}^{\Gamma}(\varphi,\psi).

=\Tr\varphi(M_{N,\gamma}^f)$ with probability tending to one, so

 (G_{\varphi_\ell})_{\ell=1}^k,

with the covariance \eqref{eq:Gaussian-covariance-main}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.351460+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c0fc8f01bf0470a4e19c40cfcbd48f63ad3e9919d3e37b9d46aff505e0204a9c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 187 (approximate quadratic variation processes) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$, define $\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$ to be the piecewise linear process with increments
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)
	\equiv
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d,B)
	\equiv
	\frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\sigma}(q_d,a)\Big)
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\tau}(q_d,a)\Big)\,.
	\eeq
For the Ising case, we also define
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\Ising}(q_d)
	\equiv \frac{1}{|B||B^{\Ising}|}
	\sum_{a\in B,i\in B^{\Ising}}
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\sigma}(q_d,a)\Big)
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_d,i)\Big)

	\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)
	\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)\Big)
	\eeq
for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$; 
as well as
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\Ising}(q_d)
	\equiv
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\Ising}(q_d,B^\Ising)
	\equiv 
	\frac{1}{|B^{\Ising}|}
	\sum_{i\in B^{\Ising}}
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_d,i)\Big)^2\,.
	\eeq
Denote also $E^{\sigma,\tau}\equiv Q^{\sigma,\tau}-\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$. We define likewise $\Delta\tilde{Q}^\frozen$ using increments of $X^\frozen$. Then, 
analogously to \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus},
for all $\sigma , \tau \in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$ we have for $B^\frozen \cap [M] = B \neq \emptyset$
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\frozen,\sigma,\tau}(q_d,B^\frozen)
	=\frac{|B|}{|B^\frozen|}
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d,B)

A similar relation holds between $\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\Ising}$ and $\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\frozen,\sigma,\Ising}$, and likewise between

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:49:17.487720+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c10225c2ffe8a02997a0757643ca7917ee9b0d4a83b3e4fa60b2c96241747b96","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (XY model) of arXiv:2605.28473, 'The BKT transition and surface tension differentiability'] Consider a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ with edge weights
    $J=(J_{uv})_{uv\in E}\subset[0,\infty)$.
    Let $\Omega=\S^V$, where $\S\subset\C$ denotes the unit circle, and endow
    $\Omega$ with the product Haar probability measure $\diff\sigma$.
    The \emph{XY model} on $G$ with \emph{coupling constants} $J$ is the Gibbs measure
    $\langle\blank\rangle_{G,J}$ on $\Omega$ defined by the formula
    \begin{equation}
        
        \langle X\rangle_{G,J}:=\frac1{Z_{G,J}}\int_\Omega X(\sigma)
        e^{\frac12\sum_{uv\in\vec E}J_{uv}\sigma_u\bar\sigma_v} \diff\sigma,
    \end{equation}
    where $\vec E$ is the set of directed edges, and $Z_{G,J}\in(0,\infty)$ is the
    \emph{partition function}.
    Often $J$ is taken to be a constant $\beta\in[0,\infty)$, in which case we write
    $\langle\blank\rangle_{G,\beta}$.
    The parameter $\beta$ is called the \emph{inverse temperature}.

    We are interested in the \emph{mass} (the inverse of the \emph{correlation length})
    of the XY model in 2D.
    Write $\Lambda_n$ for the nearest-neighbour graph on $[-n,n]^2\cap\Z^2$.
    Then the \emph{mass} $\frakm_\XY(\beta)$ is defined via
    \begin{equation}
        
        \frakm_\XY(\beta):=\lim_{k\to\infty}-\frac1k\log\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle\sigma_0\bar\sigma_{k
        e_1}\rangle_{\Lambda_n,\beta}\in[0,\infty].
    \end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the per-sample relative L2 loss as used by the EMIT/OCO-2 stacking pools; independent errors across rows","the multiplicative-versus-additive question is empirical and is measured by ens_rmt_elast.py (P21 of the RMT program)"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T11:47:28.061008+00:00","domain":"ensemble learning / weighted regression","id":"claim_c109e1a78941f0a6a45f877d2453aa489942de8d28e336dd0f0d21122d68470e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Fitting a stack (or any linear predictor) under the per-sample relative L2 loss, mean over rows of ||y_i - yhat_i||^2 / ||y_i||^2, is weighted least squares with case weights s_i = 1 / ||y_i||^2. By the two-regimes corollary those are Aitken's variance-stabilising weights exactly when the error scale is proportional to the target norm (multiplicative error, elasticity of log ||e_i|| on log ||y_i|| equal to one); then the relative-metric fit is the efficient one and its optimism is 2m/n relative to its own noise level, regardless of how concentrated 1/||y_i||^2 is. If the error carries an additive floor, the rows with the smallest targets - exactly the rows the relative weights concentrate on - have the largest floor relative to their target, the concentration re-enters, and Kish's n_eff of the relative weights measures how far the fit is from balanced. The discriminating measurement is the elasticity of the out-of-fold residual norm to the target norm and the nonnegative fit ||e_i||^2 = a + b ||y_i||^2 (the floor share a / (a + b median ||y||^2)) on the calibration rows; on a pool whose targets vary by orders of magnitude (the EMIT radiance outputs) the question is live, on one whose targets are homogeneous (the OCO-2 retrievals, n_eff within a few percent of n) the two metrics coincide and it is moot.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["finite simple graphs (loops make P identically 0; parallel edges do not change P)","k a nonnegative integer in the counting definition; the polynomial identity then holds for all k"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.479653+00:00","domain":"graph theory","id":"claim_c11359eb703fe597fd324079d34608d788354417c8b886cc4a0e84bab112bea7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a finite graph G and a positive integer k let P(G, k) be the number of proper colourings of the vertices of G with k colours (adjacent vertices receive different colours).
