{"assumptions":["(X, mu) is a measure space","the sets are measurable"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T07:49:53.248663+00:00","domain":"the symmetric-difference (Frechet-Nikodym) distance on measurable sets","id":"claim_d0da117483c01810993ee9f9b28c742923b9170388b7a408f5aabea94e9531b6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a measure space (X, mu) and measurable sets A, B, d_mu(A, B) = mu(A symmetric difference B), possibly infinite. For an increasing sequence E_1 in E_2 in ... with increments D_k = E_{k+1} minus E_k and union E, d_mu(E_m, E_n) = sum_{k=m}^{n-1} mu(D_k) for m <= n and d_mu(E_m, E) = sum_{k >= m} mu(D_k). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:59:53.386594+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d0e74f929ce062ec42ed39aee3972e3d5cfb03147c9f5ca658e0a0b4d6c6e977","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:complexZero of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\beta>0$ be noninteger and let $      \beta=n_\beta+\theta_\beta$ with $       n_\beta=\lfloor\beta\rfloor$.

nonreal zeros, counted with multiplicity. They occur in conjugate pairs.

Suppose that $n_\beta$ is odd. Let $q_\beta$ be the number of zeros
of $f_\beta$ in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and,
for $0\leq k\leq n_\beta+1$, let $M_k(\beta)$ be the total
multiplicity of the real zeros of $f_\beta$ in $\mathcal I_k$. Then
each $M_k(\beta)$ is odd and
\begin{equation}
        2q_\beta
        +
        \sum_{k=0}^{n_\beta+1}
        \left[M_k(\beta)-1\right]
        =
        n_\beta+1.
\end{equation}
In particular, $f_\beta$ has at most $n_\beta+1$ nonreal zeros,
counted with multiplicity.

Consequently, for every noninteger $\beta>0$, only finitely many zeros
of $f_\beta$ are nonreal or multiple. All the remaining zeros are real
and simple.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Compatible factor dimensions and differentiable convex loss C","Conditional escape application additionally requires the full hypotheses of Theorem G.2"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:59:19.888440+00:00","domain":"optimization; deep linear networks","id":"claim_d123bf590725fc5f7969f141b98ab52076f76946f3e08837af58a3d7ec9607e4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For B in R^(m x w), A in R^(w x n), and differentiable convex loss C on m-by-n matrices, set U=[B;A^T], Z=UU^T and F(Z)=C(Z12)+C(Z21^T) on (m+n)-square matrices. Then F(UU^T)/2=C(BA). At symmetric Z, with G=grad C(Z12), grad F(Z)=[[0,G],[G^T,0]]. Section 3 of arXiv:2012.09839, PDF p.3 explicitly gives the square asymmetric-to-symmetric reduction; these formulas spell out arbitrary rectangular block sizes and the exact gradient-flow normalization. Applying Theorem G.2 requires all its hypotheses; for quadratic regression its all-real-time convention requires a local complete extension, since quadratic flow need not be backward complete. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.351868+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d12426fdfbbc66523751b41528059a535ae1c7d914220fbadbddbab890b7560a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Cor 190 (quenched first moment bounds on $Q^\sigma$ and $Q^{\sigma,\frozen}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $Q$ as in Definition~\ref{d:Q}, we have

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:37:15.397581+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d1649d346df95cd64f9a91f52e88a391a9b033628f405d75164cb27f6da83b54","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 11 (Jacobi case: explicit Bernoulli variable) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Let $Z=(Z_t)_{t\ge0}$ be the Jacobi martingale solving

\[

Let    $(x_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a sequence in ${\boldsymbol{X}}$ and  $(c_n)_{n\geq 0}$  a sequence of positive real numbers such that
\[
\sum_{n\geq 1}c_n\Vert x_n\Vert<\infty. 
\]
Denote by ${\boldsymbol{Y}}$ the closure of the span of $(x_n)_{n\geq 1}$. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent standard normal random variables defined on the probability space $(\Omega,\EuScript{S},{{\mathbb P}})$. Then the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}

\[
\sum_{n\geq 1}A_n(\omega) c_nx_n
\]
converges in ${\boldsymbol{X}}$ to an element in ${\boldsymbol{Y}}$  for any $\omega\in \Omega\setminus \EuScript{N}$.

\[

0, & \omega\in \EuScript{N}
\end{cases}
\]
is Borel measurable and the push-forward  $\Gamma_S:=S_\# {{\mathbb P}}$ is a nondegenerate Gaussian measure on ${\boldsymbol{Y}}$. 

\item For any  nonempty open subset $\EuScript{O}\subset {\boldsymbol{Y}}$, ${{\mathbb P}}\big[\, S\in \EuScript{O}\,\big]>0$.

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Full-support verification in every variable context including paired S, without orientations","Independent fair algorithmic orientation tie coins; robust source Mis_infinity<=c on every data/coin outcome","All other hypotheses and sample protocol exactly as C013, specialized as stated"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T21:03:25.815424+00:00","domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; verified truth supports","id":"claim_d17d974d73b26ffacf67c5e666254e1060bc965f7a41bc88aeee96c154a3cb86","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Positive-budget global risk differs from expected conditional minimax risk

T379-C014 v2: proof (unaudited), exact rational checks PASS. Target 2;
route-failure of a tempting extension, not a new exact global frontier.

Use the full-verifier, untagged experiment of C013 with d=3,K=2,r=1,
n=1,N>=7. Write lambda=1/(2N), kappa=1/2 and choose robust calibration
budget c=2lambda=1/N. The three pairs are numbered 0,1,2. Conditional
on the verifier output, relabel each certified candidate as 0. Each A
therefore has only candidate 0 true; S has both candidates true. This
relabeling preserves all factual probabilities. Fixed S contexts are
6,...,N-1. The verifier supplies no orientation labels.

One factual sample outside the certified sets resolves exactly one
pair; otherwise all three are unresolved. Thus P(U=3)=1-3lambda and
P(U=2)=3lambda, uniformly in every fixed world and verifier output.
C013's conditional worst-world frontier is zero at U=2 and lambda/2
at U=3. Its expectation is

 E V(c,U)=lambda/2-3lambda^2/2.                         (1)

## Feasible asymmetric algorithm

On U=2, use C013's attainer, removing all posterior mass 2lambda from
the unresolved outside-certificate atoms and adding it to fixed S.
This has zero false mass in every compatible world and Mis<=2lambda.

On U=3, leave pair 0 balanced. For each of pairs 1 and 2, if the factual
sample is a certified candidate in that pair, predict that its context
is A. Otherwise predict either orientation by an independent fair coin.
This is a rule using observed data only. Form two sets of outside-
certificate atoms:

* B1: both atoms of pair 0 and the predicted-S atom of pairs 1 and 2;
* B2: the predicted-A atom of pairs 1 and 2.

Assign g=lambda/4 to each of B1's four atoms, g=0 to B2's two atoms,
g=3lambda/2 to each of the six certified atoms, and
g=lambda+lambda/(N-6) to each of the 2(N-6) fixed S atoms.
These masses sum to lambda+9lambda+2(N-6)lambda+2lambda=1.

For ANY compatible orientation let t be the number of true S atoms
in B1 from pairs 1 and 2. The source mass of B1 is lambda(1+t),
that of B2 is lambda(2-t), and that of the six certified atoms is
9lambda, all with the latter group assigned equal g. The fixed S
group receives exactly 2lambda extra g mass. Uniformly coarsening p
within these four groups gives TV to g equal to

 [t lambda+(2-t)lambda+2lambda]/2=2lambda.

Each group has constant g; the exact score partition can only merge
groups. Uniform averaging is TV-contractive and fixes g, so actual
source Mis_infinity<=2lambda even at N=8 where two scores coincide.
This verifies robust feasibility for every orientation and every coin
realization, without assuming that the orientation predictions are right.

Let E be the number of wrong orientation predictions in pairs 1 and 2.
Exactly one atom of pair 0 is false. Therefore on U=3 the ACTUAL false
mass is

 H=(lambda/4)(1+E).                                   (2)

For example, if both predictions happen to be right, H=lambda/4 is
strictly below the conditional minimax value lambda/2. For the opposite
orientations the same generator has H=3lambda/4. Thus a conditional
worst-world lower bound is not a lower bound in each actual world.

## Expectation in each fixed world

The one-sample categories below are disjoint. Each expected H averages
only the algorithm's independent fair tie coins; their probabilities
are factual sampling probabilities in a fixed actual world.

| Observation | Probability | Expected H |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outside certificate in any S of the three pairs | 3lambda | 0 |
| Certified atom in pair 0 | 3lambda | lambda/2 |
| Certified atom in true A of pair 1 or 2 | 4lambda | 3lambda/8 |
| Certified atom in true S of pair 1 or 2 | 2lambda | 5lambda/8 |
| Fixed S context | 1-12lambda | lambda/2 |

Multiplying and summing gives, in EVERY fixed world and conditional
on EVERY verifier realization,

 E H=lambda/2-7lambda^2/4
     < lambda/2-3lambda^2/2=E V(c,U),                  (3)

with strict gap lambda^2/4=1/(16N^2). Thus the global minimax expected
value is at most the left expression and is strictly below the expected
conditional worst-world value. For N=7 these values are 3/112 versus
11/392, separated by 1/784. No optimality of this algorithm is asserted.

This does not contradict C013, whose exact GLOBAL value was asserted
only at c=0; its positive-budget conditional statement and global bracket
remain intact. This auxiliary-route counterexample is not claimed to
score as a target narrowing. Source calibration definition: Kalai--
Vempala 2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9. All other work here is
an own-work unaudited draft. Priority and independent audit pending.

Exact verification: logs/positive_budget_separation_check.json records
13824 compatible-world feasibility checks, 1920 sample/coin outcomes,
32 fixed-world expectation checks and 384 pointwise negative controls.
The runs include N=7,8,9,12; N=8 checks the merged-score case directly.
The construction and expectation derivation above cover every N>=7.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:36:23.134099+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d194b3d064b052a65f243782076070b4a27cbb94744ff15e5bd7ecc64100ab1c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem MainSeriesKeyLem of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $L_{1},\cdots,L_{r}$ be given vectors
of positive integers and let $n_{0}\geqslant1$. Suppose that $|L_{1}|+\cdots+|L_{r}|+n_{0}=k\leqslant N.$
Then one has 
\begin{align}
 & \sum_{\xi_{0}+\xi_{1}+\cdots+\xi_{r}=l-r}{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{r}}\circ{\rm ad}_{\hat{F}_{w}(H_{L_{r}})}\circ\cdots\circ{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{1}}\circ{\rm ad}_{\hat{F}_{w}(H_{L_{1}})}\circ{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{0}}\big(\hat{F}_{w}(D_{n_{0}}\tilde{L})\big)\nonumber \\
 & =\sum_{i}\sum_{\mu=1}^{r+1}\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}\cdot(b_{i}^{i+n_{0}^{\mu-1}-1})^{l+1-\mu}\nonumber \\
 & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \sum_{I\in{\cal W}_{\mu,r}}\frac{(-1)^{\varepsilon(I)}\Psi_{I,n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf L}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}\cdot}{b_{(i_{\mu}),n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}b_{(i_{\mu},i_{\mu+1}),n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}\cdots b_{I,n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}}E_{i-|{\bf n}_{{\bf p}}^{\mu,r}|,i+n_{0}^{\mu-1}+|{\bf n}_{{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}|}.
\end{align}
Here \textcolor{black}{$\mathcal{W}_{\mu,r}$} denotes the set of words $I=(i_{\mu},i_{\mu+1},\cdots,i_{r})\in\{\pm1\}^{r-\mu+1}$. Given such a word $I$, the vector $\mathbf{p}$
denotes the subword of $(\mu,\cdots,r)$ which records the locations
of $-1$'s in $I$ and ${\bf q}\triangleq(\mu,\cdots,r)\backslash{\bf p}$.
The quantity $\varepsilon(I)$ denotes the length of ${\bf p}$ (i.e.
number of $-1$'s in $I$). The function $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}$
is defined by 
\[
\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}\triangleq\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0},i}(b_{i},b_{i+1},\cdots,b_{i+k-1}),
\]
where $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0},i}$ is a suitable meromorphic
function in $m$ complex variables ($m\triangleq n_{0}+|L_{1}|+\cdots+|L_{\mu-1}|$)
whose shape depends on $(L_{1},\cdots,L_{\mu-1}),n_{0}$ and $i$.
The family $\{\Theta_{L_{1},\cdots,L_{\mu-1},n_{0}}^{i}\}$ of functions
satisfy the following property: for any integer $i$, $1\leqslant\nu\leqslant r$
and any sequence of vectors ${\bf V}=(V_{1},\cdots,V_{r})$, under
the one-dimensional reduction $b_{j}\triangleq b_{j}^{*}+w$ the function
\begin{equation}
w\mapsto\sum_{\sigma\in{\cal S}_{\nu}}\Theta_{V_{\sigma(\nu)},\cdots,V_{\sigma(1)},n_{0}}^{i}
\end{equation}
is analytic near $w=0$ and vanishes at $w=0$. When $\mu=1,$ the
function $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}$ depends only
on $n_{0}$ and $i$. As a convention, if $\mu=r+1$ the summation
$\sum_{I\in{\cal W}(\mu,r)}$ in ((lem:MainSeriesKeyLem of the paper)) is
set to be one and $|{\bf n}_{{\bf p}}^{\mu,r}|=|{\bf n}_{{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}|\triangleq0$
. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:49:06.341725+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d1a070576fba0f9bc92a433f31638306ebe34f1e51076ecd4ef5173c7631c12d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2602.04303, '\Large\textbf{Strong solutions to SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian '] $($Weighted Sobolev sapce$)$ Fie $p_1\in(1,\infty)$. Let $w:\mathbb{R}^d\mapsto[0,\infty)$ be a Borel-measurable function satisfying
			$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+|x|^{p_1})w(x)\mathrm{d} x<\infty.$$
			Let $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d,w)$ denote the Banach space of all the Borel-measurable functions $f$ such that $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|f(x)|^{p_1}w(x)\mathrm{d} x<\infty$ equipped with the norm 
			$$\Vert f\Vert_{L^{p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)}=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|f(x)|^{p_1}w(x)\mathrm{d} x\right)^{\frac1{p_1}}.$$
			Then, the weighted Sobolev space with weight $w$ is defined as the linear space of functions $f\in L^{p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)$ with weak partial derivatives $\frac{\partial}{\partial x_j}f\in L^{p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)$ for $j=1,\cdots,d$. We equip this space with the complete norm
			$$\Vert f\Vert_{W^{1,p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)}:=\Vert f\Vert_{L^{p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)}+\sum_{i=1}^d\left\Vert\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}f\right\Vert_{L^{p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)}.$$","status":"unverified"}

\[\mu^\tau_{\Lambda\setminus\Lambda'}\colon\Omega_{\Lambda\setminus\Lambda'}\to{\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} \colon\sigma\mapsto \sum_{\eta\in\Omega_{\Lambda'}}\mu^\tau_\Lambda(\eta\cdot\sigma).\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:10.967855+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d1c4317ddc05c7087c8a6d882907a4b843a055d2331d1a97dd72af0452edba31","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.12820, 'Averaging principles for nonautonomous multiscale McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems'] For a matrix-valued map $h(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot):\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n)\times\mR^m\rightarrow\mR^{n \times d_1}$, we say $h\in C^{k,(1,d),l}(\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n)\times\mR^m,\mR^{n \times d_1})$, if $h(x,\cdot,y)\in C^{(1,d)}(\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $x\in\mR^n,y\in\mR^m$, and $h(\cdot,\mu,\cdot)\in C^{k,l}(\mR^n\times\mR^m,\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $\mu\in\cP_2(\mR^n)$, and the derivatives

{"assumptions":["1 < p <= q < infinity and e^{-t} <= sqrt((p-1)/(q-1))","the standard Gaussian measure and the generator normalisation L = Laplacian minus x . gradient","the constant in the contraction is exactly 1 and is dimension-free"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543694+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d1cf7dae8a836624c27473f7845ae1273f14a2ce5a18a3ccc841f38670804eeb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (P_t) be the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup on L^p of the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For 1 < p <= q < infinity, || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_p for every f, PROVIDED e^{-t} <= sqrt( (p-1)/(q-1) ). The constant is exactly 1 - the semigroup is a contraction from L^p to the strictly larger L^q, not merely bounded - and the condition on t is sharp. Two consequences used constantly: taking p = 2 gives || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_2 for e^{-t} = 1/sqrt(q-1); and restricting to the n-th Wiener chaos, where P_t acts as multiplication by e^{-nt}, gives the MOMENT COMPARISON || F ||_q <= (q-1)^{n/2} || F ||_2 for every F in the n-th chaos and every q >= 2. That comparison is dimension-free and is the reason all L^q norms on a fixed chaos are equivalent, with a constant depending only on the chaos order and q. GROSS'S THEOREM: hypercontractivity of (P_t) with these exponents is EQUIVALENT to the logarithmic Sobolev inequality Ent(f^2) <= 2 E|grad f|^2 for the same measure; each implies the other by differentiating or integrating the relation at q = q(t). The discrete-cube analogue with the noise operator is the Bonami-Beckner inequality, and the Gaussian case follows from it by the central limit theorem. [Nelson (1966, 1973); Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["covariates satisfy an isoperimetric (concentration) inequality, e.g. Gaussian, uniform on the sphere, or a mixture of such","labels have irreducible noise of variance sigma^2 > 0","the model class has p parameters in the sense of a log covering number of order p","the model fits the data below the noise floor (an interpolation-type condition)"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049028+00:00","domain":"learning theory (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_d1d727b283a6487fc2bb1b7576453bf946721a7c8e73d18d800d0f36de04d9dc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Bubeck and Sellke (2021): let (x_i, y_i), i = 1..n, be data with covariates x_i in R^d drawn from a distribution satisfying isoperimetry (Lipschitz functions of x concentrate like they do for a Gaussian; a mixture of such distributions is allowed) and labels y_i carrying genuine noise (conditional variance sigma^2 > 0 that no function of x can remove). Let F be a class of functions parametrized by p real parameters (more precisely, with log covering number of order p). Then with high probability every f in F that fits the data to within a constant fraction of the noise level (a fraction of the sum of the y_i's conditional variances remains unexplained) has Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n d / p), up to logarithmic factors. Consequence: interpolating n noisy points in dimension d smoothly (Lipschitz constant O(1)) needs p of order n d parameters, a factor d beyond the n needed merely to memorize. The bound is vacuous without noise (a smooth interpolant can exist) and without the isoperimetry hypothesis on the covariates.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:16:46.102491+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d1f31894947d57e91d98c5aff8b0897234abacea84d9cf9a27da436f0d5c60df","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm main:IG of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] The following hold for all $\omega$ in a full $\mathbb{P}$-probability event and for all $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$.
\begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt

\item
$\IG\theta$ is closed, nowhere dense, and has no isolated points.

\item
The connected components of the open set $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\IG\theta$ are all bounded, and distinct components have disjoint closures. Moreover, there are countably infinitely many such components. We call these components \emph{stability islands}.

\item Each island has a unique boundary point with minimal time, called the \emph{bottom}, and a unique boundary point with maximal time, called the \emph{tip}. The boundary of the island consists of two continuous space-time paths, the \emph{left boundary} and the \emph{right boundary}, each connecting the bottom to the tip. Except at the bottom and the tip, the left boundary lies strictly to the left of the right boundary.

\item The islands are dense in $\IG\theta$: for any $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\rho>0$, there exists an island whose closure is inside the ball of radius $\rho$ and center $(x,s)$.\vspace{2pt}

Let $\mathcal D^\theta$ denote the subset of $\IG\theta$ consisting of points that are not on the boundary of any stability island. Points in $\mathcal D^\theta$ are called \emph{dust points}.\vspace{4pt}

\item
$\mathcal D^\theta$ {\rm(}and hence also $\IG\theta${\rm)} is temporally bi-infinite: there exists an uncountable family of continuous bi-infinite space-time paths $\tau_\alpha:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\tau_\alpha(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathcal D^\theta$ for all $\alpha$, the paths are pairwise disjoint
{\rm(}$\tau_\alpha(\mathbb{R})\cap\tau_\beta(\mathbb{R})=\varnothing$ for $\alpha\ne\beta${\rm)}, and each path is $\theta$-directed in both time directions, i.e.\ $t^{-1}\tau_\alpha(t)\to(\theta,1)$ as $|t|\to\infty$.

\item For any $s\in\mathbb{R}$, the set $\mathcal D^\theta\cap(\mathbb{R}\times\{s\})$ has no isolated points and is unbounded above and below. Moreover, for any $a<b$ such that $\IG\theta\cap((a,b)\times\{s\})\neq\varnothing$, the set $\mathcal D^\theta\cap((a,b)\times\{s\})$ is uncountable.

\item For each $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$, there exists at least one continuous bi-infinite space-time path through $(x,s)$ that remains on $\IG\theta$ and is $\theta$-directed in both time directions.

\item
$\IG\theta$ forms a path-connected graph: for any $(x,s),(y,t)\in\IG\theta$, there exist $z,z'\in\mathbb{R}$ and times $r<s\wedge t\le s\vee t<r'$ such that $(z,r),(z',r')\in\IG\theta$, and there are continuous space-time paths contained in $\IG\theta$ from $(z,r)$ to each of $(x,s)$ and $(y,t)$, and from each of these two points to $(z',r')$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:42:08.469985+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d205b82822862b043fea1969dbf66d0b3bbae9b4b916bebb1315229513e096f6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:increment of arXiv:2511.17101, 'Central limit theorem for the range of critical branching random walk'] \begin{enumerate}
\item
The sequence $(\Delta C(i))_{i\ge 1}$ is i.i.d., taking values in $\{1,-1\}$ with probability $\frac 1 2$ each.
\item
When $\Delta C(i)=1$, $\Delta V(i)$ is a uniform unit vector independent of $\sigma(C(-\infty,i-1],V(-\infty,i-1])$.
\item 
When $\Delta C(i)=-1$, $\Delta V(i)$ is the vector from $u_{i-1}$ to $\overleftarrow{u_{i-1}}$, completely determined by $(C(-\infty,i-1],V(-\infty,i-1])$.
\item In particular, $u_{2i-1}$ is bad if and only if $\Delta C(2i-1)=1,\Delta C(2i)=-1$, and $-\Delta V(2i-1)=\Delta V(2i)$ is the vector from $u_{2i-2}$ to its parent. Therefore,
\[
\mathbb P\parsof{u_{2i-1}\text{ is bad}}{C(-\infty,2i-2],V(-\infty,2i-2]}=\frac 1{8d},
\]
and the event $\{u_{2i-1}\text{ is bad}\}$ is independent of the past $\sigma$-algebra  $\sigma(C(-\infty,2i-2],V(-\infty,2i-2])$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

        \[

            \text{\emph{ conditioned on $\mathbf a_i$,}}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.772445+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d252a8fd0252e7170506cfada985f15bcf94747300f62a105cb9082e2ba6807f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 15 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Let $\theta^0$, $\{b^t\}_{t \geq 0}$, and $\{g^t\}_{t \geq 0}$
be mutually independent scalar variables/processes on a filtered
probability space $(\Omega,\cF,\{\cF_t\}_{t \geq 0},\P)$, where
$\Law(\theta^0)$ is given by Assumption \ref{assump:dynamics}(c),
$\{b^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ is a standard $\cF_t$-adapted Brownian motion, and
\[\{g^t\}_{t \geq 0} \sim \GP(0,C_g)\]
is a continuous, mean-zero, $\cF_t$-adapted Gaussian process with a symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariance kernel $C_g:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty)
\to \R$. Let $\{\theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ be the solution of the SDE
\begin{equation}
\d\theta^t=\left[f(\theta^t)+\int_0^t R_g(t,s)\theta^s ds+g^t\right]
\d t+\sqrt{2 \gamma}\,\d b^t, \qquad \theta^t|_{t=0}=\theta^0,
\end{equation}
where $R_g:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty) \to \R$
is a response kernel satisfying $R_g(t,s)=0$ for $s>t$. Let
$\{\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\}_{t \geq s \geq 0}$ be the solution of the
response equation
\begin{equation}
\frac{\d}{\d t} \frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}=\left[f'(\theta^t)\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}
+\int_s^t R_g(t,r)\frac{\d \theta^r}{\d g^s}\d r\right],
\qquad \frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\bigg|_{t=s}=1.
\end{equation}
These kernels $C_g,R_g$, in conjunction with a pair of auxiliary kernels
$C_\theta,R_\theta:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty) \to \R$,
are self-consistently defined from the laws of the above processes by the
fixed point conditions
\begin{align}
C_\theta(t,s)&=\E[\theta^t \theta^s]\\
R_\theta(t,s)&=\E\left[\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\right]
\text{ for } s \in [0,t],
\quad R_\theta(t,s)=0 \text{ for } s>t,
\\
C_g(t,s)&=\sum_{p,q \geq 0} \kappa_{p+q+2}\,
R_\theta^{\ast p} * C_\theta * \bar R_\theta^{\ast q}(t,s),
\quad
\text{ where } \bar R_\theta(t,s)=R_\theta(s,t) \text{ for all } s,t \geq 0,\\
R_g(t,s)&=\sum_{p \geq 1} \kappa_{p+1}\,R_\theta^{\ast p}(t,s).
\end{align}
Here, $A*B$ denotes the standard convolution for kernels defined over
$[0,\infty)$,
\[[A \ast B](t,s)=\int_0^\infty A(t,r)B(r,s)\d r,
\quad A^{\ast p}=\underbrace{A \ast \ldots \ast A}_{p \text{
times}}, \quad A^{\ast 0}*B=B*A^{\ast 0}=B.\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f lower semicontinuous AND bounded below (boundedness below can be relaxed to a linear minorant);","the approximation is from BELOW and increasing.","For an upper semicontinuous f bounded above the dual sup-convolution gives a decreasing sequence of Lipschitz functions."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:01:51.298930+00:00","domain":"real analysis, convex analysis","id":"claim_d260b03e2f3333274936e1cd451507f7f128ecfe5257b820323708fee2f6bbf4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a metric space and let f : X -> (-infinity, +infinity] be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. For each n define f_n(x) = inf over y in X of ( f(y) + n d(x,y) ). Then each f_n is real-valued and n-Lipschitz, the sequence is nondecreasing, f_n <= f for every n, and f_n(x) increases to f(x) at every x. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:05:09.630000+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d26e3fae6618b03d40b56c873a44b791e77af6fa124000a5f177c47238854c10","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:lower_bound_gaussian_lim of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with

Gaussian component of $\bm{X}$ in its L\'evy--It\^o decomposition~(equation eq:levy_ito_decomp of the paper) and define

{"assumptions":["Injectivity of the solution map does not imply continuity of its inverse","The range of the forward solution operator is a proper dense subspace","Conditional (Holder) stability requires an a priori bound at the initial time and degenerates as t tends to 0"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.107167+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations / inverse problems","id":"claim_d293093269857df5a07b55e84088e12c20119ec34fc0008386b758c4e986eecc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Backward uniqueness says the map from $u(\\cdot,T)$ to $u(\\cdot,0)$ is injective; it says nothing about continuity of that map or about its range, and both fail badly -- the backward heat problem is the standard ill-posed problem of Hadamard. (1) No stability: on $U=(0,\\pi)$ with Dirichlet data, $u_k(x,t)=e^{-k^2t}\\sin(kx)$ has $\\|u_k(\\cdot,T)\\|_{C^m}\\le k^me^{-k^2T}\\to0$ for every $m$ while $\\|u_k(\\cdot,0)\\|_{L^2}=\\sqrt{\\pi/2}$ is fixed. Hence there is no estimate $\\|u(\\cdot,0)\\|\\le C\\|u(\\cdot,T)\\|$ in any pair of norms, and numerical backward continuation must be regularized. (2) No solvability: $e^{T\\Delta_D}$ has range $\\{\\psi=\\sum_kc_k\\sin(kx):\\sum_k e^{2k^2T}c_k^2<\\infty\\}$, a dense but meagre subspace of $L^2$; for instance $\\psi(x)=\\sum_{k\\ge1}k^{-2}\\sin(kx)\\in L^2$ is not $u(\\cdot,T)$ for any solution with $u(\\cdot,0)\\in L^2$, since that would require coefficients $e^{k^2T}k^{-2}$ at time $0$. Backward-in-time data must be analytic-like (exponentially decaying spectral coefficients). (3) What does survive is conditional stability of logarithmic or Holder type: under the a priori bound $\\|u(\\cdot,0)\\|_{L^2}\\le M$, log-convexity gives $\\|u(\\cdot,t)\\|_{L^2}\\le M^{1-t/T}\\|u(\\cdot,T)\\|_{L^2}^{t/T}$ for $0<t<T$, with the estimate degenerating exactly as $t\\downarrow0$. An auditor should flag any argument that uses backward uniqueness to produce a bound at the earlier time without such an a priori bound.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.233527+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d2a0dcd257710e1834d13e5faeef247b13c8eca9593d239904d89474fb22667b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 33 (Airy uniformisation and cubic Stokes multiplier) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let
\[
 H_3(x)=x^3-3x,
 \qquad
 \varphi_3(t)
 =
 \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \int_{\R}
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{x^2}{2}+itH_3(x)\right)\dd x .
\]
Then \(\varphi_3\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 27t^3(18t^2+1)y''
 +(486t^4+99t^2+1)y'
 +6t(18t^2+1)^2y=0.

\end{equation}

On a simply connected sector at \(t=0\) containing the positive real
axis, choose the branches for which \(t^{1/3}>0\) when \(t>0\), and put
\begin{align}
 z(t)
 &=
 \frac{1-36t^2}
 {12\,3^{1/3}t^{4/3}},
 \\
 C(t)
 &=
 \sqrt{2\pi}\,
 (3t)^{-1/3}
 \exp\!\left(\frac1{108t^2}-\frac12\right),
 \\
 \zeta(t)
 &=
 \frac23 z(t)^{3/2}
 =
 \frac{(1-36t^2)^{3/2}}{108t^2}.
 
\end{align}
Then the real Gaussian cycle is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \varphi_3(t)=F_0(t):=C(t)\Ai(z(t)),
 \qquad t>0.

\end{equation}
In particular, the local solution space of \eqref{eq:h3-airy-ode} is the
pullback, with gauge \(C(t)\), of the Airy equation
\[
 w''(z)=zw(z).
\]

Let \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\) and define
\begin{align}
 F_+(t)
 &=
 C(t)e^{i\pi/6}\Ai(\omega z(t)),
 \\
 F_-(t)
 &=
 C(t)e^{-i\pi/6}\Ai(\omega^2 z(t)).
 
\end{align}
The functions \(F_+\) and \(F_-\) are the two lateral sectorial
realisations of the same dominant formal solution at the positive real
Stokes ray, and
\begin{equation}
 F_+(t)-F_-(t)=iF_0(t).

\end{equation}
Consequently, for
\[
 \mathcal Y_-=(F_0,F_-),
 \qquad
 \mathcal Y_+=(F_0,F_+),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Y_+
 =
 \mathcal Y_-
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&i\\
 0&1
 \end{pmatrix}.

\end{equation}
Thus the multiplier selected by the real Gaussian cycle is nonzero and,
in the normalisation \eqref{eq:h3-Fplus}--\eqref{eq:h3-Fminus}, equals
\(i\).  Reversing the orientation replaces \(i\) by \(-i\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:52:17.366014+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d2ac658add71f430966436be8bacdfffcf232fd4e27539ea4fd5e7f1471fb1d2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3 (SDE theory) of arXiv:2606.02786, 'Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups'] Let $d \geq 2$. Assume that the Borel measurable drift $b:\mathbb R^{1+d} \rightarrow \mathbb R^d$ satisfies {\rm($\mathbf{H}_1$)}. (Or, in complete generality, assume that the operator norms in \eqref{adams_est_weight}, \eqref{adams_est2_weight} are sufficiently small.)
Then
 the following are true:
 
 \smallskip

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] 

\item {\rm (Weak existence)} For each $x \in \mathbb R^d$ and $0 \leq s < T$, there exists a  probability measure $\mathbb P_{s,x}$ on $\mathbf{D}_{s,T}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item 
$$
\mathbb P_{s,x}[\omega_s=x]=1,
$$

\item
$$
\mathbb E_{s,x}\int_s^t |b(r,\omega_r)|dr<\infty, \quad t \geq s,
$$

\item 
$$
\omega_t = x - \int_s^t b(r, \omega_r) dr + Z_t-Z_s,
$$
for an $\alpha$-stable process $Z_t$ defined on the completion of  $\mathbf{D}_{s,T}$ with respect to $\mathbb P_{s,x}$. 
\end{enumerate}

That is, the pair (coordinate process $X_t$, $Z_t$ defined via (c)) is a weak solution to the SDE \eqref{sde1}.

Also, assuming that the constant $\theta$ in the definition of weight $\rho$ is fixed to satisfy $d<\theta<d+\alpha$, and $\kappa$ is fixed sufficiently small, the following Krylov-type bound holds: for every $x \in \mathbb R^d$ and any Borel vector field $\mathsf{f}:\mathbb R^{1+d} \rightarrow \mathbb R^d$ that admits decomposition \eqref{b_decomp} with finite Morrey norm of the singular part, for every $p>d+1$ 
there exists a constant $K$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb E_{s,x}\int_s^T |\mathsf{f}(r,\omega_r)h(r,\omega_r)|dr \leq K\|\mathbf{1}_{[0,T]}|\mathsf{f}|^{\frac{1}{p}} h\|_{L_\rho^p}, 
\end{equation}
for all $h \in C_b(\mathbb R^{1+d})$.
In particular, taking $\mathsf{f}=b$, we obtain that the constructed weak solution to \eqref{sde1} does not spend too much time around the singular set of the drift. 
This Krylov-type bound also holds for $|\mathsf{f}|=1$ and $h \in (C_b \cap L^p)(\mathbb R^{1+d})$.

\medskip

\item {\rm (Feller propagator)}
The operators
\begin{equation}

P^{t,r}f(x):=\mathbb E_{t,x}[f(X_r)], \quad 0 \leq t \leq r, \quad x \in \mathbb R^d
\end{equation}
constitute a backward Feller propagator on $C_\infty$.

\medskip

\item  {\rm (Conditional weak uniqueness)} Let $x \in \mathbb R^d$. Any probability measure $\mathbb Q_{s,x}$ on $\mathbf{D}_{s,T}$ that satisfies (a)-(c) in (\textit{i}) and, for some $p>d+1$ from (\textit{i}),
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{s,x}}\int_s^T |h(r,\omega_r)|dr \leq K\|\mathbf{1}_{[s,T]}h\|_{p},
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{s,x}}\int_s^T |b(r,\omega_r)h(r,\omega_r)|dr \leq K\|\mathbf{1}_{[s,T]}|b|^{\frac{1}{p}}h\|_{p}
\end{equation*}
for all $h \in (C_b \cap L^p)(\mathbb R^{1+d})$ also satisfies $$\mathbb Q_{s,x}=\mathbb P_{s,x}$$
(it is seen that the weak solution constructed in {\rm (\textit{i})} satisfies the previous two inequalities).

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

for every $V \in \dom{\Ent_\QP}$ and $n \in \N$. We denote by $\MM_\tau(U_\tau^0) \subset \mcP_{[U_\tau^0]}(\U)^{\times \infty}$ the collection of all $\tau$-discrete minimising movements starting at~$U_\tau^0$;

$$\overline{U}_\tau(t):={U}^n_\tau \quad t \in ((n-1)\tau, n\tau) \cquad \overline{U}_\tau(0):=U^0_\tau \scolon$$
\item We say that a curve $u: [0,+\infty) \to \mcP_{[u_0]}(\U)$ is a {\it minimising movement (a.k.a.~JKO scheme)}, denoted by $u \in \MM(\mcP_{[u_0]}(\U), \mssW_{2, \mssd_\U}, \Ent_\QP)$,  if $u(0)=u_0 \in \dom{\Ent_\QP}$ and there exists an element~$(U_\tau^n)_{n \in \N} \in \MM_\tau(u_0)$ for sufficiently small $\tau$ such that its piecewise constant interpolation~$\overline{U}_\tau$ satisfies

$$\mssW_{2, \mssd_\U}\text{-}\lim_{\tau \downarrow 0}\overline{U}_\tau(t)=u(t) \quad t \ge 0  \fstop$$
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:48:30.920892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d2ee27e3fff78f733aab52028fa5098ce9d2e317533b205d04d28538bd7ce8b0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 12 (Partial Fraction Decomposition, {\cite[Theorem 2) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] {PFD_euclidean_1989}}]
    Let $k$ be a field of any characteristic.
    Let $f\in k(x)$ be a rational function. Let $f=\frac{a}{b}$ be a presentation of $f$, where $a,b\in k[x]$ and $(a,b)=1$. Let $b=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i^{m_i}$ be a decomposition into pairwise distinct irreducible factors. Then, there exists the \textbf{partial fraction decomposition} (PFD) of $f$:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item A polynomial $Q\in k[x]$.
        \item For each $1\le i\le n$ and $1\le j\le m_i$ a polynomial $s_{ij}\in k[x]$ with $\op{deg}(s_{ij})<\op{deg}(p_i)$.
    \end{itemize}
    These polynomials are\textbf{ unique} such that the following equality holds:
    \[
    f=Q+\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} \frac{s_{ij}}{p_i^j}.
    \]
    In particular, if $k$ is algebraically closed, then, without any loss of generality, we can assume that $p_i=x-a_i$, so $s_{ij}\in k$ and we define:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Polynomial Part: $P(f)=Q$
        \item Logarithmic Part: $L(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{s_{i1}}{x-a_i}$, and we call $s_{i1}$ the residue of $f$ at $a_i$.
        \item Higher Part: $H(f)=\sum_{i>1}^n\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} \frac{s_{ij}}{{(x-a_i)}^j}$
    \end{enumerate}
    In total, we have $f=PFD(f)=P(f)+L(f)+H(f)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.017447+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d2f91ba1715071477e14b671c751b0d520ef9e14ac7a4192586af86387f779b1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 10 (Conditional determinantal resampling kernel) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $(z_{ij})$ be the complex Gaussian array above, and let $((m_t,n_t))_{t=0}^T$ be an elementary up-right path with $T\geq1$. Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_t&=\min(m_t,n_t),
 &q_t&=\max(m_t,n_t),
 &r_t&=q_t-p_t,\\
 \epsilon_t&=p_{t+1}-p_t,
 &P&=p_T.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Condition on all entries of
\[
 X_0=(z_{ij})_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m_0\\1\leq j\leq n_0}},
\]
and let
\[
 x_1>\cdots>x_{p_0}>0
\]
be its positive squared singular values. Define
\[
 \kappa_t=\epsilon_{t-1}(r_{t-1}-1)-\epsilon_tr_t
 \quad(1\leq t<T),
 \qquad
 \kappa_T=\epsilon_{T-1}(r_{T-1}-1),
\]
and
\[
 w_t(u)=u^{\kappa_t}\quad(t<T),
 \qquad
 w_T(u)=\ee^{-u}u^{\kappa_T}.
\]

Let
\[
 E_t=(0,\infty)\sqcup\{v_{p_t+1},\ldots,v_P\},
 \qquad 1\leq t\leq T.
\]
Use the augmented transfers $B_t$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:arbitrary-path-kernel}. Define source states
\[
 \zeta_i=
 \begin{cases}
 x_i,&i\leq p_0,\\
 v_i,&i>p_0,
 \end{cases}
\]
and define on $E_1$
\[
 \phi_i(y)=
 \begin{cases}
 B_0(\zeta_i,y)w_1(y),&y>0,\\
 B_0(\zeta_i,v_k),&y=v_k.
 \end{cases}
\]
For $1\leq t<T$, define $W_t$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:arbitrary-path-kernel}, and put
\[
 \psi_i(y)=y^{P-i}.
\]
Let $F_i^{(t)}$, $G_j^{(t)}$, and $M$ be the corresponding forward functions, backward functions, and moment matrix.

Conditionally on $X_0$, augment each strictly future configuration by its deterministic virtual points. This conditional process is determinantal, $M$ is finite and invertible, and its kernel is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_x(s,z;t,y)
 &=-\ind_{\{s<t\}}W_{s,t}(z,y)\\
 &\quad{}+\sum_{i,j=1}^P
 G_j^{(s)}(z)(M^{-1})_{ji}F_i^{(t)}(y),
 \qquad 1\leq s,t\leq T.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Restriction to real arguments gives the conditional multi-time process of positive squared singular values. The kernel depends on $X_0$ only through $x$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:58:24.514661+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d2fdfc8643839364f1037604a92f27311c93eaabc0d837f8886b49c59bdd4c1d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm t:mm of arXiv:2601.09537, 'Gene genealogies in haploid populations evolving according to sweepstakes reproduction'] (Thm.~1 of [M98])

Let $X_N = (X_N(r))_{r \in \ensuremath{\mathds N}_0}$ be a sequence of time homogeneous  Markov
chains on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ with the same finite
state space $S$ and let $\Pi_N$ denote the transition matrix of $X_N$. Assume
that the following conditions are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The square matrix $A := \lim_{N\to \infty}\Pi_N $ exists and $\Pi_N \neq A $ for $N$ large enough.
\item The matrix $P := \lim_{m\to \infty}A^m$ exists.
\item The matrix $G := \lim_{N\to \infty}PB_NP $ exists, where  $B_N := (\Pi_N
 - A)/c_N$, and $c_N := \ensuremath{\left\lVert \Pi_N - A \right\rVert }  $ for all $N \in \ensuremath{\mathds N}$.

If the sequence of initial probability measures $P_{X_N(0) }$ converges weakly

continuous Markov process $\{X_t; t \ge 0 \}$ with initial distribution 
\bd
    X_0 \overset{d}{=} \mu,

transition matrix $\Pi(t) = P - I + e^{tG} = Pe^{tG}$, and infinitesimal
generator $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:47:53.350974+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3230833e7efd12de6216c3eff4c3e041e15e9c05edeae6163c37f1f3c1a3053","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\nu,q\in\Prob(\RR)$ such that Assumption~\ref{ass:technical-assumptions} holds, let $f$ be the corresponding $n$-atomic $q$-Bass map, and let
$\Ccal\in \Lambda_\nu^{p_1,\dots,p_n}$.
Let $r \in \NN$, $\emptyset \neq I \subsetneq \{1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\iadd \notin I$, and
$h \in [0, \diam(\supp(q)))^{n-1}$.
Define
\[
H = \max \left(
\max_{i \in I \cup \{\iadd\}} \widetilde f_i^{-1}(\Ccal_i),
\|h\|_\infty
\right),
\]
where $\widetilde f:\RR_{\ge 0}\to\RR^{n-1}$ is given by
\begin{equation}

	\widetilde f_i(h) = \int_\RR Q_\nu\!\left(p_i^* F_q(z) + (1-p_i^*)F_q(z-h)\right)\, p_i^* \rho_q(z)\,dz.
\end{equation}
Assume that there exists $L\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
\max_{\substack{
\xi \in [0,H]^{n-1}\\
\Jcal \subseteq \{1,\dots,n-1\}\\
i,j \in \Jcal,\ i\neq j
}}
\left|
\frac{\adj(Jf(\xi)_{\Jcal,\Jcal})_{ij}}{\adj(Jf(\xi)_{\Jcal,\Jcal})_{ii}}
\right|
\le L,
\qquad
K:=1-L.
\]
Let $\delta$ be the minimal diagonal gap of $\Ccal$, and let $i_\delta$ be a minimal-gap index for $\Ccal$.
Assume that $i_\delta \notin I$.
Let $\Ccal^{(r)}$ be the $L$-approximation of $\Ccal$ of order $r$ along $i_\delta$, and let
$E^{(r)}$ be the corresponding error map of order $r$.
Assume that $E_i^{(r)}(h)=0$, for all $i \in I$. If $\iadd=i_\delta$, assume moreover that
\begin{equation}
	
(i_\delta=1 \implies 2 \in I),\qquad
(i_\delta=n-1 \implies n-2 \in I),\qquad
(1<i_\delta<n-1 \implies i_\delta-1,\, i_\delta+1 \in I).
\end{equation}
Suppose that there exists $m \in \NN$ such that
\begin{equation}

|E_{\iadd}^{(r)}(h)| \le L^m K\delta
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sup_{\substack{j=1,\dots,n-1 \\ j \neq \iadd}} |E_j^{(r)}(h)|
\le \sum_{k=1}^m L^k K\delta
\le L\delta.
\end{equation}
Then there exists $\widehat h \in [0,H]^{n-1}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item  $\widehat h_i = h_i$ for all $i \notin I \cup \{\iadd\}$, and
    $E_i^{(r)}(\widehat h)=0$ for all $i \in I \cup \{\iadd\}$;
    \item  the following bound holds:
    \[
    \sup_{j=1,\dots,n-1} |E_j^{(r)}(\widehat h)|
    \le \sum_{k=1}^{m+1} L^k K\delta
    \le L\delta.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:05:57.774401+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d33191c1458e93b51dc31850206d53134b261e002ea7837d2f27736aa08d6b12","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX, d)$ be a quasi-metric space and let $\emptyset \neq \SC \subset \XX$ be bounded.
  Then, writing $\AR^\ast := (\umd(\SC))^{-1}$, the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item (A suitable family of controlled complexity achieves every rate below $\AR^\ast$)
          There exists a family $(\CalA_n^\ast)_{n \in \N}$ of subsets
          $\emptyset \neq \CalA_n^\ast \subset \XX$
          of controlled complexity in $\XX$ such that for every $0 \leq \AR < \AR^\ast$,
          there exists $C(\AR) > 0$ satisfying
          \[
            \sup_{x \in \SC} \,\, \dist(x, \CalA_n^\ast) \leq C(\AR) \cdot n^{-\AR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N.
          \]

    \item (No family of controlled complexity can achieve a rate above $\AR^\ast$
          uniformly over $\SC$)
          Let $(\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}$ be a family of controlled complexity in $\XX$.
          If
          \begin{equation}
            \sup_{x \in \SC} \,\, \dist(x, \CalA_n) \leq C(\AR) \cdot n^{-\AR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N
            
          \end{equation}
          holds for some $\AR \geq 0$ and some constant $C(\AR) > 0$, then $\AR \leq \AR^\ast$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Now, set $\AR^\sharp := \bigl( \lmd (\SC) \bigr)^{-1}$ and
  assume that $\mu$ is a probability measure on $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$.
  Then the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),resume]
    \item (Any rate above $\AR^\sharp$ is only achievable on a $\mu$-null set)
          For every $\AR > \AR^\sharp$ and every family $(\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}$
          of subsets $\emptyset \neq \CalA_n \subset \XX$ of controlled complexity in $\XX$,
          the set
          \[
            \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr)
            := \Bigl\{
                 x \in \SC
                 \,\,:\,\,
                 \sup_{n \in \N}
                 \bigl(
                   n^\AR \cdot \dist (x, \CalA_n)
                 \bigr)
                 < \infty
               \Bigr\}
          \]
          is a $\mu$-null set, i.e.,
          $\mu^\ast \bigl( \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr) \bigr) = 0$.
          In fact, we even have
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \biggl(\,\,
              \bigcup_{\AR \in (\AR^\sharp, \infty)}
                \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr)
            \biggr)
            = 0
            .
          \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:51:12.739828+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d35af5f7e23e13eae1bf60058462292ba160261820f287e83bfe11ffb5eb8cd8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 5 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{GW trees and forests}) Let $\mu\eqo (\mu(k))_{k\in \bbN}$ 
be a probability measure on $\bbN$. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{a})\, $ A \textit{GW tree with offspring distribution $\mu$} (a \textit{GW($\mu$)-tree}, for short) is a random tree $\tau$  that satisfies the following. 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[] \textbf{(1):} $k_\varnothing (\tau)$ has law $\mu$. \textbf{(2):} For all $k\ino \bbN^*$ such that $\mu(k)\! >\! 0$, the subtrees $\theta_{(1)} \tau, \ldots , \theta_{(k)} \tau$ under $\bP (\, \cdot \, | k_\varnothing (\tau)\! = \! k)$ are independent with the same law as $\tau$ under $\bP$. 
\end{compactenum}

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{b})\, $ Let $(\tau^{_{(k)}}_{^{\!}})_{k\in \bbN^*}$ be i.i.d.~GW($\mu$)-trees. We generically denote by $\tau_\infty$ the tree associated with the forest $(\tau^{_{(k)}}_{^{\!}})_{k\in \bbN^*}$. We call $\tau_\infty$ a GW($\mu$)-forest. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{c})\, $ We say that $\tau$ is a \emph{grafted GW($\mu$)-tree} if $k_\varnothing (\tau)\eqo 1$ and if $\theta_{(1)}\tau$ is a GW($\mu$)-tree. \cq","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.562496+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d366b05412a3e341a925361e2bcac865f52b1b7fa52494cce480623291c2309f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn of arXiv:2603.13873, '{Solvability of BSDEs with possibly unbounded stochastic coefficients \\ on a general weig'] A continuous function $u(t,x):[0,T]\times {\mathbb R}^n\rightarrow {\mathbb R}^k$ with $u(T,\cdot)=h(\cdot)$ is a viscosity sub-solution (super-solution) of PDE (equation PDE' of the paper) if for any $1\leq i\leq k$ and any function $\phi\in C^{1,2}([0,T]\times {\mathbb R}^n;{\mathbb R})$, it holds that
$$
\frac{\partial \phi(t_0,x_0)}{\partial t}+\mathcal{L}\phi(t_0,x_0)+g_i(t_0,x_0,u(t_0,x_0),
(\nabla_x\phi\sigma)(t_0,x_0))\geq 0\  (\leq 0),

as long as the function $u_i-\phi$ has a local maximum (minimum) at the point $(t_0,x_0)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}^n$. A viscosity solution of PDE (equation PDE' of the paper) is both a viscosity sub-solution and viscosity super-solution.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.298544+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d36aadf58ab0d13884210791987860ff7ccf3a869661d3036493ad47e1a35ca8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Fixed-measurement posterior information budget) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Fix a measurement value $r$ with $0<p_R(r)<\infty$ and define
\[
q_t^r(x):=p_t(x\mid r),
\qquad
\mathcal K_t(r):=\KL(q_t^r\|p_t).
\]
Let $0<s<t<\infty$.  Assume $\mathcal K_s(r)<\infty$, the relative Fisher
information
\[
\int q_u^r(x)
\left\|\nabla\log\frac{q_u^r(x)}{p_u(x)}\right\|^2\dd x
\]
is integrable over $u\in[s,t]$, and the integration-by-parts boundary terms
vanish.  Then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal K_s(r)-\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\int_s^t
\E_{X_u\mid r}\|g_u(X_u,r)\|^2\,\dd u.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for almost every $t>0$ (and at every differentiability point),
\begin{equation}

-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\E_{X_t\mid r}\|g_t(X_t,r)\|^2.
\end{equation}
Averaging over the measurement gives
\begin{equation}

\MI(R;X_s)-\MI(R;X_t)
=
\int_s^t\E\|g_u(X_u,R)\|^2\,\dd u,
\qquad
-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\MI(R;X_t)
=
\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2
\end{equation}
whenever the derivative exists.  Thus force energy is the forward-time
dissipation rate of posterior--prior relative entropy, or the corresponding
reverse-time assimilation rate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:38:25.210318+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d377750ce2a4a4ea29cc3f31320391e3be52e3274f8c248f6ca1e0bb71f98bcf","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be a compact, orientable 3-manifold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{irreducible} if and only if every 2-sphere in $M$ bounds a copy of $D^3$ in $M$.
    \item We say that an orientable embedded surface $F$ in $M$ with $\partial F \subseteq \partial M$ is \emph{compressible} if either
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item there exists a curve $k \subseteq \mathring{F}$, homotopically essential in $F$, and a disc $D \subseteq M$ with $\mathring{D} \subseteq \mathring{M}$ and $D \cap F = \partial D =k$; or
        \item there exists a 3-ball $E \subseteq M$ with $E \cap F = \partial E$.
    \end{enumerate}
    If an orientable, embedded surface $F$ is not compressible, we say that $F$ is \emph{incompressible}.
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{boundary irreducible} if and only if $\partial M$ is incompressible.
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{Haken} (or sufficiently large) if it contains an incompressible surface.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.501734+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d38ed9fc1e17f4dfce2eb8e15ab63c4dd61992ec0cfb8abeae8bc29607040e8f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition eq:general-mixture of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:general-moment-correction}
Fix \(q\ge1\).  Let \(Q\) be any symmetric probability law with finite
moments through order \(2q\).  For all sufficiently small
\(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a symmetric compactly supported
\(C^\infty\) density \(\nu_\varepsilon\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \mu_\varepsilon=\varepsilon Q+(1-\varepsilon)\nu_\varepsilon
\end{equation}
matches the standard Gaussian moments through order \(2q\).  If \(\nu_\varepsilon\) is supported in \([-R,R]\), then
\[
 \mu_\varepsilon(A)=\varepsilon Q(A)
 \quad\text{for every Borel }A\subset\mathbb R\setminus[-R,R].
\]
In particular, \(\mu_\varepsilon\) and \(Q\) have identical logarithmic tail asymptotics.
If \(Q\) has a strictly positive \(C^\infty\) density, then so does
\(\mu_\varepsilon\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["ferromagnetic pairwise interactions; the exponential-decay conclusion needs finite-range (or exponentially decaying) couplings, since G(x,y) >= tanh(beta J_xy) by Griffiths' inequality","finite volume, or an infinite-volume Gibbs state for which the relevant correlation inequalities (e.g. Griffiths inequalities) hold","existence of a family of finite sets separating the two points of interest","the model's symmetry, such as spin-flip Z_2 symmetry, used in the classical derivation of the inequality"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T12:13:53+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d393890b51a665689a58b52bbeacddfa45ba308a4e92ffc9e53fce0dc9def944","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For the Ising model, or more generally ferromagnetic spin systems with finite-range interactions (with merely summable long-range couplings G(x,y) >= tanh(beta J_xy) by Griffiths' inequality, so exponential decay can fail), let G(x,y) = <sigma_x sigma_y> be the two-point function. The Simon-Lieb inequality bounds G(x,y) across any finite set Lambda separating x from y (x in Lambda, y outside Lambda) by G(x,y) <= sum_{u in Lambda, v not in Lambda} G_Lambda(x,u) beta J_{uv} G(v,y), with G_Lambda the two-point function of the model restricted to Lambda (free boundary condition) and beta the inverse temperature (forms with tanh(beta J_{uv}) in place of beta J_{uv} are also used), a one-step recursive bound relating the two-point function across a separating surface to the two-point function up to the boundary of Lambda times the coupling crossing it. Iterating the inequality over a sequence of nested separating sets, such as concentric boxes, yields exponential decay of G(x,y) once the associated generating function drops below its self-consistency threshold, giving a classical route, predating and complementary to the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, to sharpness of the phase transition and analyticity of the free energy in the high-temperature regime. It does not determine the exact critical temperature directly, only characterizing it implicitly through the inequality's self-consistency condition, and it applies specifically to ferromagnetic spin systems with a workable notion of finite separating surfaces; it does not transfer automatically to percolation, which uses combinatorially different, though philosophically related, inequalities. Typical failure: Iterating the Simon-Lieb inequality across many nested separating surfaces while implicitly assuming a geometric decay rate that has not actually been verified to be summable; turning the one-step recursive bound into exponential decay requires checking that the relevant generating function, summing G times J over the boundary, lies strictly below its self-consistency threshold, and this check is exactly where the difficulty of locating beta_c resides, so skipping it silently assumes the conclusion. Canonical reference: Simon, 1980, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Lieb, 1980, Communications in Mathematical Physics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["a specified target distribution with a known, workable Stein characterizing operator or equation","an auxiliary coupling structure connecting to W, such as an exchangeable pair, a size-biased coupling, or a dependency graph","sufficient smoothness or explicit derivative bounds on the solution f of the Stein equation for the specific target distribution","control of the resulting expectation bound in terms of the coupling's own closeness or error parameters"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.996944+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d39aa2bb9e25135cdd42c23538dfcea568834d63bc2b2b834c74380b75fd1b82","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). To bound the distance, in Kolmogorov, Wasserstein, or total variation metric, between the law of a random variable W and a target distribution, classically the standard normal but also Poisson, exponential, and other targets, Stein's method characterizes the target law via a characterizing (Stein) equation: for the normal, E[f'(Z) - Zf(Z)] = 0 for all sufficiently smooth f if and only if Z is standard normal. Given a test function h, one solves the associated Stein equation f'(x) - xf(x) = h(x) - E[h(Z)] for f, and then bounds E[f'(W) - Wf(W)] directly using structural information about W, typically supplied by an auxiliary coupling such as an exchangeable pair, a size-biased coupling, or a dependency-graph/local-dependence construction, without going through characteristic functions or moment matching. This yields explicit, often near-optimal-rate, quantitative bounds on distributional distance for sums of dependent or weakly dependent random variables and for counts in combinatorial structures, settings where classical central limit theorem machinery is difficult to apply directly because of dependence. It does not automatically give a good bound for an arbitrary random variable, since constructing the right coupling matched to the problem's dependence structure is the substantive and typically hardest step, and the quality of the final bound is entirely determined by the quality of that coupling. Typical failure: Treating Stein's method as an automatic black box that produces a good rate on its own, when in fact the rate is entirely determined by the quality of the coupling constructed for the specific problem, such as an exchangeable pair with a large error term or a dependency graph with high maximum degree; a poorly constructed coupling yields a valid but far-from-optimal, or even useless, bound, and this construction step, rather than the abstract Stein equation itself, is where nearly all the technical difficulty and risk of error lies. Canonical reference: Stein, 1972, Proceedings of the Sixth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability; Chen, Goldstein and Shao, Normal Approximation by Stein's Method, 2011, Springer.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:19:42.675913+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3a2bf016f46a45c5a2e65e7fd09af9214a8f29ec66480713669aaa45f71ba3d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2609.03556, 'An Effective SPDE Model for a Schr\"odinger Equation with a Fluctuating Magnetic Potential'] \label[lemma]{lemma_ito_limit_martingales}
Let $v,v'\in H^1(\R^d)$ and $0\leq s\leq t\leq T$. Set
\begin{align*}
 a_k^v(r)&:=\langle \sigma_k\bar\psi_r,\nabla v\rangle,
 &b_{k,j}^v(r)&:=\langle (\sigma_k\cdot\sigma_j)\bar\psi_r,v\rangle,
 &c_{k}^v(r,r')&:=\langle A_r^n\cdot\sigma_k\bar{\psi}_{r'},v\rangle.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align}
    \langle\mathbb{E}\left[\Theta^n_t-\Theta^n_s\mid\mathcal{F}^n_s\right],v\rangle&=- \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau_n}}\int_s^t e^{-r/\tau_n}\langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle dr\notag\\ &- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{{\tau_n}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t \int_0^s e^{-(r-u)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r) dW^{k,n}_u dr,\\
        \langle\mathbb{E}\left[\Gamma^n_t-\Gamma^n_s\mid\mathcal{F}^n_s\right],v\rangle&=\int_s^t e^{-2r/\tau_{n}} \left\langle\frac{\wick{|A^n_0|^2}}{\sqrt{\tau_n}}\bar{\psi}_r,v\right\rangle dr\notag\\ & +\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I }\int_s^t\int_0^s e^{-2(r-u)/\tau_n} c_k^v(u,r) dW^{k,n}_u   dr,
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \left|\left\langle
   \mathbb E[\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n\mid\mathcal F_s^n],v
  \right\rangle\right|\right]
 &\lesssim \sqrt{\tau_n}\,
  \sup_{r\in[0,T]}\|\bar\psi_r\|\,\|v\|_{H^1},
 \\
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \left|\left\langle
   \mathbb E[\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n\mid\mathcal F_s^n],v
  \right\rangle\right|\right]
 &\lesssim \sqrt{\tau_n}\,
  \sup_{r\in[0,T]}\|\bar\psi_r\|\,\|v\|_{H^1}.
 
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]\notag\\
 &\qquad=\frac1{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}
  \int_s^t\!\!\int_s^t e^{-|r-r'|/\tau_n}
  a_k^v(r)a_k^{v'}(r')\,dr\,dr'
  +\rho_{s,t}^{1,n}(v,v'),\\
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]\notag\\
 &\qquad=\frac2{\tau_n}\sum_{k,j\in I}
  \int_s^t\!\!\int_s^t e^{-2|r-r'|/\tau_n}
  b_{k,j}^v(r)b_{k,j}^{v'}(r')\,dr\,dr'
  +\rho_{s,t}^{2,n}(v,v'),\\
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]
  =\rho_{s,t}^{3,n}(v,v'),
\end{align}
where
\begin{align*}
    \rho^{1,n}_{s,t}(v,v')&=\frac{1}{\tau_n}\int_s^t\int_s^t e^{-(r+r')/\tau_n} \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_{r'},\nabla v'\rangle dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-(r+r'-u)/\tau_n}\langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle a_k^{v'}(r') dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-(r+r'-u)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r) \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_{r'},\nabla v'\rangle  dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ &+\frac{2}{\tau_n^2}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^s \int_0^s e^{-(r+r'-u-u')/\tau_n}a_k^v(r)  a_k^{v'}(r') dW^{k,n}_u dW^{k',n}_{u'}dr dr'\\ & -\frac{1}{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t \int_s^t  e^{-(r+r'-2s)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r)a_k^{v'}(r') dr dr',
    \\ \rho^{2,n}_{s,t}(v,v')&=\frac{1}{\tau_n}\int_s^t\int_s^t e^{-2(r+r')/\tau_n} \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_r, v\rangle \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_{r'}, v'\rangle dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-2(r+r'-u)/\tau_n}\langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_r, v\rangle c_k^{v'}(u,r') dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-2(r+r'-u)/\tau_n} c_k^{v}(u,r) \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_{r'}, v'\rangle  dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ &+\frac{8}{\tau_n^2}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^s \int_0^s e^{-2(r+r'-u-u')/\tau_n} c_k^v(u,r) c_{k'}^{v'}(u',r') dW^{k,n}_u dW^{k',n}_{u'}dr dr'\\ & -\frac{2}{\tau_n}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t \int_s^t  e^{-2(r+r'-2s)/\tau_n} b_{k,k'}^v(r) b_{k,k'}^{v'}(r') dr dr'   \\
    \rho^{3,n}_{s,t}(v,v')&=-\frac{1}{\tau_n}\int_s^t\int_s^t e^{-(r+2r')/\tau_n} \langle A_0 \bar{\psi}_r, v\rangle \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_{r'}, v'\rangle dr dr'\\ & -\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f real analytic on an open set U in R^n","x solves the gradient flow x' = -grad f(x) on [0, infinity)","the trajectory has compact closure in U (precompact; bounded is enough when U = R^n)"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:12:37.001254+00:00","domain":"real-analytic gradient flows, optimization dynamics","id":"claim_d3b09a78eebe9d043b33f43006ca699084a5e2f256ecfc3a1bfc55dbccdda3be","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Lojasiewicz gradient inequality. Let U be an open subset of R^n, f: U -> R real analytic, and p in U. There are an open neighbourhood W of p in U and constants theta in (0,1) and c > 0 such that |f(x) - f(p)|^theta <= c |grad f(x)| for every x in W. Consequence (finite length and convergence of bounded gradient trajectories). Let x: [0, infinity) -> U solve x'(t) = -grad f(x(t)) and suppose the trajectory {x(t): t >= 0} has compact closure in U. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:54:15.645672+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3b9152418ee3e5cdc599366e866f02ab1900036e73e363714b9e9c83792bb9e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 98 (Evolution-family stochastic entrance and Galerkin stability) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $U(t,s)$ be a deterministic evolution family on a separable Hilbert space
$H$.  Let $N$ be a continuous square-integrable martingale on a Hilbert noise
space $U_0$, and let $K_s:U_0\to H$ be predictable.  For every terminal time
$t$ assume that $s\mapsto U(t,s)K_s$ is stochastically integrable and put
\[
 Z_r^{s\mid t}=\int_{(s,r]}U(t,a)K_a\,\mathrm dN_a,
 \qquad s\le r\le t.
\]
Assume locally in $t$ that the terminal-frame trace energies
\[
 \mathcal E_t^{(t)}
 =\operatorname{Tr}\langle\!\langle Z^{0\mid t}\rangle\!\rangle_t
\]
are finite.  Then the split degree-two increments
$\mathbf Z_{s,t}=(Z_t^{s\mid t},A_{s,t}^{(t)},Q_{s,t}^{(t)})$ are critical
entrances.  For a bounded spatial map $B$, write
$B_\#(x,A,Q)=(Bx,BAB^*,BQB^*)$.  With this convention they satisfy the
transported Chen law
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Z_{s,t}
 =U(t,u)_\#\mathbf Z_{s,u}\circ\mathbf Z_{u,t},
 \qquad s\le u\le t.
 
\end{equation}
Here the early increment is first constructed in the terminal $u$ frame and
then pushed to the terminal $t$ frame.

Let $K^{(m)}$ be finite-rank Galerkin approximants.  For a fixed terminal
$t$, if
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}
 \langle\!\langle
  Z^{K^{(m)}-K,\,0\mid t}
 \rangle\!\rangle_t\longrightarrow0,
 
\end{equation}
then the corresponding first levels, areas, and brackets converge ucp on
$[0,t]$ in the critical split topology.  The estimates are uniform over a
family of deterministic terminal frames whenever their energy and error
bounds are uniform.  Joint ucp convergence in the terminal parameter requires
an additional terminal-frame continuity or maximal estimate.  Adding an adapted finite-variation drift whose range on each compact
interval is contained in a deterministic finite-dimensional subspace of $H$
changes the area only by trace-class terms and preserves the entrance.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The uniform growth bound with constants M and omega, which every C_0-semigroup has by the uniform boundedness principle.","The renorming changes the geometry of the space - the new norm need not be, for instance, a Hilbert norm even if the original was, so any argument relying on inner-product structure must be checked rather than assumed to survive."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:06:45.871401+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, semigroup theory","id":"claim_d3dac9e684fa7cee76a6e64a5e95a24fd4a86841256053c866427af3587cab08","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (T(t)) be a C_0-semigroup on a Banach space X satisfying the growth bound ||T(t)|| <= M exp(omega t). Then there is an EQUIVALENT norm on X, namely |||x||| = sup over t >= 0 of exp(-omega t) ||T(t) x||, in which the semigroup satisfies |||T(t) x||| <= exp(omega t) |||x||| - that is, the constant M is normalised away and the semigroup becomes a quasi-contraction. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:41:29.024738+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3e2c77622f8024859707cc8bf75fa031012b848d26a17bad25860cbfb4c5410","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26490, 'Bayesian methods and Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms for curve reconstruction and poin'] For a fixed $n=1,\dots,N$, let $r_n$ be a random position generated according to the sampling scheme in \cref{eq:un,eq:sn,eq:pi,eq:L}. Then \cref{eq:rn} follows.
\begin{proof}
Given a geometry $G$, the position $r_n$ specifies and is specified by a global coordinate $v_n$ that equals the arc-length from $h^1$ along the curve $\mathcal{G}$ encoded by $G$. Consequently, it suffices to show that $v_n$ is uniformly distributed over $[0,L^G]$ where $L^G=\sum_{k=1}^K L_k^G$ is the total arc-length of $\mathcal{G}$.

Conditional on $s_n$ and $u_n$, such global coordinate $r_n$ is obtained deterministically by
\begin{align*}
v_n|s_n,u_n
&\sim\delta_{C^G_{s_n-1}+u_nL_{s_n}^G},
\end{align*}
where the cumulative segment lengths are defined by
\begin{align*}
C^G_0&=0,
\\
C^G_k&=\sum_{k'=1}^K L^G_{k'},
&
k&=1,\dots,K.
\end{align*}
According to the law of total probability, we obtain the marginal
\begin{align*}
p(v_n)
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
p(v_n|s_n,u_n)p(s_n,u_n),
\end{align*}
and, because of independence in \cref{eq:sn,eq:un}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
p(v_n)
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
p(v_n|s_n,u_n)p(s_n)p(u_n)
\\
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{C^G_{s_n-1}+u_nL_{s_n}^G}(v_n)\pi_{s_n}^G
\\
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\frac{1}{L_{s_n}^G}\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)\frac{L_{s_n}^G}{L^G}
\\
&=\frac{1}{L^G}
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)
\\
&=\frac{1}{L^G}
\end{align*}
indicating that, indeed, $v_n$ is uniformly distributed over $[0,L^G]$ which completes our proof. Here, the last equality holds because, from the $K$ different summands $\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)$, only one integrates over the singularity.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.375253+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3f32c57622f501a973e02951c88eed0f9ce246702496a185162ddc51105af59","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $T\colon (V,\|\cdot\|)\to (W,\|\cdot\|)$ be a linear map between vector spaces with diagonalizable norms.
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item Define an increasing $\bR$-filtration, $\cF^-(T)$, on $\operatorname{gr}V$ whose restriction to $(\operatorname{gr}V)_\alpha$ is 
        \[
        \left(\cF^-(T)_{\leq\beta}\right)_\alpha\coloneqq\left\{v\in (\operatorname{gr}V)_\alpha\mid\exists\text{ lift }\tilde{v}\in V:\|T\tilde{v}\|\leq e^{\alpha+\beta}\right\}.
        \]
        (Note the inequality can be written, for $v\neq 0$, as $\log(\|T\tilde v\|/\|\tilde v\|)\leq \beta$.)
        
        \item Define a decreasing $\bR$-filtration, $\cF^+(T)$, on $\operatorname{gr}W$ whose restriction to $(\operatorname{gr}W)_\alpha$ is 
        \[
     \left(\cF^+(T)_{\geq\beta}\right)_\alpha\coloneqq\left\{w\in (\operatorname{gr}W)_\alpha\mid\exists v\in V:Tv \text{ lifts }w,\|v\|\leq e^{\alpha-\beta}\right\}.
        \]
        (Note the inequality can be written, for $w\neq 0$, as $\log(\|Tv\|/\|v\|)\geq \beta$.)
        
        \item The \textbf{singular values}\footnote{They should really be called \textit{logarithms of singular values}, in analogy with the Archimedean case.} of $T$ are the numbers $\sigma_1\geq\ldots\geq \sigma_r$, $r=\operatorname{rk}T$, where the filtration $\cF^-(T)$ (equivalently: $\cF^+(T)$) jumps, where the multiplicity of the jump $\sigma_i$ in the descending list is  $\dim_\mathbf k\cF^-(T)_{\leq\sigma_i}/\cF^-(T)_{<\sigma_i}$.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:55:42.094718+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d3fb2c64e557b43deed33a846015af5640ab57829eaf42f21b12daa16d2d0247","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:dCoulomb of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] Consider the discrete Coulomb gas ensemble (equation eq:discreteCoulomb of the paper) under Assumption~(assumption:dCoulomb of the paper). Scale it around a bulk point $x^*$ as in (equation eq:corrkerneldiscrete of the paper) and let $\sigma$ be as in (equation eq:sigmadsine of the paper).

For any compactly supported continuous function $h:\mathbb{R}\to [0,+\infty)$, the limit
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal G_n^{\sigma_n}[h]=\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}[h],
\]

is valid, where $\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}$ and $\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma$ are the probability generating functionals of the discrete sine point process on $\Omega=\frac{\kappa_V(x^*)}{\rho(x^*)}\mathbb{Z}$ and its $\sigma$-deformation,

\[
\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}[h]\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}\sqrt h),\qquad \mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}[h]\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma\sqrt h),
\]
with

\[
\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \sqrt{1-\sigma}\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}(\mathsf{1}-\sigma\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}})^{-1}\sqrt{1-\sigma}.
\]

In particular, the deformed discrete Coulomb gas $\mathcal X_n^{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly as $n\to\infty$ to the deformed discrete sine point process $\mathcal X_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:55.642574+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d401a3cd427a7085cf62848e53807cfe68398c4334970a00a4c1b8b0218f8704","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 11 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(Y\) be a subordinator with L\'evy measure \(\nu\) and Laplace exponent \(\psi\).
Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(c\ge0\), and let \(K\) be a slowly varying function at \(\infty\).
Define
\[
h(x):=\frac{x^\alpha}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)K(x)}
\quad (x>0),
\]
and let \(g\) be the right-continuous inverse of \(h\), that is,
\[
g(\lambda):=\inf\{y\ge0 \mid h(y)>\lambda\}.
\]
Let \(Z^{(\alpha)}\) be the \(\alpha\)-stable subordinator characterized by
\[
E[e^{-qZ^{(\alpha)}_t}]=e^{-tq^\alpha}
\quad (q,t\ge0).
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\left(\frac{Y_{\lambda t}}{g(\lambda)}\right)_{t\ge0}
  \xrightarrow[\lambda\to\infty]{d}
  \bigl(c^{1/\alpha}Z^{(\alpha)}_t\bigr)_{t\ge0}\) on \(D([0,\infty),\bR)\).
  \item
  \(\nu(x,\infty)\sim c x^{-\alpha}K(x) \quad (x\to\infty)\).
  \item
  \(\psi(q)\sim c \Gamma(1-\alpha) q^\alpha K(1/q) \quad (q \to 0)\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

Let $X=(X_t)_{t\geq0}$ be a killed subordinator which is not identically zero. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label={\upshape (\arabic*)}]

\item The killing rate $a$ is zero, and the tail $\Pi((x,+\infty))$ of the L\'evy measure  is regularly varying at $+\infty$ with index $-\alpha$.

\item The Laplace exponent $\Phi:(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ (restricted over $(0,+\infty)$) is regularly varying at $0+$ with index $\alpha$. 

\item	
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to+\infty}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\bigg(\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s} \leq t\bigg)=\frac{\sin(\pi\alpha)}{\pi}\int_0^t x^{-1+\alpha}(1-x)^{-\alpha}\,dx$ for any $0\leq t\leq 1$.

\item 
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to+\infty} s^{-1}\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X_{T(s)-}]=\alpha$.

\item The law of $tX_{1/\Phi(t)}$ converges weakly to a stable law with index $\alpha$, as $t\to0+$. 

\item The distribution function $U([0,x])$ of the potential measure  is regularly varying at $+\infty$ with index $\alpha$.  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:55:42.109127+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d41882080b2749343036fd187567d18ddcb485e397c5f42ec97101ce99f62ddf","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:weakconvergence of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] Let $(\nu_n)$ be a sequence of finite Borel measures over a fixed Euclidean space $E$, converging weakly to a finite Borel measure $\nu$ on $E$ as $n\to\infty$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:32:56.100267+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_d418d5c7eb52ca818ca1e9c4347b8a9a10fdde559c2dab7d205f0e3ac6e5705f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $G$ be non-deterministic and $B>t_{0}(G)$. For any edge $e$ of the lattice, we define the \emph{detour height} as the distance to an edge with small passage time:
\[
k_B(e):=\min\left (k\ge 1 | \,  \min( \tau(e+(0,k)),\tau(e-(0,k)))< B\right).
\]
The \emph{detour} of $e$ is the path that starts at one edge of $e$, goes $k_B(e)$ edges upwards or downwards, passes the horizontal edge with weight less than $B$ and goes $k_B(e)$ edges down back to the other endpoint of $e$.  \e\!\left(\frac u2\lambda_m\right).
\]
For $h\in C_c(\R)$ set
\[
 \widehat h(s)=\int_\R h(u)\e(us/2)\,du.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \int_\R S_{1,X}(u)\overline{S_{2,X}(u)}h(u)\,du
 =\frac1X\sum_{m,n\in M}
 \psi_1\!\left(\frac{\lambda_m}{X}\right)
 \psi_2\!\left(\frac{\lambda_n}{X}\right)
 \widehat h(\lambda_m-\lambda_n).
\end{equation}
If $\lambda_m$ is a positive quadratic polynomial on a lattice coset, the
left side of \eqref{eq:theta-pair-identity}, with $v=X^{-1}$, is a finite
linear combination of integrals of products of the form
$\Theta_f\overline{\Theta_{f'}}(g_\alpha n(u)a(v))$.","status":"unverified"}
