{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.897970+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_df3e6ebb290d7b0f2ea7bfc5e4c3bc16082f28eb79826863386b3b49d7f365fc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \label[definition]{def:orders}
    Suppose that $G$ is an infinite graph such that a phase transition occurs at $\lambda^*>0$. 
    For $\lambda>0$ and a vertex $u$ of $G$, let $D_{G,u}(\lambda)$ be defined as 
    \[ D_{G,u}(\lambda) = \sup_{\mu,\nu}\left| \mu(u) - \nu(u) \right|, \]
    where the supremum is over all pairs of hard-core measures $\mu,\nu$ on $G$ at fugacity $\lambda$.
    Suppose also that for each vertex $u$, the one-sided limit from above $\ell_{G,u}(\lambda^*) = \lim_{\lambda\downarrow \lambda^*} D_{G,u}(\lambda)$ exists.
    
    If there exists a vertex $u\in V(G)$ such that $\ell_{G,u}(\lambda^*)>0$, then we say that $\lambda^*$ is a \emph{first-order} phase transition.
    If, on the other hand, $\ell_{G,u}(\lambda^*)=0$ for all $u\in V(G)$, then we say that $\lambda^*$ is a \emph{second-order} phase transition.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.689739+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_df843acee6adbfcb8ab5a15ff3e7f7276ed8bc1fb676aa8bf0382e1793e2809f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 108 (All-order generation from the least state) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $\tau=(\eta;\mathcal S_2,\mathcal S_1)$ be accessible, write
$\operatorname{ch}_\tau(z)=(x(z),A(z),q(z))$, and put
\[
 \mathsf Q_\eta
 :=C_0^{0,2\eta}\bigl([0,T];\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}\bigr)
\]
with its natural truncations.  The projective
families
\[
 \mathbf S^{S,\infty}:=(\mathbf S^{S,N})_{N\ge2},
 \qquad
 \mathbf S^{I,\infty}:=(\mathbf S^{I,N})_{N\ge2},
\]
endowed with the projective-limit topologies generated by their finite-degree
Hilbert-tensor projections, are stable-causal readouts of $Z_\tau$.

\textup{(i) Geometric quotient.}
Let $\pi_{\rm geom}(z):=(x(z),A(z))$, with the image topology and induced
truncations.  The geometric tower factors through $\pi_{\rm geom}$ and is a
lossless representation of precisely this quotient.  Its degree-one and
degree-two coordinates give the stable-causal decoder
\[
 x=\pi_1\mathbf S^{S,\infty},
 \qquad
 A=\Anti\pi_2\mathbf S^{S,\infty}.
\]
Consequently a causal source state $S$ realizes the geometric tower if and only
if $\pi_{\rm geom}(Z_\tau)\preceqsc S$.  The covariance path is not determined
by this tower.

\textup{(ii) Lossless augmented towers.}
For $\bullet\in\{S,I\}$, define
\[
 \mathcal T^\bullet(z)
 :=\bigl(\mathbf S^{\bullet,\infty}(z),q(z)\bigr)
\]
and equip its image with the topology inherited from the product of the
projective tower space and $\mathsf Q_\eta$.  Then $\mathcal T^\bullet$ is a
stable-causal homeomorphism onto its image.  A stable-causal decoder is
\[
 \mathcal D^\bullet(\mathbf s,q)
 :=\operatorname{ch}_\tau^{-1}
   \bigl(\pi_1\mathbf s,\Anti\pi_2\mathbf s,q\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D^\bullet\mathcal T^\bullet=I.
\]
Thus both augmented towers are lossless representations of the complete
state.

\textup{(iii) Algebraic recovery from the It\^o tower.}
The unaugmented It\^o tower determines $q$ algebraically through
\[
 q=x^{\otimes2}-\pi_2\mathbf S^{I,\infty}
   -\bigl(\pi_2\mathbf S^{I,\infty}\bigr)^*.
\]
In infinite dimension this formula does not in general define a continuous
decoder from the standard projective Hilbert-tensor topology to the
$\mathcal S_1$ state topology.  The explicit $q$ coordinate in
$\mathcal T^I$ retains this trace-class topology.  It may be omitted when the
declared covariance range has equivalent $\mathcal S_2$ and $\mathcal S_1$
topologies, in particular when $H$ is finite dimensional.

\textup{(iv) Least-state consequence.}
For every causal source state $S$ and either $\bullet\in\{S,I\}$,
\[
 S\text{ jointly realizes }\mathcal T^\bullet(Z_\tau)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 Z_\tau\preceqsc S.
\]
Hence $Z_\tau$ remains the unique least sufficient state for every response
program containing either augmented tower and whose remaining responses are
stable-causal readouts of $Z_\tau$.","status":"unverified"}

Associate to each bond $e\\in (\\mathbb Z^2)^*$, dual to some edge $(x,y)\\in\\mathbb Z^2$, the gradient $(\\nabla \\phi)_e := \\phi_x - \\phi_y$, where $x$ is taken to be the \\textsc{north} vertex if $(x,y)$ is vertical and the \\textsc{west} vertex if $(x,y)$ is horizontal. Call $e$ a \\emph{disagreement bond} of $\\phi$ if $(\\nabla\\phi)_e\\neq 0$. A \\emph{disagreement polymer}~$\\gamma$ is a (maximal) connected component of the disagreement bonds of $\\phi$. For such a polymer, let $D_i$ be the connected components of $V \\setminus \\gamma$. By construction, within each $D_i$, all the vertices that are $*$-adjacent to $V\\setminus D_i$ must have the same height $h_i$ in~$\\phi$. Hence, we can view each $\\gamma$ as a triple $(\\gamma, \\{D_i\\}, \\{h_i\\})$, and it makes sense to talk about the components $D_i$ of $\\gamma$ and their corresponding heights $h_i$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","a one-parameter family of unitaries or an exponential e^{itT} is being used","the continuity and self-adjointness hypotheses are the ones at issue"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.772569+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, spectral theory, quantum dynamics","id":"claim_df9328ea820c9b58103e280388d82cc43f63148f9a76b0b2e1fdd63f459b8d1b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: (i) U(t) is unitary for every t ∈ ℝ and satisfies the group law on all of ℝ; (ii) t ↦ U(t)x is continuous (weak continuity or, on a separable space, weak measurability suffices, but some regularity is required); (iii) the generator is self-adjoint. What fails. Without any continuity: pick a discontinuous additive function φ: ℝ → ℝ (a Hamel basis construction) and set H = ℂ, U(t) = e^{iφ(t)}. This is a one-parameter group of unitaries with U(0) = 1, but φ is non-measurable and unbounded on every interval, so U(t) is not of the form e^{ita} for any real a; no generator exists. Hence 'one-parameter unitary group' without a continuity hypothesis carries no spectral information. Overshooting in the other direction: if one assumes t ↦ U(t) is continuous in operator norm, then the generator is necessarily bounded, so norm continuity is the wrong hypothesis for Schrodinger evolutions, where A is unbounded. With a symmetric but not self-adjoint generator: on L²(0, ∞) the right translation semigroup (T(t)f)(x) = f(x − t) for x > t, 0 for x ≤ t, is a C_0-semigroup of isometries that is not a group (T(t) is not surjective), and its generator is A = −d/dx on {f ∈ H¹(0, ∞) : f(0) = 0}, i.e. A = −iS with S = −i d/dx closed and symmetric with deficiency indices (1, 0). There is no unitary group whose generator extends S, so exponentiating a symmetric operator to 'e^{itS}' is not legitimate: only self-adjointness (or essential self-adjointness followed by taking the closure) licenses the unitary group. Audit rule: in quantum dynamics arguments, check that the Hamiltonian has been shown self-adjoint on a stated domain before using e^{itH}, unitarity, conservation of norm, or invariance of D(H).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["M is a compact Riemannian manifold and f a C^1 diffeomorphism of M","mu is an f-invariant Borel probability measure (compactness makes the Oseledets integrability condition automatic)","the exponents, multiplicities and subspaces are measurable and f-invariant; constant a.e. when mu is ergodic","the Oseledets splitting is measurable, generally not continuous, and the Pesin blocks are not invariant"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:09:43.732600+00:00","domain":"smooth ergodic theory, Lyapunov exponents","id":"claim_dfb0e656c58d4f14dd665a85b8ce62d25a662a2455b987541fa0436ab64565e1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be a C^1 diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold M and mu an f-invariant Borel probability measure. Since M is compact, log of the norm of Df and of Df^{-1} are bounded, hence integrable, so Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem applies: for mu-a.e. x there are finitely many numbers lambda_1(x) > lambda_2(x) > ... > lambda_{k(x)}(x) (the LYAPUNOV EXPONENTS at x) and a Df-invariant splitting of the tangent space

  T_x M = E_1(x) + ... + E_{k(x)}(x),   Df_x E_i(x) = E_i(f x),

such that for every nonzero v in E_i(x) the limit of (1/n) log |Df^n_x v| as n -> +-infinity exists and equals lambda_i(x). The functions x -> lambda_i(x), the multiplicities dim E_i(x), and the subspaces are measurable and f-invariant; if mu is ergodic they are constant almost everywhere. The splitting is in general only MEASURABLE, not continuous, and the convergence is not uniform in x.

Two structural facts that every application uses. (1) TEMPEREDNESS: any measurable positive function that is subexponential along orbits -- such as the angle between the Oseledets subspaces, or the norm of the change to Lyapunov (adapted) coordinates -- can be chosen tempered, meaning (1/n) log of its value at f^n x tends to 0; this is what lets one build Lyapunov charts in which Df is uniformly contracting on the negative-exponent bundle at the cost of a chart size that shrinks subexponentially along the orbit. (2) PESIN BLOCKS: for each l one collects the points where the Oseledets estimates hold with uniform constants depending on l; the resulting sets Lambda_l are COMPACT (after discarding a null set and restricting the subbundles continuously), increase in l, exhaust a full-measure set, and carry uniform hyperbolic-like estimates. They are NOT f-invariant -- an orbit wanders between blocks -- which is exactly why non-uniformly hyperbolic statements are local-and-measurable rather than uniform.

A point x is called (non-uniformly) hyperbolic when no exponent at x is zero; the stable bundle E^s(x) is the sum of the E_i(x) with lambda_i(x) < 0 and the unstable bundle the sum of those with lambda_i(x) > 0. Zero exponents are the obstruction: nothing in this framework says anything about directions with zero exponent.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:30:52.738823+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_dfeae846fc728b813d8462c1bf3d183847b4171b9188dcd17a1e88853ae6fbfd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Geometric interpolation of two equivalent Gaussian measures on Hilbert space}]

		for $\alpha \in [0,1]$,

			(p_0p_1)^{G}_{\alpha}(x) = \frac{d\mu_{\alpha}}{d\mu_{*}},
			
			
		\end{align}
		where $\mu_{\alpha} = \Ncal(m_{\alpha}, C_{\alpha}) \in \Gauss(\Hcal,\mu_{*})$, $C_{\alpha} = C_{*}^{1/2}(I-S_{\alpha})C_{*}^{1/2}$, with
		\begin{align}
			S_{\alpha} &= I - [(1-\alpha)(I-S_0)^{-1} + \alpha (I-S_1)^{-1}]^{-1} \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{< I},
			
			\\
			C_{\alpha} &= C_{*}^{1/2} [(1-\alpha)(I-S_0)^{-1} + \alpha (I-S_1)^{-1}]^{-1}C_{*}^{1/2},
			
			\\
			m_{\alpha} &= m_{*} + C_{*}^{1/2}(I-S_{\alpha})[(1-\alpha)(I-S_0)^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_0 - m_{*}) 
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad + \alpha(I-S_1)^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_1 - m_{*})].
			
		\end{align}
	The normalizing factor is given by
	\begin{align}
		&Z_{\alpha}^G(p_0:p_1)
		\nonumber
		= 
		\int_{\Hcal}p_0^{1-\alpha}(x)p_1^{\alpha}(x) d\mu_{*}(x)
		\\
		&=\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}]^{-1/2}
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times \exp\left[-\frac{1-\alpha}{2}||(I-S_0)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_0 - m_{*})||^2\right]
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times 
		\exp\left[-\frac{\alpha}{2}||(I-S_1)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_1 - m_{*})||^2\right]
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times \exp\left(\frac{1}{2}||(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})||^2\right).
		
	\end{align}
		Here $I + A = (I-S_1)^{-1/2}(I-S_0)(I-S_1)^{-1/2} > 0$, with $A =(I-S_1)^{-1/2}(S_1-S_0)(I-S_1)^{-1/2} \in \Sym(\Hcal)\cap \HS(\Hcal).$

			\nonumber
			\\
			& \quad \times \exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\la C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*}), S_{\alpha}(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*})\ra \right\}
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad \times \exp(\la C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*}), (I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})\ra)
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad \times \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}||(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})||^2\right].
			
		\end{align}
Let $P_N = \sum_{k=1}^Ne_k \otimes e_k$, $N \in \Nbb$, be the orthogonal projection onto the $N$-dimensional subspace of $\Hcal$ spanned
by $\{e_k\}_{k=1}^N$, where $\{e_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ are the orthonormal eigenvectors of $C_{*}$.
In the expression in Eq.\eqref{equation:geometric-interpolation-Gaussian-S-Tr},
\begin{align}
	&\la C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*}), S_{\alpha}(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*})\ra 
	\nonumber
	\\
	& \doteq \lim_{N \approach \infty} \la C_{*}^{-1/2}P_N(x-m_{*}), S_{\alpha}(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}P_N(x-m_{*})\ra 
	\\
	&
	\la C_{*}^{-1/2}(x-m_{*}), (I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})\ra

	\\
	&\doteq \lim_{N \approach \infty} \la C_{*}^{-1/2}P_N(x-m_{*}), (I-S_{*})^{-1}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})\ra,

\end{align}
on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}  [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt
\item \textup{(}No $\pm$ distinction at fixed $h$\textup{)} For each $h \in \mathcal{H}$, 
\[
\mathbb{P}\{B^{h-}= B^{h+}\}=1.
\]
When $B^{h-}(\omega) = B^{h+}(\omega)$, call the common cocycle $B^h(\omega)$.
\item \textup{(}Forward measurable Busemann function\textup{)} For each $h\in \mathcal{H}, B^h \in \mathcal K_c^+$.
\item \textup{(}Mean $-h$\textup{)} For each $h \in \mathcal{H}$ and $i\in\{1,2\}$, $\mathbb{E}[B^h(0,e_i)] = -h \cdot e_i.$
\item \textup{(}Monotonicity\textup{)} For $h,h'\in \mathcal{H}$ with $h \cdot e_1 \leq h' \cdot e_1$, all $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and $\mathbb{P}$ almost every $\omega$
\[ 
    B^{h-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  B^{h+}(x,x+e_1) \geq  B^{h'-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  B^{h'-}(x,x+e_1)  
\]
and

    B^{h-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  B^{h+}(x,x+e_2) \leq  B^{h'-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  B^{h'-}(x,x+e_2).
\]
\item \textup{(}Left-/right-continuity\textup{)} For $\mathbb{P}$-almost all $\omega$, all $h\in \mathcal{H}$, and all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
B^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{\mathcal{H}\hspace{0.5pt}\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt} \hspace{0.5pt} h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \nearrow h \cdot e_1}} B^{h\pm}(x,y) \,\text{ and }\, B^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{\mathcal{H}\hspace{0.5pt}\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt} \hspace{0.5pt} h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \searrow h \cdot e_1}} B^{h\pm}(x,y).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, this process is unique in the sense that any two processes satisfying the above conditions are equal almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593474+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e01d5d09db42bfc35e775f7244f04d49e8975ab9c0242e8d9c0df1121448b943","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02743, 'Sharp mean-field estimates for diffusive log/Riesz gases in the Hilbert--Schmidt regime'] \\begingroup We study fixed-temperature logarithmic and Riesz gases after subtracting the leading mean-field contribution relative to a prescribed background law. For repulsive interactions in the Hilbert--Schmidt regime, we prove $N$-uniform bounds and quantitative convergence of the resulting modulated partition function to a normalization expressed by the Carleman--Fredholm determinant of the centered interaction operator. We show that the Hilbert--Schmidt threshold is sharp and obtain explicit lower bounds on the rate of divergence at and above it; these rates are expected to be nonoptimal. The proof combines positive-definite truncations and a low/high-frequency decomposition with exponential inequalities and Gaussian-chaos asymptotics for canonical degree-two $U$-statistics. As consequences, we establish entropic commutator estimates with the sharp $O(N^{-1})$ additive scale in the modulated-free-energy method, a static joint linear-statistics central limit theorem, and a dynamical central limit theorem for joint linear statistics at finitely many times. This extends the logarithmic partition-function estimates of the first two authors to the full Riesz Hilbert--Schmidt range and identifies the limiting determinant normalization. For the attractive logarithmic interaction at sufficiently small inverse temperature, we also prove analogous results. \\endgroup","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.976050+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0228a8876c77951bd23cfc70305cbadfb799fd70fa98dfc56f36d6b1b3550f2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 48 (Fock energy and free-capacity balance) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Assume in this theorem that \(M\) is continuous and that \(V_T\leq K\)
almost surely for a deterministic \(K<\infty\).  Let \(Z^\lambda\) and
\(Z^{\lambda,N}=P_{\leq N}Z^\lambda\) be the exterior lifts above, and put
\[
 T_t^N=Z_t^{\lambda,N}\otimes Z_t^{\lambda,N},
 \qquad T_t=Z_t^\lambda\otimes Z_t^\lambda.
\]
The finite-level bracket is \eqref{cc:eq-exterior-Fock-bracket}, and its
trace-class limit is the equality of positive
\(\mathcal S_1(\mathcal F_{\wedge}(H))\)-valued measures
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm d\langle Z^\lambda\rangle_t
 =\lambda^2\mathcal B_{\mathrm dR_t}(T_t).
 
\end{equation}
More explicitly, write
\(
 \mathrm dR_t=r_t\,\mathrm dV_t
\), where \(r_t\succeq0\) and
\(\operatorname{Tr}r_t=1\) for \(\mathrm dV\)-almost every \(t\), and set
\[
 Y_t=\|Z_t^\lambda\|^2,
 \qquad
 L_t=2\int_0^t
      \langle Z_s^\lambda,\mathrm dZ_s^\lambda\rangle.
\]
Then \(L\) is a real continuous local martingale and
\begin{align}
 \mathrm dY_t
 &=\mathrm dL_t
   +\lambda^2\operatorname{Cap}^{\mathrm{free}}_{r_t}(T_t)
      \,\mathrm dV_t \notag\\
 &=\mathrm dL_t
   +\lambda^2\left(
      Y_t-\operatorname{Tr}(\mathrm d\Gamma(r_t)T_t)
     \right)\mathrm dV_t,
 \\
 \mathrm d[L]_t
 &\leq4\lambda^2Y_t
   \operatorname{Cap}^{\mathrm{free}}_{r_t}(T_t)
   \,\mathrm dV_t.
 
\end{align}
Thus the predictable growth of Fock energy is exactly the free capacity;

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:28:49.056837+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e02df6e7008de2572a83edb0462c226bcad4b7a0dff7276dbd117a9e18dd763b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:first-order-interval-correspondence of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Suppose that Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) holds.  For every $\alpha\geq0$,
every regular weight $w$ of order $\alpha$, every interval $I=(r_0,r_1)$,
every integer $m\geq1$, and
\begin{equation*}
 F\in L_w^2(I;\mathbb R^m),\qquad \eta\in L^2(\mu_{r_1};\mathbb R^m),
\end{equation*}
there is a unique first-order occupation-energy solution in the sense of
Definition~(def:first-order-occupation-solution of the paper), denoted by
$\mathcal U_I^w(F,\eta)$.  In the following BSDE, $D_xu$ is the $m\times d$
Jacobian and
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf Z u:=(D_xu)\sigma\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}.
\end{equation*}
For $m=1$, its single row is identified with the column vector
$\sigma D_xu$ in (equation eq:reference-operators of the paper).  For every
$s\in(r_0,r_1)$, the composition of $u$ has a continuous version on
$[s,r_1]$ and
\begin{equation}
 u(t,X_t)=\eta(X_{r_1})+\int_t^{r_1}F(r,X_r)\,\mathrm d r
 -\int_t^{r_1}\mathsf Z u(r,X_r)\,\mathrm d W_r.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, for $\kappa\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 \kappa\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{w_\kappa;I}^2
 +\left\lVert \mathsf Z u\right\rVert_{w_\kappa;I}^2
 \leq e^{\operatorname{osc}_{\alpha,I}(w)}\left(
  \kappa^{-1}\left\lVert F\right\rVert_{w_\kappa;I}^2
  +w_\kappa(r_1)\norm\eta_{L^2(\mu_{r_1})}^2\right).
 
\end{equation}
The construction is independent of the weight: if the same data belong to
the spaces associated with two regular weights $w_1,w_2$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal U_I^{w_1}(F,\eta)=\mathcal U_I^{w_2}(F,\eta)
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(I\times\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^m).
 
\end{equation}
Thus the superscript may be omitted and the solution written as
$\mathcal U_I(F,\eta)$; the full-interval notation is $\mathcal U(F,\eta)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:06:39.320429+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0591a8f177295dd9b78ddf50bd06a308d4e4040b19920696ab99bffde067828","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:local_solutions_NSE of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Suppose that (equation eq:ass_caccioppoli1 of the paper) and (equation eq:ass_caccioppoli4 of the paper) are satisfied.

We say that $(v,\pi,(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n)$ is a local solution to (equation eq:turbulent_stokes_caccioppoli of the paper) if the following are satisfied.

v:I \times \Omega\to H^1(B;{\mathbb R}^d), \quad \pi:I \times \Omega\to L^2(B) \ \ \text{ and }\ \  (\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n:I \times \Omega\to H^1(B;\ell^2),

are progressively measurable, and a.s.,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:15:34.382573+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e05b89d0a5bff8dabc6ca1eec6c0a09d10cbafa8740552cc2e2e1d811913f672","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 5 (Theorem 3.1 in \cite{ZhangLiShangGuo2018}) of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Suppose $b\geq 0$, $c\geq 0$ and $\delta>-1$.     J_{b,c,\delta}(z,w)=\int_{\mathbb{B}_n}\frac{(1-|u|^2)^{\delta}}{|1-\langle z,u\rangle|^{b}|1-\langle w,u\rangle|^c}{\rm d}v(u),\quad z,w\in\mathbb{B}_n.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:55:18.060628+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e05b91a1c5270332be7572b9980f8499073e2f5c7e468d516e6039c7f73ed5ab","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.17381, 'Large deviation principle for friendship-biases\\ in Galton--Watson trees'] {\bf [Type characterisation lemma]}

Consider a Galton--Watson tree with the offspring law $(p_k)_{k\in\N_0}$ satisfying $p_1 =p\in (0,1)$ and $p_2= 1 -p$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm{(a)}] 
The root can only be either positive or neutral. It is neutral if and only if it is a branching point and its two children are branching-linear points.
\item[\rm{(b)}] 
A linear point is negative if and only if it is the child of the root and is not the parent of a branching point. It is positive if and only if it is the parent of a branching point and is not the child of the root.
\item[\rm{(c)}] 
A branching-linear point is neutral if and only if its parent is the root and its child is a linear point, otherwise, it is positive.
\item[\rm{(d)}] 
A branching point that is not the root is either negative or neutral. It is neutral if and only if its parent and both of its children are also non-root branching points.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.316467+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e06c9c1b22cc8ee294a21c9b44ee41ee097f09f666f1ef1955026596409609f2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition scalloped region of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] A \emph{scalloped region} is an open set \(U\subset P_{\varphi}\) satisfying following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The boundary \(\partial U\) consists of four biuinfinite families of leaves, \(l_{k}^{1,s},l_{k}^{2,s}\) in \(\mathcal{F}^{s}\) and \(l_{k}^{1,u},l_{k}^{2,u}\) in \(\mathcal{F}^{u}\), where \(k\in \mathbb{Z}\).
\item Each \(l_{k}^{i,s}\), \(i=1,2\), contains a fixed point \(p_{k}^{i,s}\) such that \(p_{k}^{1,s},p_{k}^{2,s}\)  are two corners of a lozenge, \(p_{k}^{1,s},p_{k}^{2,s}\) are two corners of a lozenge. The union of these lozenges is equal to \(U\).

\item The restriction of \(\mathcal{F}^{s/u}\) on \(U\) is product.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[  \left\langle E,\phi\right\rangle \left\langle E,\psi
\right\rangle \right]  =\sigma^{2}\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{0}^{3}}\frac{\chi
^{2}\left(  k\right)  }{\left\vert k\right\vert ^{2}}\left\langle
\frac{k\otimes k}{\left\vert k\right\vert ^{2}}\widehat{\phi}\left(  k\right)
,\overline{\widehat{\psi}\left(  k\right)  }\right\rangle
\end{equation}
with
\[
\chi\left(  k\right)  =\sqrt{\int_{0}^{\infty}\left\vert \widehat{\theta
_{\ell}^{T}}\left(  k\right)  \right\vert ^{2}f\left(  \ell\right)  d\ell},

{"assumptions":["(X,d) is a compact metric space","T: X -> X is a homeomorphism","T is expansive with expansive constant c > 0 for the metric d","alpha is a finite Borel partition with diam(A) < c for every A in alpha","for the cover statement, U is a finite open cover with mesh(U) < c","for the entropy consequence, mu is a T-invariant Borel probability measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.814532+00:00","domain":"topological and ergodic dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_e0991e6f5703dfafed9b8ef66c327d54b46c44f7e1c7b2d0847a9c270a85228d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and let T: X -> X be a homeomorphism which is EXPANSIVE with expansive constant c > 0, meaning: for every pair of distinct points x, y in X there exists an integer n with d(T^n x, T^n y) > c. Let alpha = {A_1, ..., A_k} be a finite Borel partition of X whose mesh is below the expansive constant, i.e. diam(A_i) < c for every i. CONCLUSION: alpha is a two-sided generator. Precisely, the smallest sigma-algebra containing T^{-n}(A_i) for all n in Z and all i is the full Borel sigma-algebra of X. Consequently, for EVERY T-invariant Borel probability measure mu, alpha is a generator mod mu, and the Kolmogorov-Sinai theorem gives h_mu(T) = h_mu(T, alpha) = lim_n (1/n) H_mu(alpha v T^{-1}alpha v ... v T^{-(n-1)}alpha): the measure-theoretic entropy is already computed by that one fixed finite partition, with no refinement over scales. TOPOLOGICAL COUNTERPART, same hypotheses: if U is a finite OPEN cover of X with mesh(U) < c, then h_top(T) = h_top(T, U); in particular an expansive homeomorphism of a compact metric space has finite topological entropy, and the entropy is reached at one fixed finite scale. SHARP EDGES. (a) Expansiveness is indispensable, not a convenience: for the identity map on [0,1] (which is not expansive) every finite partition alpha satisfies alpha v T^{-n}alpha = alpha for all n, so the generated sigma-algebra is the finite algebra generated by alpha and never the Borel sigma-algebra, however small the mesh. More generally, for a non-expansive system no bound on the mesh forces the generator property. (b) The constant c depends on the metric even though expansiveness itself does not: on a compact metric space expansiveness is independent of the choice of compatible metric, but 'mesh below c' must be read in the SAME metric for which c is an expansive constant. (c) The conclusion is about the TWO-SIDED sigma-algebra, using T^{-n} for all n in Z. For a one-sided generator (only n >= 0), which is what is needed for one-sided entropy statements and for non-invertible maps, one needs POSITIVE expansiveness (some n >= 0 with d(T^n x, T^n y) > c); a homeomorphism of an infinite compact metric space is never positively expansive, so that strengthening is not available here. (d) The theorem says the entropy is captured by alpha; it does NOT say h_mu(T) = H_mu(alpha) or that alpha is independent under T.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:38:36.830346+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0a65af24f67596daca271b5090e101206d886a00bd633a311924e7a3983a8a7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:master of arXiv:2606.28869, '\bfseries A General Theory of Paths:\\ \large Signatures, Jump Lifts, and Expected Signatu'] The constructions in the paper assemble into the following six-layer representation theorem, each layer being valid under the hypotheses stated in the cited results.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.25em]
\item \textbf{Algebraic path layer.} Bounded-variation signatures satisfy Chen multiplicativity and the shuffle identity; group-like signatures have Lie logarithms, and reduced bounded-variation paths are characterized by their signatures modulo tree-like equivalence.
\item \textbf{Jump and stream layer.} Finite-variation c\`adl\`ag{} paths admit forward It\^o{} and Marcus lifts. The forward lift fails shuffle by the jump bracket, while the Marcus correction restores geometricity. For pure-jump paths, the forward lift is the iterated-sums signature and the Marcus lift is Hoffman's exponential image.
\item \textbf{Geometricity-defect layer.} The two canonical failures of shuffle multiplicativity are second order: quadratic covariation for non-geometric conventions and coordinate covariance for expected signatures. Consequently, an expected signature is group-like only in the deterministic reduced-path case.
\item \textbf{Probabilistic and geometric layer.} Truncated signature kernels yield MMDs equal to Euclidean distances between truncated expected signatures, while the truncations of geometric signatures form a central tower of free nilpotent groups whose forgotten layers have Witt dimensions.
\item \textbf{Self-exciting layer.} Affine processes have finite linear closures for truncated expected signatures after state-weight augmentation. Scalar exponential Hawkes clocks admit the explicit systems (equation eq:hawkes-matrix of the paper) and (equation eq:A2 of the paper), local parameter recovery through (equation eq:ident-reconstruct of the paper), and a directional cross-area detecting two-channel excitation asymmetry to first order.
\item \textbf{Boundary and continuation layer.} Raw expected signatures have intrinsic heavy-tail moment thresholds, normalized expected signatures provide bounded characteristic replacements under the hypotheses of [chevyrev2022], reversal acts by the tensor antipode, and signature large deviations follow by contraction from rough-path large deviations.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

five-vertex cores
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:53:39.165864+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0cf0aae4f110b1bf6096c4a0fa9d899be0cbcfdf5524cc0fb1e74508ef9d983","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 7 (Coordinatewise equivariant endpoint prediction) of arXiv:2608.26961, 'Gromov--Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation'] Assume that \(G\subset\mathfrak S_D\) acts by coordinate permutations, where
\(g\cdot d\) is determined by \((gx)_{g\cdot d}=x_d\), and let
\(
\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_M\}~\subset~\R.
\)
Let \(\mu,\nu\in\mP_2(\R^D)\) be arbitrary, assume that \(\nu\) is supported
on \(\mathcal A^D\), and let \(\pi\in\mathrm{c}_{\R^D}(\mu,\nu)\). Then the
conditional coordinate probabilities \(q^{\ast,\pi^G,d}\) associated
with \(\pi^G\) admit a representative satisfying
\[
q_t^{\ast,\pi^G,g\cdot d}(n\mid gz)
=
q_t^{\ast,\pi^G,d}(n\mid z)
\]
for every \(t\in I\), \(g\in G\), \(d\in[D]\), \(n\in[M]\), and
\(z\in\R^D\), and minimize
\( J_\pi^{\rm coord}\) over all such equivariant coordinate
kernels:
\[
\bigl(q^{\ast,\pi^G,d}\bigr)_{d=1}^D
\in
\argmin_{\substack{q^d:I\times\R^D\to\Delta_M\ \mathrm{jointly\ Borel}\\
q_t^{g\cdot d}(n\mid gz)=q_t^d(n\mid z)}}
 J_\pi^{\rm coord}\bigl((q^d)_{d=1}^D\bigr).
\]
Writing \(\mu_t^G\coloneqq\pr^t_\sharp\pi^G\), for a.e.\ \(t<1\) and
\(\mu_t^G\)-a.e.\ \(z\),
\[
\bigl(v_t^{\pi^G}(z)\bigr)_d
=
\frac{1}{1-t}
\left(
\sum_{n=1}^M a_nq_t^{\ast,\pi^G,d}(n\mid z)-z_d

\]
In particular, this defines a \(G\)-equivariant representative of
\(v^{\pi^G}\), without requiring \(\mu\) or \(\nu\) to be

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:30:28.833348+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0ed456e7f08134808cf4300af917ed11213bf142f741b9f29c2b3417681c442","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 2 (Overlap profile) of arXiv:2609.02156, 'The higher-dimensional Shepp problem: an exact criterion for random ball coverings of tori'] For $0\le t\le2r$, define
\[
 u_r(t):=\mathcal L^d(B_{\R^d}(0,r)\cap B_{\R^d}(te_1,r))
       =\kappa_dr^d\psi_d(t/r).
\]
For $0<r<1/4$ and $z\in\T$,
\[
 m(B(0,r)\cap B(z,r))
 =\begin{cases}
   u_r(|z|),&|z|\le2r,\\
   0,&|z|>2r.
  \end{cases}
\]
Moreover,
\begin{align}
 \psi_d(x)
 &=\frac{2\kappa_{d-1}}{\kappa_d}

 &=-\frac{\kappa_{d-1}}{\kappa_d}

 \left(1-\frac{\kappa_{d-1}}{\kappa_d}x\right)_+
 &\le\psi_d(x)\le(1-x/2)_+.
 
\end{align}
Here $\psi_d(x):=0$ for $x\ge2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:46:36.165059+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e0f2f94beed90791c65604a7df83dd8e71e3c2b80b11263d5db5dd08942ed710","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Def_KosmannLift of arXiv:2609.02848, 'The universal moduli space of non-degenerate $\Z/2\Z$~harmonic spinors'] {Kosmann1972}[Proposition 17]{Bourguignon1992}}]
  
  For every ${\mathbf{p}} = (g;\gamma,\nabla) \in \mathbf{Dir}$ the \defined{Kosmann lift} is the tame linear map $\mathrm{lift}_{\mathbf{p}}^K \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace \mathrm{Vect}(X) \to \Lie(\widehat\mathscr{G}(S))$ defined by
  \begin{align*}
    \mathrm{lift}_{\mathbf{p}}^K(v)
    &\coloneq
      \mathrm{lift}_\nabla(v) + \kappa_v
      \quad\text{with} \\
    \kappa_v
    &\coloneq
      -\frac18 \sum_{i,j=1}^d g(\nabla_{e_i}v,e_j) [\gamma(e_i),\gamma(e_j)]
      \in
      \Gamma\paren{X,{\mathfrak o}(S)}.
      \qedhere
  \end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.356673+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e10d86a0e5ae172fc845f728151fa8a6f3e5bef5b0cd722074bd9020ffc74a17","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 235 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] There exists $C(\alpha) > 0$ such that for all $\fq\in [1,2)$ and any sequence of $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_N)_{N\ge 1}$, the following holds.
	For all sufficiently large $N$,
	\[
		\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu(\cA_N), \mu(\cA_{N[K]})\Big)
		\le \frac{C(\alpha)}{K^{2/\fq-1}}\,.
	\]
\begin{proof}
	Consider $N$ large enough that the conclusion of Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound} holds: this gives
	\[
	C(\alpha)
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l2} }{\ge}
	\|\mu(\cA_N)\|_{L^2}^2
	= \frac{\E[\|\fm\|^2]}{M}
	\ge \frac{\|\E\fm\|^2}{M}
	\ge \frac{|S_K(\cA_N)| K^2}{M}\,.
	\]	
We can thus couple $x\sim \mu(\cA_N)$ and $y\sim \mu(\cA_{N[K]})$ such that 
$\P(x\neq y) \le C(\alpha) / K^2$. It follows from  the first assertion of  Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound} that 
	\[
		\E[|x-y|^2]
		\le 2\E[x^2+y^2]
		= 2(\|\mu(\cA_N)\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\mu(\cA_{N[K]})\|_{L^2}^2)
		\stackrel{\eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l2}}{\le} 4C(\alpha)\,.\]
Applying H\"older's inequality then gives
	\begin{align*}
		&\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu(\cA_N), \mu(\cA_{N[K]})\Big)^\fq
		\le \E[|x-y|^\fq]
		\le \P(x\neq y)^{1-\fq/2} \E[|x-y|^2]^{\fq/2}
	\\
	&\qquad
		\le \bigg(\frac{C(\alpha)}{K^2}\bigg)^{1-\fq/2} (4C(\alpha))^{\fq/2}
		= \frac{2^\fq C(\alpha)}{K^{2-q}}
		\le \bigg(\frac{2\max\{1,C(\alpha)\}}{K^{2/\fq-1}}\bigg)^\fq\,.
	\end{align*}
	The result follows by renaming $2\max\{1,C(\alpha)\}$ to $C(\alpha)$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the optimism theorem for weighted least squares; weights normalised to sum to one","regime (2) beyond the Loewner bounds uses row exchangeability given the weights as a first-order approximation of the two moment matrices"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T11:47:28.060880+00:00","domain":"regression / model assessment","id":"claim_e133d7fdae691c4a0638ff9a8fb3a814a36acd27f937ccf5fa74ff1dd0aeeb11","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"In the setting of the optimism theorem for weighted least squares, normalise the weights to sum_i s_i = 1. (1) Uniform weights and homoscedastic errors give the Mallows-Efron optimism 2 sigma^2 m / n. (2) Concentrated weights with homoscedastic errors: the Loewner bounds s_min X'SX <= X'S^2 X <= s_max X'SX give 2 sigma^2 m s_min <= optimism <= 2 sigma^2 m s_max, and when the rows are exchangeable given the weights (E[x x'] = G for every row) the two moment matrices are (sum s_i) G and (sum s_i^2) G to first order, so the optimism is 2 sigma^2 m sum_i s_i^2 = 2 sigma^2 m / n_eff with Kish's n_eff = (sum s)^2 / sum s^2; relative to the noise level sigma^2 of the loss the gap is 2 m / n_eff, and a concentrated weighting behaves as a small sample. (3) Variance-stabilising weights s_i = c / sigma_i^2 (Aitken's weights) give S^2 Sigma = c S, the trace collapses to c m, the optimism is 2 c m whatever the concentration of the weights, and relative to the noise level c n of the loss it is 2 m / n again: under Aitken weights a small Kish n_eff is not a small sample but the balanced sample of the stabilised problem. Which regime a weighted fit is in is therefore an empirical question about how the error variance scales with the weights; an additive error floor sigma_i^2 = a + b/s_i mixes the two, the summand becoming s_i (a s_i + b), and the concentration re-enters through the floor on the heavily weighted rows.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:24:34.433144+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e13c4bb5b7b15fa4b295add3df7371dcb7e50fa4025db8d552613ef5d06903f2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] Let $\Psi \in C^1(\bG(N,m) , (0,\infty) )$ be a convex anisotropy with $\sup_{T \in \bG(N,m)} \|B_{\Psi}(T) - T \| < \ve_{N,m}$.
    Then, the following properties are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item There exists a constant $c(N,m,\Psi)>0$ such that every rectifiable $m$-varifold $V$ in $\bR^N$ with $\Theta^m( \|V\|,x) \geq \theta_0$ with anisotropic first variation locally in $L^p$ for $p>m$ satisfies $\Theta^m_* (\|V\|,x) \geq c \theta_0$ for every $x \in \textup{spt} \, \|V\|$.
    \item Let $V_i \rightharpoonup V$ be a converging sequence of rectifiable $m$-varifolds satisfying
    \[
    \Theta^m ( \|V_i \|, x) \geq \theta_0 > 0 \qquad \text{for } \; \|V_i\|\textup{-a.e.~} \; x
    \]
    and having locally uniformly bounded anisotropic mean curvature in $L^p$ for $p>m$.
    Then, $\textup{spt} \, \|V_i \| \to \textup{spt} \, \|V\|$ locally in the Hausdorff distance.
    In particular, the supports converge in the Hausdorff distance on $\bT^N$, or in $\bR^N$ if they are contained in a common compact set.
\end{enumerate}
Assume in addition that $\Psi$ satisfies the atomic condition.
Then the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item[(iii)] Let $V_i$ be rectifiable $m$-varifolds in $\bR^N$, or equivalently in the flat torus $\bT^N = \mathbb{R}^N / \mathbb{Z}^N$, with locally uniformly bounded anisotropic first variation and $\Theta^m ( \|V_i \|,x) \geq \theta_0>0$ for $\|V_i\|$-a.e.~$x$.
    If $V_i \rightharpoonup V$ as varifolds, then $V$ is rectifiable and $\Theta^m ( \|V\|,x) \geq \theta_0$ for $\|V\|$-a.e.~$x$.
    Equivalently, there is no sequence of rectifiable $m$-varifolds in $\bR^N$ with uniformly bounded anisotropic first variation that exhibit diffuse concentration.
    \item[(iv)] Allard's strong constancy lemma holds for anisotropic varifolds, cf.~\cite{allard-regularity}*{p.3} and~\cites{derosa-ghiraldin , dephilippis-rindler-a-free }.
    Namely, let $V_i \rightharpoonup V$ be a converging sequence of rectifiable $m$-varifolds in $\bR^N$ or $\bT^N$.
    For every $i$, let $\cD_i \subset (0,\infty)$ satisfy $\inf \cD_i > 0$ and consider Borel sets $E_i \subseteq \bR^N$ such that $\Theta^m ( \|V_i \|, x) \in \cD_i$ for $\|V_i\|$-a.e.~$x \not\in E_i$ and
    \[
    \|V_i \|(E_i \cap K) \to 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \textstyle \sup_i |\delta_{\Psi} V_i|(K) < \infty
    \]
    for every compact set $K$.
    For $\cD \subset (0,\infty)$, write $S(\cD)$ for the finite-sum set of $\cD \subseteq \bR$, i.e., 
    \[
    S(\cD) := \{ d_1 + \cdots + d_q : q \geq 1, \; d_1, \dots, d_q \in \cD \}.
    \]
    Then, after passing to a subsequence, for $\|V\|$-a.e.~$x$ there are values $v_i(x) \in S(\cD_i)$ such that $\Theta^m (\|V\|,x) = \lim_{i \to \infty} v_i(x)$.
    \item[(v)] The class of integer rectifiable $m$-varifolds in $\bR^N$ is closed under varifold convergence with locally uniformly bounded anisotropic first variation.
\end{enumerate}
All the above conclusions are local.
In particular, they hold for any non-autonomous anisotropy $\Psi(x,T)$ on $\bR^N$ and any anisotropic integrand on the Grassmannian bundle of a smooth $N$-manifold whenever the corresponding Theorem~\ref{thm:anisotropic-MS} is available on compact subsets. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:05:28.199224+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e14c5668d502ae92c05561f484c5320c8531d42370a18539837f875dba115e92","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm: pinning-1 of arXiv:2602.04429, 'Disordered systems and (subcritical) polynomial chaos\\ with heavy-tail disorder'] Assume that \( \alpha > 1-\frac{1}{\gamma} \) in Example~(ex:pinning of the paper) and that \(\beta_{\delta} \downarrow 0\) with \(\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \beta_{\delta} \delta^{\alpha-1+\frac{1}{\gamma}} = \hat \beta \in (0,\infty)\).
	Then, we have the following convergence in distribution for the disordered partition function
	\[
	Z_{\Omega_{\delta}}^{\omega,\beta_{\delta}} \xrightarrow[\ \delta\downarrow 0\ ]{ (d) } {\ensuremath{\mathcal Z}}_{\Omega}^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}} \,,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:35:10.793966+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e14e9bfbe2a49764f58470cb6fbe67e3df3743f29fabf836ad6bbb51d835b6e6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defin 31 (Level change, step up, step down) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\bs{\sg}_{N-1} \in \{ 0,1\}^{N-1}$.  One says that $\sigma_j$ with $j \in  \intn{1}{N-2}$
is a "level change" if $\sigma_j \neq \sigma_{j+1}$. Level changes come in two forms:

\begin{itemize}

\item "steps up" corresponding to $(\sigma_j, \sigma_{j+1}) = (0,1)$

\item "steps down" corresponding to $(\sigma_j, \sigma_{j+1}) = (1,0)$.

\end{itemize}

There is a natural identification $\bs{\sg}_{N-1} \mapsto \big(\sigma_1, X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \big)$
where $X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \subset \intn{1}{N-2}$ is the set of level changes.  That is, $\sigma_1$ is the first element in the sequence and

$$X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \,  = \, \big\{ j \in \intn{1}{N-2} \, : \,  \sigma_j \neq \sigma_{j+1} \big\} \, .$$

Note that one has the partitioning $X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \, = \,  X_\downarrow(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \cup X_{\uparrow}(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ where
$X_\downarrow(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ is the set of down steps and $X_{\uparrow}(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ is the set of up steps of $\bs{\sg}_{N-1}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:19:56.700051+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e158a26529489086a6fc99ab090f248350a3c5755295954738ed28b09bc2fbdf","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 31 (Local good approximations) of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $G_i$ be a sequence of locally compact Hausdorff local groups and $G$ a locally compact Hausdorff local group. We say a sequence of functions $\phi _ i : G_i \to G$ consists of \emph{local good approximations} if there are open, pre-compact, symmetric, multiplicative sets $A_i \subset G_i$, $A \subset G$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\Roman*${}_{\text{loc}}$]
        \item (Almost surjectivity) For all $U \subset A $ open nonempty, one has $\phi_i (A_i) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ for $i$ large enough.
        \item (No expansion) For all $V \subset G$ open with $\overline{A} \subset V$, one has $\phi_i (A_i) \subset V$ for $i$ large enough.
        \item (Almost homomorphism) For each identity neighborhood $U \subset G$, there is $i_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if $i \geq i_0 $ and   $g, h \in A_i ^8 $, then $ [ \phi_i (gh)^{-1} \phi _i (g) \phi_i (h) ]  \in U $. 
        \item (No compression) For each compact $K\subset A$, there is $i_0 \in \mathbb{N}$  such that if $i \geq i_0$, and $g \in A_i^8$ satisfies  $\phi_i (g) \in K $,  then $g \in A_i$. 
        \item (Almost continuity) For each identity neighborhood $U \subset G$, there is a sequence of identity neighborhoods $U_i \subset G_i$ with $\phi_i (U_i) \subset U $ for $i$ large enough. 
    \end{enumerate}
    If properties (I${}_{\text{loc}}$--V${}_{\text{loc}}$) hold, we call the sets $A_i$ and $ A$ \emph{regular neighborhoods} with respect to the approximations $\phi_i$. 

    \emph{Small subgroups} and the \emph{NSS property} in the context of local good approximations are defined in exactly the same way as they were defined for good approximations (see Definition \ref{def:ss2}).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.198217+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1755027b6b72bacceb84a2948a53af4813916207fa89947be3d5506f36530d0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the definition \eqref{e:bad.times.J}. 
If $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:levy.prohorov.derivs}, then  we have
	\[
	J^N\equiv
	J(p^N,\tep,\lambda)
		\subseteq 
		J\bigg(p,2\tep,\frac{\lambda}{2}\bigg)
	\equiv J
	\] for all $N$ large enough. 

\begin{proof}
The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. Define analogously the measure $\nu$ corresponding to the limiting function $p$.
The L\'evy--Prohorov convergence assumption implies that for all $N\ge N(\tep)$ we have
	\[
	\nu_N(A) \le \nu(A^{\tep})+\tep
	\]
where $A\subseteq[q_0,1]$ is any Borel set, and $A^{\tep}$ is the $\tep$-fattening of $A$. (The same inequality also holds with $\nu$ and $\nu_N$ exchanged.) It follows that
	\begin{align*}
	&-\Big[(p^N)'(t+\tep)-(p^N)'(t-\tep)\Big]
	= \nu_N([t-\tep,t+\tep])\\
	&\qquad\le \nu([t-2\tep,t+2\tep]) + \tep
	=-\Big[p'(t+2\tep)-p'(t-2\tep)\Big]+ \tep
	\le \frac{\lambda}{2}+\tep\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last bound holds provided $t\notin J$. Since $\tep\ll\lambda$ by Assumption~\ref{a:params}, this shows that if $t\notin J$ then $t\notin J^N$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.506242+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1a7d34e91f2f0976f773bd3135152e1bc9d3d8151c236c9717840a98f0ff0a8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 11 (Parseval-type identity and intrinsic reconstruction) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Assume that the family $\{\Psi_{j,k}\}_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$
is a Parseval $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-module frame, i.e.\ for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ one has the reconstruction
\begin{equation}
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\end{equation}
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ define
\[
C_{j,k}:=\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\in\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R}).
\]
Then:
\[
\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,
\langle \Psi_{j,k},f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
and
\[
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d} C_{j,k}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\]
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. In particular, the coefficient family $\{C_{j,k}\}$ uniquely determines $f$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:28:04.857968+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1a8c776afc11ed45db87d9b859fdde2be200552a6ed9c5288be5d9ddaaf5e66","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.20875, 'Double $q$-Wigner Chaos and the Fourth Moment'] Let $q\in[0,1)$, and let $m,n \in\N$ have opposite parities.  Let $H=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+)$.  For each $k\in\N$, let $f_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^m_+)\cong H^{\odot m}$ and $g_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n_+)\cong H^{\odot n}$ be fully symmetric functions, and let $X_k = I_q(f_k)$ and $Y_k=I_q(g_k)$ be the $q$-Wigner integrals in $\Gamma_q(H)$. Assume $\|f_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}$ and $\|g_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}$ converge and define
\[ \sigma_X = \lim_{k\to\infty}\|f_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)} \quad \& \quad \sigma_Y = \lim_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}. \]
Then the following three conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} \tau_q[(X_k+Y_k)^4] = (2+q^{m^2})\sigma_X^4 + (2+q^{n^2})\sigma_Y^4 + (4+2q^{mn})\sigma_X^2\sigma_Y^2}$.
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k \overset{p}{\frown} f_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(m-p)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,m-1$ and $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} g_k \overset{p}{\frown} g_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(n-q)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,n-1$.
    \item The sequence $(X_k+Y_k)_{k\in\N}$ converges in distribution to a mixed $Q$-Gaussian random variable with respect to the vector $[\sigma_X,\sigma_Y]$, where
    \[ Q = \begin{bmatrix} q^{m^2} & q^{mn} \\ q^{mn} & q^{n^2} \end{bmatrix}. \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.164974+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1ab87659c9828464b5b9edeaac9c25323ecc986248336539b1663089ed6c98c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 55 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] Let \(\nu\in M_{\chi,\sigma}(E)\) and consider:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
\(\nu=\nu_Z\) for some \(E\)-valued random element \(Z\).

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(h:E\to[0,\infty)\) such that
\[
L_h=1\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(f:E\to(0,\infty)\) such that
\[
0<K_f<\infty\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Conditions \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} are always equivalent.
If \(\rho\not\equiv1\), all three conditions are equivalent.

If \(\rho\equiv1\), condition \textup{(i)} holds if and only if
there is an \(h\) as in \textup{(ii)} satisfying
\[
\int_Eh(x)\,d\nu(x)=1.
\]
Whenever positive representing measures exist, they have a common
total mass, and a probability representing measure exists precisely
when this common mass is one.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.014408+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1b28c55a60eddf968566c36d8138741dc846c5c5595bfef0863ecc2aa17e999","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(U\subset Y^{\rm rv}\) be open.  We say that
\((\mathrm S)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and \(c_U>0\), independent

We say that \((\mathrm Q)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and
\(C_U<\infty\), with the same uniformity, such that
\begin{equation}

 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.148711+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1ba5cc6782dbe119dc23f6823d03dd94daf10ae75432259117f319071b13319","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.29361, 'Convergence of the subcritical $\gamma$-LQG metric to the critical $2$-LQG metric as $\gam'] Let $\mathcal{D}'(\CC)$ denote the space of distributions (generalized functions) on $\CC$, equipped with the standard weak topology. Fix $\xi>0$. A \textbf{(strong) LQG metric with parameter $\xi$} is a measurable function $h \rightarrow D_h$ from $\mathcal{D}'(\CC)$ to the space of lower semicontinuous metrics on $\CC$ such that the following hold whenever $h$ is a whole-plane GFF plus a continuous function on $\CC$.
    \begin{enumerate}[(I)]
        \item  
        \textbf{Length space.} A.s., $(\CC,D_h)$ is a length space.
        \item 
        \textbf{Locality.} Let $U \subseteq \CC$ be a deterministic open set. The $D_h$-internal metric $D_h(\cdot,\cdot ; U)$ is a.s. determined by $h|_U$.
        \item 
        \textbf{Weyl scaling.} For each continuous function $f : \CC \rightarrow \RR$, we define
        \begin{equation*}
            (e^{\xi f} \cdot D_h)(z,w):=\inf_{P : z \rightarrow w} \left\{\int_0^{\text{len}(P;D_h)} e^{\xi f(P(t))} dt \right\} \quad \text{for all} \quad z,w \in \CC,
        \end{equation*}
        where the infimum is over all $D_h$-rectifiable paths from $z$ to $w$ parameterized by $D_h$-length. Then, we have that $e^{\xi f} \cdot D_h = D_{h+f}$ for all continuous functions $f : \CC \rightarrow \RR$ a.s.
        \item 
        \textbf{Scale and translation invariance.} Let $Q$ be as in \eqref{eq:lfpp_normalizing_factor}. For each fixed and deterministic $r>0$ and $z \in \CC$, a.s.
        \begin{equation*}
            D_h(ru+z,rv+z) = D_{h(r \cdot +z)+Q \log r}(u,v) \quad \text{for all} \quad u,v \in \CC.
        \end{equation*}
        \item 
        \textbf{Finiteness.} Let $U \subseteq \CC$ be a deterministic, open, connected set and let $K_1, K_2 \subseteq U$ be disjoint, deterministic, compact, connected sets which are not singletons. Almost surely, $D_h(K_1,K_2 ; U) < \infty$.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:56:17.365327+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1bc1c93d17ac8382e28d7da3e397a756e3b42e7d640cc512f1f6b71d4e6d4b8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:sepstatdetcon of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] From two sequences $(X_j^{i})_{j\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$ with $X_j^{i} \in \{0,1,\ldots, j-1\}$, generate a paired tree sequence $(T_k^{1}, T_k^{2})_{k\geq 1}$, where the edges of $T_k^{i}$ are $\{\{j, X_j^{i}\}\}_{j=0}^k$.
    Fix a sequence of time steps $0<K_0<K_1<\cdots< K_\ell< m<n$, and assume  $(X_j^{1},X_{j}^{2})_{j\geq 1}$  are such that the following hold. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For all $j=0,\ldots, \ell$, the $K_j$ most central nodes of $(T_k^{i})_{k\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$, do not change after step $m$, meaning
        \[
        A_{K_j}^{i}(N) = A_{K_j}^{i}(m) \text{ for all } N \geq m, \, i=1,2, \, \text{and } j=0,\ldots, \ell.
        \]
        \item After time step $m$, the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}$ in each of the two trees has the following uniform bound
        \ba{
         \max_{j \in \{0,\ldots, \ell \}} \left| \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m)\right\} } \right| \leq \log(n)^{2/3}.
        }
         \item After time step $m$, the weighted sum of squares of the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}(m)$ in each of the two trees satisfies the bound
        \[

       \]
       for some fixed  $C>0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then
    \ban{
        \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} &\bbbclr{ \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{1}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{1}}(x) -  \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{2}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{2}}(x)  }^2
            \\
         &> C  - \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{2(m+1) \log(n)^{2/3} + (m+1)^2}{K_j}. \notag
    } (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Lebesgue measure on [0,1] for the counterexample","0 < p < 1"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.553704+00:00","domain":"real analysis, Lp spaces","id":"claim_e1f1d09dab661f59168150611995537e63e0f249b26c9ceb645e324eb84a1360","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For 0 < p < 1 the functional ||f||_p = (int |f|^p)^{1/p} is NOT a norm and the triangle inequality is false. Counterexample: on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure take f = 1_{[0,1/2]} and g = 1_{(1/2,1]}. Then ||f+g||_p = ||1_{[0,1]}||_p = 1, while ||f||_p + ||g||_p = 2 * (1/2)^{1/p} = 2^{1 - 1/p} < 1 for every p < 1 (e.g. 2^{-1} = 0.5 at p = 1/2). What survives: (i) the reverse inequality ||f+g||_p >= ||f||_p + ||g||_p for nonnegative f, g when 0 < p < 1; (ii) the quasi-triangle inequality ||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p); (iii) the p-th power is subadditive, int |f+g|^p <= int |f|^p + int |g|^p, so d(f,g) = ||f - g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric and L^p (0 < p < 1) is a complete metric topological vector space - but it is not locally convex on a nonatomic space, and its dual is {0}. Related trap: the generalized Hölder inequality with 1/r = sum 1/p_i remains valid for r < 1, but the TWO-exponent Hölder inequality with a negative conjugate exponent (0 < p < 1, q = p/(p-1) < 0) points the other way under the appropriate positivity and finiteness hypotheses, so the standard direction may not be quoted when p < 1.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.864288+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2069d1afb6f67b3701640a860faeb5ff84d4044d1c572cc42e53b268a42a291","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ of ranked tree shapes with $N$ leaves and $K$ internal nodes is in bijection with the space $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$ of $K\times K$ lower triangular matrices with non-negative integer entries that obey the
following constraints:
\begin{enumerate}[label={F\arabic*.}]
    \item The diagonal elements $F_{i,i}$ are strictly increasing: $F_{1,1}< F_{2,2}<...<F_{K,K}$ with $F_{K,K}=N$. The subdiagonal elements satisfy $F_{i+1,i} = F_{i,i}-1$ for all $i=1,...,K-1$.
    \item The elements $F_{i,1}, i=3,...,K$ in the first column satisfy \[ \max\{0, F_{i-1,1}- 1\} \leq F_{i,1} \leq F_{i-1,1}\] This just implies the column elements are decreasing by at most 1 if $F_{i-1,1}$ is non-zero. 
    \item All other elements $F_{i,j}, i=4,...,K, j=2,...,i-2$ satisfy these three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\alph*.}]

        \item $F_{i-1, j}-1 \leq F_{i,j} \leq F_{i-1, j}$: Column-wise change is either 1 or 0.
        \item $0\leq (F_{i-1, j} - F_{i,j}) - (F_{i-1, j-1}- F_{i,j-1}) \leq 1$: in any $2\times 2$ grid, sum of off-diagonal elements minus sum of on-diagonal elements is 1 or 0. 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.651647+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2081f0ae91205c715cd1ca304eefcc1ccfbf302567ce8bf25fd2909aa22a6b0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 21 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sR=(R,\alpha_R\colon N\to R)$ be as in \eqref{eq;SN} and write $\sR/p=(R/p,N)$. The restriction on the subcategory $\mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ of affine fine log-smooth algebras of Cartier type of the log-crystalline cohomology functor
      	\[
      	R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR) \colon \PreLog_{\sR/p} \to \mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p
      	\]
      	is the left Kan extension of its restriction to $\mathrm{lPoly}_{\sR/p}$. In particular, derived log crystalline cohomology and underived crystalline cohomology coincide for log smooth algebras of Cartier type.  
         Moreover, the algebra structure of $R\Gamma_{crys}(X/\sR)$ for $X\in \mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ is left Kan extended from that for polynomial objects. 
     	\begin{proof}This is basically well-known, and follows the same argument of the non-logarithmic counterpart. We give a proof for the convenience of the reader. 
      		Considering the restriction of $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to  polynomial pre-log algebras and the resulting left Kan extension, (here, we use the fact that $\mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p$ admits colimits)
      		we obtain a natural comparison map from derived log crystalline cohomology $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$. Both functors satisfy étale descent: this is clear for the underived version. As for derived log crystalline cohomology, it is enough to note that, since $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ takes value in $p$-complete $\sR$-modules, we can check descent by reduction modulo $p$. Since by construction derived log crystalline cohomology is obtained by Kan extension from polynomials pre-log algebras over $\sR/p$, on any such algebra 
      		$\sP$,  we can choose a polynomial algebra $\widetilde{\sP}$ over $\sR$ as its smooth lift. Then, the derived log crystalline cohomology $R\Gamma_{\text{crys}}(\sP/\sR)$ is exactly computed by the $p$-completion of $\omega_{\widetilde{\sP}/\sR}^{*}$ as \eqref{eq;omegalogcryscomparison}. 
      		Reducing modulo $p$ again, this is precisely $\omega_{\sP/(\sR/p)}^{*}$, thus $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)/p$ is $L\omega^*_{-/(\sR/p)}$, which satisfies étale descent. At this point, the claim of the Lemma follows again from the fact that         for log smooth pre-log algebras $\sA$ of Cartier type over $\sR/p$,
      		the comparison map 
      		$L\omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}\to \omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}$ is an equivalence (see for example \cite[Proposition 4.6]{BLPO-HKR}).
            Finally, the last statement follows from Remark \ref{rmk;multiplicativity}). 
                 	\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.299975+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e24889e4fd5825bc288daedce508a877706cdda9e02cf792d8e1985c8e632777","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 14 (Aligned anisotropic Gaussian allocation) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$, where
\[
\Sigma=V\diag(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)V^\top,
\qquad \lambda_i>0.
\]
Let $A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$ have full row rank and suppose the measurement
is aligned with the prior eigenbasis,
\[
A=U\begin{bmatrix}\diag(s_1,\ldots,s_{d_y})&0\end{bmatrix}V^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma=\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y},
\]
with $s_i=0$ for $i>d_y$.  Define
\begin{equation}

B_{i,t}=a_t^2\lambda_i+\Delta_t,
\qquad
v_{i,t}=\frac{\lambda_i\Delta_t}{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\tau_i^2=\left(\lambda_i^{-1}+s_i^2/\sigma_y^2\right)^{-1},
\qquad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=a_t^2\tau_i^2+\Delta_t,
\end{equation}
where $\tau_i^2=\lambda_i$ when $s_i=0$.  Under the joint law of $(X_t,R)$,
\begin{equation}

\E|s_{t,i}^{\rm prior}(X_t)|^2=\frac1{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\E|g_{t,i}(X_t,R)|^2
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}^2(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)}
=
\frac{B_{i,t}}{\widetilde B_{i,t}}-1.
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item As $a_t\to0$,
\[
\rho_i(t)=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}{s_i^2\lambda_i+\sigma_y^2}+O(a_t^4).
\]
\item For $s_i>0$, $\rho_i(t)$ is strictly increasing along the reverse
trajectory, with low-noise limit $s_i^2\lambda_i/\sigma_y^2$, and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=\frac12B_{i,t}.
\end{equation}
Thus, within this aligned linear-Gaussian model, $\rho_i=1$ is a
variance-halving, equal-Fisher-energy reference level.  It is crossed at a
unique interior noise level iff $s_i^2\lambda_i>\sigma_y^2$; when
$s_i^2\lambda_i=\sigma_y^2$, it is attained only at the clean endpoint.
\item Since the exact force is null on unmeasured aligned coordinates,
\begin{equation}

\rho_t^{\rm global}=\omega_t\rho_t^{\rm row},
\qquad
\omega_t=
\frac{\sum_{i:s_i>0}B_{i,t}^{-1}}{\sum_{i=1}^dB_{i,t}^{-1}}.
\end{equation}
For an isotropic prior, $\omega_t=d_y/d$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Y. Shmalo, Correlation of leaf heights at mesoscopic separation in the critical beta-splitting tree (October 2026). In the critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, closed into a cycle, take a uniformly random leaf and the leaf r places further round the cycle. Aldous and Janson (The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, arXiv:2303.02529, Section 3.9, Open Problem 1) asked for a proof that the correlation of the two leaf heights tends to 1 - alpha when log r_n / log n tends to alpha in [0, 1]. The paper proves that, uniformly in 1 <= r <= n/2, the covariance of the two heights is sigma^2 log(n/r) + O(sqrt(log n)) and the variance of one height is sigma^2 log n + O(sqrt(log n)), with sigma^2 = 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^3, so the correlation equals 1 - log r / log n + O((log n)^(-1/2)). The proof uses a potential of each leaf's position in its clade that decreases at rate zeta(2) up to square-integrable errors, and compares the two martingales it produces up to the cut that separates the two leaves. Exact rational checks, a Monte Carlo simulation and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation (commit e337fd88d00f). Not refereed.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:45:01.899018+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e25cf4f546bd223fd5788f3c0c2ce12c7c0495999a782eb032a5b2e26609f170","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $X_n$ be a discrete Markov chain on $\mathbb{N}$, with transition probabilities
    \[
    \mathbb{P}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+1} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]
    We say that $X_n$ is a birth-death chain if its transition probabilities $\mathbb{P}_{ij}$ is tridiagonal; that is, 
    \[
    P_{ij} = 0, \text{if} \quad |i-j|>1.
    \]
    In this case, the nonzero entries are given by $P_{i,i} = r_i, P_{i,i+1} = p_i, P_{i,i-1} = q_i$. We also define the m step transition probabilities,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}^{m}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+m} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:04.996916+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e25e0282b335a6653daee5319699acd7b83cece7214931f9dce26c2e161bebfd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 48 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\FF,\mu)$ be a measure space. The integral enjoys the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Additivity: $\mu[ f+g ]=\mu[f]+\mu[g]$ whenever $\{f,g\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $\mu[f^-]\lor \mu[g^-]<\infty$.
			\item Integral of indicator: $\int \mathbbm{1}_A\dd \mu=\mu(A)$ for all $A\in \FF$ (in particular $\int 0\dd \mu=0$, hence $\int f\dd\mu=\int f^+\dd\mu-\int f^-\dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$). 
			\item Integrals vanishing, integrals finite: For $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[0,\infty]}$, $\int f\dd \mu=0$ iff $f=0$ a.e.-$\mu$, while $\int f\dd \mu<\infty$ implies that $f<\infty$ a.e.-$\mu$.  
			\item Triangle inequality: $\vert \int f\dd\mu\vert\leq \int \vert f\vert \dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$.
			\item Measure zero sets are ``invisible'': $\int f\dd\mu=\int g\dd \mu$ whenever $\{f,g\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $f=g$ a.e.-$\mu$. 
					\item  Monotonicity: $\int g\dd\mu\leq\int f\dd \mu$ whenever  $\{g,f\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, $g\leq f$ and $\int g^-\dd\mu <\infty$.
			\item Homogeneity: $\int cf\dd\mu=c\int f\dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ for which $\int (cf)^-\dd \mu\land \int (cf)^+\dd\mu<\infty$,  for all $c\in [-\infty,\infty]$.	
		\end{enumerate}
		Furthermore, the integrals appearing in  \eqref{lebesgue:additivity}-\eqref{properties:indicator}-\eqref{properties:v} \& \eqref{properties:iii} are all well-defined. The same is true for \eqref{properties:ii} except  when $c=0$  and $\mu[f^+]= \mu[f^-]=\infty$. Finally, in \eqref{properties:vi}, $\int f\dd\mu$ is well-defined iff $\int g\dd\mu$ is well-defined. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.179516+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2625d957dbeafa21c7d1caca97d4ada8270ebbc0476643f8dc29e54931a3975","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 93 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have
\begin{align*}
\sM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,,\\
\sM^{\sideal,\sym}(\alpha,0) &\subseteq \sM^{\sx,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym} for the first assertion: 
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\GREATdefn{sy}\\
\SPRdefn{sy}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The $\svi$ and $\svii$ classes
 differ only in the constraint on $p$: the $\svi$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6} (i.e. $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, among other conditions) while the $\svii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7} (i.e. $p\equiv 1$). Consider any
	\[\mu = \mu^\sym(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0)
	 \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,,\]
corresponding to controls
	\[(q_*=0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) \in \Adm^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,.\]
In particular, $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}.
Recall the notation of Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}: 
we have $(b,\sigma) \in \Adm(0;p,f)$
for budget function $f(t) = (\bbE w_t)^2 / \alpha$, so
    \[
        \acute\mu = \mu(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0) \in \cM(0;p,f)\,.
    \]
Note that $\mu = \sym(\acute\mu)$.
Now consider the functions $\tilde p, \hat p \in \incr([0,1];[0,1])$ given by $\tilde p \equiv 1$ and
    \[
        \hat p(t) = \begin{cases}
            p(\epsilon) & t\in [0,\epsilon) \,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [\epsilon,1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    Since the restrictions of $p$ and $\hat p$ to $[\epsilon,1]$ agree, Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p.near.0} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;p,f),\cM(0;\hat p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(9(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,,
    \eeq
    for $\cM(0;p,f)$ specified in Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}, we have $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, and so
    \[
        \|\hat p' - \tilde p'\|_1
        =\|\hat p' \|_1 
        = \hat p(1) - \hat p(\epsilon)
        = p(1) - p(\epsilon)
        \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
    Then Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;\hat p,f),\cM(0;\tilde p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(6(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
    For some $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon)$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff1} and \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff2} imply the existence of $\tilde \mu \in \cM(0;\tilde p,f)$ such that

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:50:44.859485+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2653505b5e58787e96ef89c3576115a7583b9ee5f40884e291ff263333c16c7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 (Non-stationary case) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \( \bm{X} \) be a continuous centered Gaussian process satisfying
  assumptions~\ref{D1}--\,\ref{D3}, let \( \Gamma \) satisfy

  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item If \( \alpha < \beta \) and Assumptions~\ref{B3}--\ref{B4} hold on
    every interval \([0,S]\), \(S\ge0\), for the limiting model
    \[
      \bm Z=\bm Y_{\alpha,V_{I,I}},

      }

      \mathcal{H}_{\Gamma, L, \alpha, V_{I, I}, \Sigma, \bm{b}} \, 
      \Gamma ( 1 / \beta + 1 ) \,
      \tau_{\bm{w}}^{-1 / \beta} \,
      u^{2 / \alpha - 2 / \beta - |I|} \, 
      \varphi_{\Sigma} ( u \bb ),

    where \( \tau_{\bm{w}} = \bm{w}^\top A \bm{w} \).
    \item If \( \alpha = \beta \), \(\bm d(t)=t^\beta A\bm w\), and
    Assumptions~\ref{B3}--\ref{B4} hold on every interval \([0,S]\), \(S\ge0\),
    for the limiting model
    \[
      \bm Z=\bm Y_{\alpha,V_{I,I}},
      \qquad
      \bm q(t)=S_{\alpha,V_{I,I}}(t)\bm w_I+\bm d_I(t),
    \]

    then with \( L_u = L \cdot u^{-2 \lambda_\Gamma / \beta} \) we have
    \begin{equation*}
      \pk{
        \Gamma_{[0, T]} ( \uu ( \bm{X} - u \bm{b} ) ) > L_u
      }
      \sim

    where

      \mathcal{C}_{\Gamma, L, \bm d, \Sigma, \bm{b}}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:31.970547+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e27a55c2fa1bbf0ef450ed2a3f87000565c4c962e36680301a921ab1c0f61f59","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[1 16 of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Let ${\cal A}=[a_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}] \in \mathbb R^{u \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $w \le n$, be an $m$th order tensor and ${\cal E} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ be an $m$th order tensor of all ones. Then, ${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ is an $m$th order tensor such that 
$${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}=\left[\sum_{j=1}^u a_{ji_2\ldots i_m}\right],$$
i.e., it effects a summation operation over the first index of $\cal A$. In particular, for an $m$th order identity tensor ${\cal I} \in \mathbb R^{u \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $u \le n$, 
\be

{\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal I}={\cal E}.
\ee
Moreover, if ${\cal B} \in \mathbb R^{w \times v \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $v \le n$, is an $m$th order tensor too, then 
\be

({\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}) \boxtimes {\cal B}={\cal E} \boxtimes ({\cal A} \boxtimes {\cal B}),
\ee
i.e., there is associativity for such a special case of $\boxtimes$ multiplication. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a Hilbert space","a is bounded sesquilinear on H × H","the claimed coercivity constant α > 0 must hold on all of H"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.772311+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, elliptic PDE, finite element analysis","id":"claim_e2aa108ac361aa69126eca86591b9d8beaedd4bc7bdd886699f31c317c3ce026","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: Re a(u, u) ≥ α‖u‖² for all u in the Hilbert space H, with a fixed α > 0 and the norm of H itself (the trial and test space). What fails: strict positivity a(u, u) > 0 for u ≠ 0, or injectivity of the associated operator, is not enough - the solution operator need not be bounded and the problem need not be solvable. Counterexample 1: H = ℓ², a(u, v) = Σ_{n ≥ 1} n^{-1} u_n conj(v_n). Then a is bounded (C = 1), Hermitian, and a(u, u) > 0 for every u ≠ 0, but the associated operator is the injective compact diagonal operator with entries 1/n, whose range is not closed. For f = (1/n)_n ∈ ℓ², the equation a(u, v) = ⟨f, v⟩ for all v forces u_n = 1 for all n, which is not in ℓ²: no solution exists. Counterexample 2 (the practical one): on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω, a(u, v) = ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v̄ on H = H¹(Ω) is bounded and positive semidefinite but not coercive, since a(1, 1) = 0; the Neumann problem −Δu = f, ∂_ν u = 0 is solvable only under the compatibility condition ∫_Ω f = 0, and is never uniquely solvable in H¹(Ω) (constants can be added). Coercivity is recovered only on the subspace {u ∈ H¹(Ω) : ∫_Ω u = 0} via the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality; on H_0^1(Ω) it is recovered via the Poincaré inequality, which is why the Dirichlet problem is the easy case. Other silent hypotheses: H must be complete (a coercive bounded form on a dense non-closed subspace gives no existence), and the coercivity constant α must be uniform, not depending on u. Note a is not assumed symmetric - that part is genuinely unnecessary. For non-coercive but well-posed problems (e.g. mixed or saddle point formulations, convection dominated problems, different trial and test spaces), the correct replacement is the Banach-Necas-Babuska inf-sup theorem: an inf-sup condition on a plus injectivity of the adjoint form, of which coercivity is only a sufficient condition.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:44:28.011274+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2ab19483bdad4ec5a450f66847c9d0b226843208191aae1ff63beccdde21247","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 (Weighted Besov spaces \cite{HZZZ22}) of arXiv:2607.13379, 'Quantitative Propagation of Chaos and Fluctuations for Kinetic McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Si'] For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and $p,q\in[1,\infty]$, define
\begin{align*}

\end{align*}
with the usual modification when $q=\infty$.
Moreover, for $\ell\in\mR$, we also define weighted Besov spaces with the norm
$$
    \|f\|_{\bB^{\alpha,q}_{p;a,\ell}}
    :=
    \|\langle z\rangle^{\ell}f\|_{\bB^{\alpha,q}_{p;a}},
    \qquad
    \langle z\rangle=(1+|z|^2)^{1/2}.
$$
For $p=q=\infty$, we write
$$
\bC^\alpha_a:=\bB^{\alpha,\infty}_{\infty;a}.
$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:56:36.582358+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2bb660e615c6f7a5f27b5b1d7e69afb5738933d751537b9fbffe9f6dbbc0342","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Thm 1.2 of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a semi-finite atomless von Neumann algebra and let $E$ be a symmetric function space on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$. \item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is $\sigma$-finite and $E$ is KB, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$.
\item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is non-$\sigma$-finite, $E$ is KB, and $E\cap L_\infty\neq L_1\cap L_\infty$, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\infty)$.
\item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is non-$\sigma$-finite and $E$ is uniformly monotone, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\infty)$.
\item If $\tau(\mathbf{1})<\infty$ and $E$ is KB, then $E=L_1$ on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$, up to equivalence of norms.
