{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.095016+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2bdc304174e9fecc0b830e21a47837cec922f95e7efd160273f5cec30664a8e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:paired-resource of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] A safe gate and its $C$-degree are as in
(def:circuit-primitives of the paper); the amplified estimate is proved in
(lem:safe of the paper).

For an active eigenframe of an arbitrary self-adjoint pure-Weyl $C$, put
\[
 (F_Cx)_a=\lambda_aA_a^Tx,
 \qquad
 F_C^*F_C=Q_2:=-\sum_a\lambda_a^2A_a^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.1}
\]
A concrete carrier for these two fronts is obtained as follows.  Let
$E_C=\ell^2(I_C)$ be the active label space,
$J_C:E_C\to\Lambda^2H$ the isometry $J_Ce_a=A_a$, and
\[
 \iota_\wedge A=2^{-1/2}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}e_i\otimes e_j,
 \qquad
 \mathsf W_C=(\iota_\wedge J_C)\otimes I_H,
\]
and define the one-hole column
\[
 (T_Cx)_{ijk}=\sum_\ell C_{ij,k\ell}x_\ell.
\tag{2.2.2}
\]
With the ordered-pair convention
$C_{ij,k\ell}=\sum_a\lambda_a(A_a)_{ij}(A_a)_{k\ell}$,
one has the exact typed identity
\[
 \mathsf W_CF_C=-2^{-1/2}T_C,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}
 :=\mathsf W_CF_CF_C^*\mathsf W_C^*
 =\frac12T_CT_C^*.
\tag{2.2.3}
\]
Thus the open token is a specified three-strand operator, up to the signed
leg permutations recorded by its port state; it is not defined merely by
having a prescribed scalar cap.  Moreover
\[
 T_C^*T_C=2Q_2,
 \qquad
 T_C=P_{[2,1]_0}T_C,
\tag{2.2.4}
\]
where $P_{[2,1]_0}$ is the trace-free hook projection on the first three
indices.

A paired-front atom contains the two correlated Hilbert--Schmidt fronts
of this single $F_C$ pair, equivalently the concrete hole
$\mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}$ in (eq:2.2.3 of the paper), any safe left and right gates, and
an untouched typed ancillary boundary $E$.  Let $\mathfrak M_C^{\rm alg}(E)$ be
the algebraic span of these atoms.  Its projective norm is the infimum,
over all atomic presentations, of the sum of the products of the two
front Hilbert--Schmidt norms and all safe-gate operator-norm bounds.  The
completion is denoted $\mathfrak M_C(E)$.  Its distinguished token
$\mathfrak q_C$ satisfies
\[
 \|\mathfrak q_C\|_{\mathfrak M_C}\le\operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.5}
\]
The two fronts form one resource: they may move or fuse but are never
duplicated.  Equality in (eq:2.2.5 of the paper) is not asserted, and the cap identity
does not identify this open pair with a differently typed polar pair.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:02:38.603589+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2e17396d5335b779d847393a74c508630ceae7b72b56dfb3bf4645cb02c0998","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2607.07552, 'Weak convergence rate for the Cox--Ingersoll--Ross process'] Consider the implicit scheme defined by~\eqref{eq:BEMscheme} with $2\alpha\geq\theta^2$. Then
	\begin{equation}
		
		d\hat{X}_t={\sigma(\hat{X}_t)\over F(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)}dW_t+{\sigma^2(\hat{X}_t)\over F^2(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)}\left[g(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)+{b(\hat{X}_t)\over \sigma^2(\hat{X}_t)}\right]dt,\quad t\in(t_n,t_{n+1}],
	\end{equation}
	where $\sigma:\mathbb{R}_{+}\to\mathbb{R}_{+}$, $\sigma(x)=\theta\sqrt{x}$, $b:\mathbb{R}_{+}\to\mathbb{R}$, $b(x)=\alpha-kx$, and
	\begin{align}
		& F(x,t;t_n)=1+{k\over 2}(t-t_n)+{(4\alpha-\theta^2)(t-t_n)\over 8x}, \nonumber \\
		&g(x,t;t_n)=-{k(t-t_n)\over 2\theta^2}+{1\over 2x}-{2(2+k(t-t_n))\over 4x(2+2k(t-t_n))+(4\alpha-\theta^2)(t-t_n)} \nonumber \\
        &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~+{(4\alpha-\theta^2)^2(t-t_n)\over 32\theta^2 x^2}. \nonumber
	\end{align}
	Moreover, 

\[
\frac{1}{F(x,t;t_n)}\le 1,~
|g(x,t;t_n)|\le K\left(1+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{t-t_n}{x^2}\right),~
\sup_{t\le T,\,N} g(x,t;t_n)\le K\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2}\right),
\]
\[
\inf_{x\ge0} g(x,t;t_n)
=
-\frac{k}{2\theta^2}(t-t_n)
\ge
-\frac{kT}{2\theta^2}.
\]
where $K>0$ is a constant depending only on $\alpha$, $\theta$ and $T$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.657234+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2e45445b85e57de6ed3a6450cd3504d560450fd726497e1b629eaa58216f12a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 20 (Exponential-moment bound) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let $k\ge1$ and $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k\in\Ccg$ be supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with
$\|\phi_i\|_\infty\le M_0$. Then
\begin{equation}
\bN\Bigl[\prod_{i=1}^k|\mu(\phi_i)|\Bigr]
\;\le\;\gamma^{k-1}\,(2k-3)!!\,\bigl(C_\star M_0\bigr)^{k}
\;\le\;A^{\,k}\,k!\,,
\end{equation}
for $A=A(R_0,M_0)$. Consequently, for every
$\varphi\in\Ccg$ supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with $\|\varphi\|_\infty\le M_0$, the
moment generating function of $\mu(\varphi)$ under the size-biased measure
$\Nh=\mu(\varphi_0)\,\bN$ is finite near the origin:
\begin{equation}
\Nh\bigl[e^{\theta\,\mu(\varphi)}\bigr]
=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\theta^k}{k!}\,\bN\bigl[\mu(\varphi_0)\,\mu(\varphi)^k\bigr]
<\infty\qquad\text{for } |\theta|<1/A',
\end{equation}
where $A'=A'(R_0,M_0,\varphi_0)$. The same holds jointly: for
$\varphi^1,\dots,\varphi^j\in\Ccg$ supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with
$\|\varphi^i\|_\infty\le M_0$, the joint MGF
$\Nh[\exp(\sum_i\theta_i\mu(\varphi^i))]$ is finite for $|\theta|$ small
enough, by H\"older's inequality.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593334+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2fc1d175bae9a5f00102fd544cb38332daba9209acf4dfe55424ec6326d61de","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] One of the most common descriptions of solutions of singular SPDEs is their characterisation as the limit of solutions of renormalised smooth random PDEs. We quantify the speed of this convergence in the case of the KPZ equation. In particular, we show that the na\\\"ive guess that the rate is given by the distance of the noise regularity from the endpoint regularity for well-posedness is not correct. Instead, we obtain convergence at the larger rate $1/2$ and show that this rate is sharp. This is achieved by considering the equation satisfied by the rescaled error, which is critical for variance blowup, and showing that this equation has a limit given by an affine linear singular SPDE driven by a new, independent noise. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:52:51.763133+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3223d8c3fad1c6c8b05cff9dce34e7d45416a97ea810ebf9d22dca071224981","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:classicalStochStab of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Suppose that $x^*$ is an equilibrium of the SDE (equation eq:main_d of the paper) and let
$X$ be a global solution with initial data $X_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $Y=X-x^*$ is a solution of the centered SDE (equation eq:main_YSDE of the paper) with $Y_0=X_0-x^*$. We say that the equilibrium  $x^*$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item stable in probability for $t\geq 0$ if  for any  $s\geq 0$ and $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\sup_{t>s}\|Y(t)\|>\varepsilon\right]=0;
\]
\item asymptotically stable in probability if  it is stable in probability and 
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\lim_{t\to\infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\right]=1;
\]
\item pth-moment stable if for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,
\]
whenever $\|Y_0\|^p<\delta$; if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square stable;
\item globally pth-moment asymptotically stable if  it is pth-moment stable, and for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]=0;
\] 
if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square asymptotically stable;
\item a.s.~stable if  for any $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\|Y(t)\|<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,\quad a.s,
\] 
whenever $\|Y_0\|<\delta$;
\item globally a.s.~asymptotically stable if  for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$, 
\[
\lim_{t\to \infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\quad a.s.
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.350731+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e33a70d0d09cf4f2fb54d7c01ab85e5224355e2dc6d011ae8099d05660c96c11","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 182 (quenched second moment bounds for 
$\bar{D}^{\RomII}$ and 
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In addition to Lemma~\ref{l:barD.II.second} we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[\max\bigg\{
	\frac{\bE[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{p(q_d)}
	: 0\le d\le \dmax-1\bigg\}
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\RomII)^2 \BUCKETS \delta}{M}\,,\]
where $\SMAX_N(\RomII)$ is a random variable satisfying the bound
	\[\P\Big(\SMAX_N(\RomII) \ge \log N\Big)
	\le\exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)\,.\]
The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ in place of
$\bar{D}^{\RomII}$.

\begin{proof} Recall that
we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.II} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)}{(p_d)^{1/2}}
	= 
	\frac{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\sum_{a\in B}
	\frac{\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)}{|B|^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1})\bigg)
	\equiv
	\frac{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)\,.
	\]
If we define the random variable
	\[
	\SMAX_N(\RomII)
	\equiv\max
	\bigg\{
	\bigg|
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)
	\bigg|
	: 
	0\le d\le \dmax-1,
	B\in \mathcal{B}(q_d)
	\bigg\}\,,
	\]
then we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[
	\frac{\bE[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{p_d}
	= \frac{\delta_d}{M}\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d)}
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by \bigg)^2
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\RomII)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{M}\,,
	\]
Note that for any $B\subseteq[M]$ we have
$\bar{\bg}^B= \bar{\bG}^\st \be_B$, so $\|\bar{\bg}^B\| \le\|\bar{\bG}\|_\textup{op}$. It then follows from Lemma~\ref{l:wishart} that for $C(\alpha)$ large enough, we have 
	\beq
	\P\Big(\|\bar{\bg}^B\|^2 \ge 
	C(\alpha) N \textup{ for any }B\subseteq[M]\Big)
	\le \frac{1}{2^N}\,.
	\eeq
The vectors $(\bar{\bg}^B : B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d))$ are measurable with respect to $\cG(q_d)$, so applying Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} gives
	\begin{align*}
	&\P\Big(\SMAX_N(\RomII) \ge \log N\Big)
	=\P\bigg(
	\bigg|
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)
	\bigg|
		\ge \log N
	\textup{ for any } 0\le d\le \dmax- 1, B \in \mathcal{B}(q_d)
	\bigg)\\
	&\qquad\le
	\dmax\BUCKETS
	\bigg\{ \frac{1}{2^N}
	+ \exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)
	\bigg\}
	\le\exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)
	\,,
	\end{align*}
where the $1/2^N$ in the second line comes from \eqref{e:II.union.bound}, and the final simplification uses Assumption~\ref{a:params}. This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\RomII}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:36:49.928517+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e347ff1c8563c534518f837e5edb616a903a413aaa066bbb80a24db7a809b259","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Openproblem op:mather-measures of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Conceptually, (equation eq:AtoM of the paper) shows that the Mather set can, in principle, be recovered from the projected Aubry set $\mathcal A$ together with the limiting function $u_\infty$. However, this characterization is not particularly convenient from a numerical point of view. It is therefore natural to ask whether Evans' variational approximation also provides a more direct way to recover the projected Mather set $\mathcal M$, or equivalently the full Mather set $\widetilde{\mathcal M}$.

Let
\[
\sigma_k(x)
:=
\frac{e^{kH(Du_k(x),x)}}
{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb T^n}
e^{kH(Du_k(y),y)}\,dy}.
\]
The pair \((u_k,\sigma_k)\) is also the logarithmically coupled stationary mean-field game associated with Evans' variational approximation; see [GY20].
Thanks to [Evans03, Evans04], along a subsequence,
\[
\sigma_{k_j}\rightharpoonup \sigma
\qquad\text{weakly in the sense of measures},
\]
where \(\sigma\) is a projected Mather measure. In dimension one, under a
suitable nondegeneracy condition, \(\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)\) coincides
with the whole projected Mather set (i.e., $\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)=\mathcal M$),  whereas degeneracy may lead to further
selection ([GISMY10]). What is the corresponding picture in higher dimensions? In
particular, under what conditions does
\[
\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)=\mathcal M,
\]
and what determines the subset of \(\mathcal M\) selected when this equality
fails? (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:10:43.924488+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3673209aa7d8cbb17b1a91d3b22351e3561bf5a777aad8375f1ad37ba043927","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Propn generalCouple of arXiv:2412.04527, 'Critical Drift for Brownian Bees and a Reflected Brownian Motion Invariance Principle'] Let $B=((B^{j}(t))_{t\geq 0})_{1\leq j\leq N}$ be a family of $N$ i.i.d Brownian motions, $\nu$ be an initial configuration of $N$ particles, $Q=(Q(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a Poisson point process of intensity $N$, and $I=(I_i)_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of i.i.d random variables which are uniform on $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. Then there exist functions $\Upsilon$ and $\Xi$ with values in $\mathbb R^N$ such that:
$$(X^N(t))_{t\geq 0}=\Theta^N\left( \Upsilon\left(\nu,B, Q, I,t\right)_{t\geq 0}\right)$$ is an $N$-Brownian bees process and

is an $N$-BBM process.

Moreover, given configurations $\nu$ and $\nu'$ such that $\nu \preccurlyeq \nu'$, we have
$$\Upsilon(\nu, B, Q, I,t) \preccurlyeq \Xi(\nu, B, Q, I,t)\preccurlyeq \Xi(\nu', B, Q, I,t) \; \forall t\geq 0$$","status":"unverified"}

\[
F_{x,t}(q):=v_0(q)-g^q(x-q,t),
\qquad q\in [r_L(x,t),r_U(x,t)],
\]
where $r_L(x,t),r_U(x,t)$ are as in Corollary \ref{cor: restriction to compact interval}. Define the two contact sets
\[
A_0(x,t):=\{q\in [r_L,r_U]: q\le x,\ g^q(x-q,t)=0\},
\]
and
\[
A_1(x,t):=\{q\in [r_L,r_U]: q\ge x,\ g^q(x-q,t)=q-x\}.
\]
Then
\[
\max_{q\in[r_L,r_U]}F_{x,t}(q)
=
\max_{q\in [r_L,r_U]\setminus (\operatorname{int}A_0(x,t)\cup \operatorname{int}A_1(x,t))}F_{x,t}(q).
\]
In particular, there exists a maximiser $q^*$ such that either
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:35:57.003752+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e37836a89c6daf091382bfc6c4ed6f0cd7343b9694cdc60e9d2e6e6e3fb81078","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:general_order of arXiv:2604.05921, 'Simplicity of random hypergraphs'] For any functions $f^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$ and $w \in \mathds{N}$, if

    \item $\forall k \in [\delta]:$

then

 \sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta}:\\\sum_{i=1}^{\delta} ia_i = \delta}} \sum_{\alpha(\cdot) \in R(\vb*{a})} H( \vb*{a},\alpha(\cdot)) &= \delta!^w (n\mathds{E}[f^{(1)}(U) ])^{\delta} + \Big( -\frac{1}{2} \frac{\delta!^{1+w}}{(\delta-2)!}(n\mathds{E}[f^{(1)}(U)])^{\delta-2} n\mathds{E}[(f^{(1)}(U))^2] \nonumber\\
 &\hspace{0.5cm} + \frac{1}{2^{1+w}} \frac{\delta!^{1+w}}{(\delta-2)!} (n\mathds{E}[f^{(1)}(U)])^{\delta-2} n\mathds{E}[f^{(2)}(U)] \Big) (1+o(1))\nonumber \\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:56.999487+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3783c37c11943ed0174f30d290547fd9494262e01ffe56769f28b1563f0997c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 34 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta$ be a fully hidden simplicial complex on $[n]$. Then
$$
\Aut(X_\Delta)\ =\ T_0\ \rtimes\ S(\Delta),
$$
a linear algebraic group of dimension~$n$ whose identity component is $T_0$.\rchange{\footnote{
For \emph{irreducible} rigid affine varieties, \cite[Theorem~1]{AG17} produces a subtorus of
$\Aut(X)$ containing every other subtorus, which is therefore normal. That statement does not
cover the present case: a fully hidden $\Delta$ on $n\geq2$ vertices has at least two facets;
a single facet would be all of $[n]$, every vertex of which is private, so $X_\Delta$ is
reducible. Their Proposition~1 does give a finite extension of the torus when the canonical
grading is pointed, a hypothesis $\KK[\Delta]$ satisfies (its weight cone is $\ZZ^n_{\geq0}$
and its degree-zero part is $\KK$), but only for an integral graded algebra, and the extension
is not asserted to split. Whether $\Aut(X)$ is a finite extension of a torus for a general rigid
$X$ is open even under strong hypotheses \cite[Remark~6.5]{BGa25}. The proof below is self-contained and gives more: the
extension splits, with finite complement $S(\Delta)$.}}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.961198+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e37d5ab70ce1f5dd051126327acaaa5bf3879f6bda6c7f479ea43213c2898b72","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 11 (Isometry relation) of arXiv:2608.12225, 'Higher-order variation and\\ pathwise It\^o calculus on manifolds'] Let $p\geq 2$ be an even integer, let $X\in V_p(M,\pi)$, and assume
that the tensor measure $[X]_\pi^{(p)}$ has no atoms. Let $\nabla$ be
an affine connection on $M$ and let $f\in C^p(M,\mathbb R)$. Let
\[
    I_t^\nabla(f,X)
    :=
    \int_0^t
    \left\langle
        T_\nabla^{p-1}f(X_s),
        d_\pi^{p-1}X_s
    \right\rangle,
    \qquad 0\leq t\leq T.
\]
be the integral defined in \eqref{eq:pathwiseintegral}. Then
$I^\nabla(f,X)\in V_p(\mathbb R,\pi),$
and its $p$-th variation along $\pi$ is given by
\begin{equation}
    d[I^\nabla(f,X)]_{\pi,t}^{(p)}
    =
    \left\langle
        (df_{X_t})^{\otimes p},
        d[X]_{\pi,t}^{(p)}
    \right\rangle.   
\end{equation}
Equivalently, for every $t\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation}
    [I^\nabla(f,X)]_\pi^{(p)}([0,t])
    =
    \int_{[0,t]}
    \left\langle
        (df_{X_s})^{\otimes p},
        d[X]_{\pi,s}^{(p)}
    \right\rangle.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Let $0<\alpha<d<(1+\gamma)\alpha$, and $F_T^2 = T^{3+\gamma-\frac{d}{\alpha}}.$

\mathrm{Cov}\big(\langle \X(s),\varphi\rangle,\langle \X(t),\psi\rangle\big)

{2(\frac{d}{\alpha}-1)(2-\frac{d}{\alpha})(3-\frac{d}{\alpha})

where
\begin{align}
\nonumber
C(s,t)

-(t+s-2w)^{\b}

\\ 
&\qquad 0\le s\le t,\quad \varphi,\psi\in\E.

{"assumptions":["conditioned Galton-Watson (simply generated) tree with n vertices","N_d = number of vertices of outdegree d"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.318625+00:00","domain":"probability/random trees","id":"claim_e3850e9afeb448f99ec9561d012acf69","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Janson's Problem 20.2 (Probability Surveys 2012, Section 20.2) asks whether the outdegree counts N_d of a conditioned Galton-Watson (simply generated) tree are asymptotically normal. (a) nu = 1 with finite variance: yes, jointly with the covariances (Janson, Random Structures Algorithms 48 (2016), Theorem 1.13 with Example 2.2 and Section 8). (b) nu = 1 with infinite variance and (c) nu < 1: yes when the offspring law is regularly varying (Thevenin, Electron. J. Probab. 25 (2020), Theorems 6.2 and 6.7, variance pi_d(1 - pi_d)), but not in general. A subcritical law whose bulk sits on {0, 1}, with two rare atoms at (1 - q - c) n_r +/- A sqrt(n_r), each of probability n_r^{-4}, makes the conditioned tree carry exactly one of the two with probability tending to 1/2 each, so N_1 = n pi_1 -/+ A sqrt(n) up to smaller terms, a near two-point law (Theorem A, full proof); the critical infinite-variance case is the same construction with the pair straddling the missing mass of an absent rarer atom (Theorem B, a sketch that still needs a lattice local moderate-deviation expansion). Thevenin's conjecture that normality holds for every such law is therefore false. The regularly varying case survives because the giant's law is locally flat at scale sqrt(n).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["product measure on a FINITE index set","BK: both events increasing","Reimer: no monotonicity hypothesis"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542992+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3854fb8e108d83f54f7a2c762956ced396b14b16573131eabefa9f8eab4f84b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let P be a product measure on {0,1}^E with E FINITE. For events A and B define the DISJOINT OCCURRENCE A box B as the set of configurations omega for which there exist DISJOINT sets of coordinates K and L such that every configuration agreeing with omega on K lies in A and every configuration agreeing with omega on L lies in B - informally, A and B occur for disjoint reasons. VAN DEN BERG-KESTEN: if A and B are both INCREASING then P(A box B) <= P(A) P(B). REIMER: the same inequality holds for ARBITRARY events A and B, with no monotonicity hypothesis. The direction is opposite to Harris-FKG, which is the point: increasing events are positively correlated, but requiring them to occur on disjoint witnesses destroys that correlation and more. The finiteness of E is a genuine hypothesis of the standard statements; infinite index sets are handled by approximation, and the definition of disjoint occurrence itself needs care there. Typical use: bounding the probability of two disjoint open crossings, or of a self-avoiding open path of length n, by a product. [van den Berg and Kesten (1985); Reimer (2000), Combin. Probab. Comput. 9; see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.12]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.487280+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3be3c9182f994af2806f0d42922ebf649a4ecf9e795918fbcd91230f3fe9f9f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn Coulomb gas correlations for a divisor on the Riemann sphere of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let the divisor
$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=\sum \sigma_j \cdot z_j,
$$
where $\left\{z_j\right\}_{j=1}^n$ is a finite set of distinct points on $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.
The Coulomb gas correlation $C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ is a differential of conformal dimension $\lambda_j$ at $z_j$, given by

\begin{equation}
\lambda_j=\lambda_b\left(\sigma_j\right) \equiv \frac{\sigma_j^2}{2}-\sigma_j b ,
\end{equation}

where $\lambda_b(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^2}{2}-\sigma b \quad(\sigma \in \mathbb{C})$
whose value is given by

\begin{equation}
C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] =\prod_{j<k}\left(z_j-z_k\right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} ,
\end{equation}
where the product is taken over all finite $z_j$ and $z_k$. 

This defines a holomorphic function of $\boldsymbol{z}$ on the configuration space
\[
\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{distinct}}^n = \left\{ \boldsymbol{z} = (z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n \,\middle|\, z_j \neq z_k \text{ for } j \neq k \right\}.
\]
In general, the function is multivalued, and one must choose a single-valued branch for each factor $(z_j-z_k)^{\sigma_j\sigma_k}$, except in special cases where all $\sigma_j$ are integers. If all $\sigma_j$ are even integers, the function becomes single-valued and independent of the ordering of the product. In the special case where $\sigma_j = 1$ for all $j$, the correlation function coincides with the Vandermonde determinant.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:25:39.120731+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3cc1fa1154102f504e898815b49b8cceb927c121b826bbd2318d87db76d9089","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def: boundary connectivity event of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Write
$\Sigma_M^c=\{-1,1\}^{\partial\Lambda_M\cup (\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda_M)}.$

For any $\xi\in \Sigma_M^c$, let
$
\mathcal P=\{x\in \partial \Lambda_M:\xi_x=1\}.
$
Let $\mathcal P_0,\mathcal P_1\subset \mathcal P$ be two disjoint subsets, and let $\mathcal U$ be a collection of mutually disjoint subsets of $\mathcal P$, each of which is also disjoint from $\mathcal P_0\cup \mathcal P_1$.

Define $\mathcal Y^{-}$ to be the event that $\mathcal P_0$ is not plus-connected to $\mathcal P_1$ inside $\Lambda_M$, and define $\mathcal Y^{+}$ to be the event that, for every $U\in \mathcal U$, the set $U$ is plus-connected to $\mathcal P_0$ inside $\Lambda_M$. We then write
$
\mathcal Y=\mathcal Y^{-}\cap \mathcal Y^{+}.
$

Next, let $\mathcal X^{-}$ be the event that there exists a $*$-minus circuit in the annulus
$
\Lambda_{M/2}\setminus \Lambda_{M/4},
$
and let $\mathcal X^{+}$ be the event that there exists a plus circuit in the same annulus which is plus-connected to $\mathcal P_0$. We define
$
\mathcal X=\mathcal X^{+}\cap \mathcal X^{-}.
$

Finally, set
$
\mathcal R=\mathcal Y\setminus \mathcal X,
\mathcal S=\mathcal X\cap \mathcal Y.
$
For simplicity, we use
$
X,X^{+},X^{-},Y,Y^{+},Y^{-},R,S\in\{0,1\}
$
to denote the indicator functions of the events
$
\mathcal X,\mathcal X^{+},\mathcal X^{-},\mathcal Y,\mathcal Y^{+},\mathcal Y^{-},\mathcal R,\mathcal S,
$
respectively.","status":"unverified"}

For each $j\in\llbracket0,s\rrbracket$ let $H_{s-j}$ and $Y_j$ be as in Corollary \ref{C4} and, if $j\ge 1$, let 
$$\l_j:=l_j-1.$$ Then the following properties hold. 

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have $\textup{g}_{Y_0}=0$ and for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ we have
\[
\textup{g}_{Y_i}=\frac{p-1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^i \l_jp^{i-j}.
\]

{\bf (2)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$, $p-1$ divides $\textup{g}_{Y_i}$.

{\bf (3)} Let $\mathcal R_X$ be the $B_0[H]$-module of Proposition \ref{P5}(2). Then we have identities 
$$\frac{\textup{g}_{Y_i}-\textup{g}_{Y_{i-1}}}{p^i-p^{i-1}}=\frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}=\frac{u_i-1}{2}$$
for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ and hence a $B_0[H]$-linear isomorphism 
$$\mathcal R_X\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}\mathcal B_i= \oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$

{\bf (4)} Let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth projective curve over $\Spec R$ whose reduction modulo $\upsilon$ is $X$ and such that there exists a homomorphism $\varrho:G\rightarrow\Aut(\mathcal X)$ that lifts $\rho$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip\noindent

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.d)} We have $B[H]$-linear isomorphisms
$$H^0(\mathcal X,\Omega_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong H^1(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$","status":"unverified"}

        M_r^{(T)}:=\sum_{\ell\in B_r}N_\ell^{(T)},
        \qquad r\ge1.
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:57:28.221127+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3e9050bed568a5832fc609ed28297c290eb9df777f984c24eb78ffc28b92d99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] A \textit{sublinear expectation} $\mathbb{E}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is a functional $\mathbb{E}\colon \mathcal{H} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}} := [-\infty, +\infty]$ satisfying the following properties for all $X, Y \in \mathcal{H}$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(a)] \textit{Monotonicity.} If $X \geq Y$, then $\mathbb{E}[X] \geq \mathbb{E}[Y]$.
			\item[(b)] \textit{Constant preserving.} $\mathbb{E}[c] = c$, $\forall\, c \in \mathbb{R}$.
			\item[(c)] \textit{Positive homogeneity.} $\mathbb{E}[\lambda X] = \lambda\,\mathbb{E}[X]$, $\forall\, \lambda \geq 0$.
			\item[(d)] \textit{Subadditivity.} $\mathbb{E}[X + Y] \leq \mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$, provided that $\mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$ does not take the form $\infty - \infty$ or $-\infty + \infty$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.653269+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3ed8a2095bd6054c4de10d9c2270c68eb0eb0119e3346760bd88d1b8453c55c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 39 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $m < n$ be positive integers and $a_1, \dots, a_n, b_1 \dots b_n$ be integers.
Let $R = \mbC [x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring endowed with a $\mbZ^2$-grading defined by the $2 \times n$ matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a_1 & \cdots & a_n \\
b_1 & \cdots & b_n 
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This means that the bi-degree of the variable $x_i$ is $(a_i, b_i) \in \mbZ^2$.
We denote by 
\begin{equation} 
\mbT \begin{pNiceArray}{ccc|ccc}[first-row]
x_1 & \dots & x_m & x_{m+1} & \dots & x_n \\
a_1 & \dots & a_m & a_{m+1} & \dots & a_n \\
b_1 & \dots & b_m & b_{m+1} & \dots & b_n
\end{pNiceArray}
\end{equation}
the toric variety whose Cox ring is $R$ and irrelevant ideal is 
\[
I = (x_1, \dots, x_m) \cap (x_{m+1}, \dots, x_n).
\]
In other words, this toric variety is the geometric quotient
\[
(\mbA^n_{x_1, \dots, x_n} \setminus V (I))/(\mbC^*)^2,
\]
where the $(\mbC^*)^2$-action is defined by
\[
(\lambda, \mu) \cdot (x_1, \dots, x_n) = (\lambda^{a_1} \mu^{b_1} x_1, \dots, \lambda^{a_n} \mu^{b_n} x_n).
\]
For a point $\msp$ of the toric variety \eqref{eq:deftoricT}, which we denote by $\mbT$, we pick a point $\msq = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mbA^n$ in the preimage of the natural projection $\mbA^n \setminus V (I) \to \mbT$ over $\msp$.
In this case we express $\msp$ as $\msp = (\alpha_1\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_m;\alpha_{m+1}\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_n) \in \mbT$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869358+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_e3fe93c1b93e4bf1bae09cdb537c1446b11a7eef12cc45dbf8842efaebdec015","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"FIRES WHEN you are about to prove a convex-order dominance for a Markov-modulated inter-event time by conditioning on the modulating state and calling the result a mixture of exponentials. THE ROUTE: conditionally on the chain's stationary sojourn structure the inter-event time is exponential with a state-dependent rate, and a MIXTURE of exponentials always dominates the matched exponential in the convex order by Jensen applied to t -> E[exp(-lambda t)]. WHERE IT FAILS: only when the chain does NOT move during the inter-event interval. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.271306+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e404df3cb2e235b58e9b1b2e17f50f5e1d2ec0e5026dbe3027870738508b3282","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 (Admissible analytic resolution) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] Let
\[
 I_k=\{n\in\mathbb N:2^k\le n<2^{k+1}\},\qquad k\ge0.
\]
A family of scalar sequences
$\sigma=(\sigma_j)_{j\ge0}$ on $\mathbb N$ is called
$(L,M,p)$-admissible if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item $\sigma_j(n)=0$ for $n\in I_k$ whenever $|j-k|>L$;
 \item $\sum_{j\ge0}\sigma_j(n)=1$ for every $n\ge1$;
 \item for every $|\ell|\le L$, the patched sequence
 \[
  m_\ell(n)=\sigma_{k+\ell}(n)\qquad(n\in I_k),
  \tag{3.8}
 \]
 with $\sigma_j=0$ for $j<0$, is an $H^p$ coefficient multiplier of
 norm at most $M$.
\end{enumerate}
Put
\[
 W_j^\sigma\phi(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_j(n)\widehat\phi(n)z^n,
 \qquad
 \mathscr S_{\phi,p}^{\sigma}a
 =a_{-1}\phi(0)+
  \sum_{j\ge0}a_j2^{-j/p'}W_j^\sigma\phi.
 \tag{3.9}
\]
The hard resolution is $\sigma_j=\mathbf1_{I_j}$ and has $L=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:19:46.227892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e40608a37e4de12076c5bc6e9e448876a6b9b555bdd13c5118d52fc6908afd03","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 5 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] The sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$ obeys the \textbf{large deviations principle} (`\textbf{LDP}') with \textbf{rate function} $I$ if the following hold:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[i.] (Upper bound) If $x \in \X$ and $a < I(x)$, then there is a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
		\[\mu_n U \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
		\item[ii.] (Lower bound) If $x \in \X$ and $I(x) < a < \infty$, then any neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ satisfies
		\[\mu_n U \ge e^{-a n - o(n)}.\]
		\item[iii.] (Exponential tightness) For every $a > 0$ there is a compact subset $K$ of $\X$ such that
		\[\mu_n (\X\setminus K) \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.574081+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e41f0b739f26bb6027eacf3b08b34476be282aed82e4038a53ce4bfa084548fb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:Wishart.integrated.deBruijn of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Under the assumptions of Proposition~(prop:Wishart.deBruijn of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Ent}(\mu \, \| \, \xi)
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.
\end{equation}
Assume furthermore that $\mu$ is the law of a random matrix $\mathfrak{X}$ and that this law has Lebesgue density $f_{\mathfrak{X}}$, that is, $\mu(\mathrm{d} X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X) \, \mathrm{d} X$. Equivalently, if $f_{\xi}$ denotes the Lebesgue density of $\xi$, then the initial relative density is $g(X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)/f_{\xi}(X)$. Assume also that $\mathfrak{X}$ has finite differential entropy
\[
H(\mathfrak{X}) \vcentcolon= -\int_{\mathcal{S}_{++}^d} f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)\log(f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)) \, \mathrm{d} X.
\]
If $\mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{X}] = \mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}] = \alpha \Sigma$ and $\mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{X}|)] = \mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}|)]\in \mathbb{R}$ with $\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}\sim \xi$, then
\begin{equation}
H(\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}) - H(\mathfrak{X})
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.343947+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e41f4766ec987f0bb5a3107a0f5fd2495a0b1918b61a8bb4fb2d6507a7b06ef9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Fix a compact set $K\Subset \C\setminus \Sigma$, where
\[
\Sigma:=\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }|\xi_1(x,z)|=|\xi_2(x,z)|\right\}
\cup
\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }\xi_1(x,z)^2=1\right\},
\]
and for each $x\in[0,1]$ the numbers $\xi_1(x,z),\xi_2(x,z)$ are the roots of
\[
\lambda^2-\frac{z-b(x)}{c(x)}\lambda+\frac{d(x)}{c(x)}=0
\]
ordered so that $|\xi_1(x,z)|>|\xi_2(x,z)|$ on $K$.

Then, for every fixed block index $j$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[

-\frac{1}{c(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}

and

\frac{\det(R_k^{(j)'}-zI)}{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)}
-\frac{1}{d(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)=o(1),

uniformly for $z\in K$.

\[

satisfies

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.163857+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e444a01e4404c33f58e4f4f48ec3e8fbc8498651ff93b0fc01e5ff4adf5a47a1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $V$ defined by \eqref{e:freeprob.V} is strictly convex on the interval $(z_0,+\infty)$, with $V(z)\to\infty$ as $z\to\infty$.
As a consequence, $V$ has a unique minimizer on the interval $[z_0,+\infty)$, which we denote $z_{\min}$.

\begin{proof} For $z>z_0$, we calculate
    \beq
        
        V'(z)
        = 1 - \alpha \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2} \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j
            \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\,.
    \eeq
Recall that $m:(\hw_1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is strictly decreasing, and we have
$\alpha - \hv_j m(z) > 0$ for all $z>z_0$. It follows that, on  the interval
$(z_0,\infty)$, the function
    \[
    \frac{m(z)}{\alpha-\hv_j m(z)}
    = \frac{1}{\alpha/m(z)-\hv_j}
    \]
is strictly decreasing, \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. Consequently, in \eqref{e:fp-V-pr}, each term
    \[      \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\]
is strictly decreasing on $(z_0,\infty)$, again \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. In the special case $s=1$, we have $m_2(z)=m(z)^2$, so we conclude in this case that $V'$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$. For $s\ge2$, we note that $m_2(z)/m(z)^2$ is positive, and
    \[
        \frac{d}{dz}\bigg[ \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2}\bigg]
        = \frac{2}{m(z)^3} \Big(m_2(z)^2 - m(z)m_3(z)\Big)
        < 0
    \]
by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. It therefore follows in this case as well that $V'$ is strictly increasing, and so $V$ is strictly convex, on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$.
Finally, as $z\to\infty$, $m(z) \to 0$. Therefore the first term of $V(z)$ tends to $\infty$ while the second term remains bounded, and so $V(z) \to \infty$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:38:17.819086+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e472937d7416053bd3ea1a75e9e020a460bd6d0795ed170360dda558098cb7e4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition d.fpc of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] For $h \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, the forward play-cone $F_h$ of $h$ is set equal to 
$$
F_h \, = \, \Big\{ \, (k,\ell) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \times \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}_+: \vert k - h \vert \leq \ell \, , \, \vert k-h \vert + \ell  \in 2\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}} \, \Big\} \, .
$$

Let $S \in \mathcal{S}$ (and recall the formulation of the strategy space~$\mathcal{S}$ from Section~(s.tlp of the paper)). A  {\em Mina deviation point} is an element $(q,\ell) \in F_h$ for which 
there exists a trajectory $\psi: \llbracket 0, \ell \rrbracket \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\psi(0) = h$ and $\psi(\ell) = q$
such that $S(\psi) \neq b_q$.
Write  $\mathsf{D}_-(S,h) \subseteq F_h$ for the set of Mina deviation points. The strategy $S$ is  {\em deviating for Mina} if  $\mathsf{D}_-(S,h) \neq \emptyset$.
 A {\em Maxine deviation point} is an element $(q,\ell) \in F_h$ such that  $S(\psi) \not= a_q$ for some path~$\psi$ as above. Write $\mathsf{D}_+(S,h)$ for the set of these points; if  $\mathsf{D}_+(S,h) \not= \emptyset$, then $S$ is deviating for Maxine.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:47:32.860637+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e48b093837fbc99ae3c41de0e737150320f1f4f5397d49d81b43e0904ffbe867","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.02423, '2609.02423'] Let $1<\sigma<s$, $z_N=P_NJ^\sigma u$, and
$z_{\nu,N}=\chi_{\nu,N}(D)z_N$.  On an $x$ chart take the single
weight scale $\lambda\simeq N$.  If $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ is the sign of
$v_x$ on the chart, the commutator with
$\tau a_{\lambda,x_0}$ has the form
\begin{equation}
 \ip{i[\omega(D),\tau a_{\lambda,x_0}]z_{\nu,N}}{z_{\nu,N}}
 =\norm{Q_{x,\nu,x_0}z_N}_2^2
 +\ip{R_{x,\nu,x_0}z_N}{z_N},
\end{equation}
where
\[
 Q_{x,\nu,x_0}
 =\Op\left(
 \left(\frac\lambda R\right)^{1/2}
 \psi_0\left(\frac{\lambda(x-x_0)}R\right)
 |v_x|^{1/2}\chi_{\nu,N}\right).
\]
This uses the smooth factorization $a'=\psi_0^2$ from
\eqref{eq:aprime-square}; in particular, no nonsmooth choice of the
square root of $a'$ is involved.  On a $y$ chart the analogous
identity holds with $\mu\simeq N^{1/2}$, $y_0$, and $v_y$.  For $R$
sufficiently large,
\begin{equation}
 |\ip{R_{r,\nu,r_0}z_N}{z_N}|
 \le \frac14\sup_{r_0'\in\R}\norm{Q_{r,\nu,r_0'}z_N}_2^2
 +C_R\norm{z_N}_2^2,
\end{equation}
where $r=x$ or $y$ and $r_0=x_0$ or $y_0$.  The constants are
uniform in $N$ and the spatial centres.  For every smooth
frequency-truncated function,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{r_0\in\R}\norm{Q_{r,\nu,r_0}z_N}_2^2
 \le C_RN^3\norm{z_N}_2^2<\infty.
\end{equation}
Thus the supremum in \eqref{eq:remainder-absorb} is finite before any
absorption is performed.

Finally, the statement holds verbatim with $\chi_{\nu,N}$ replaced by
any of the auxiliary symbols $\Theta_{\nu,N,\ell}$,
$\ell\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, of \cref{def:chart-ladder}, with constants
uniform in $\ell$.  Indeed, the proof uses only the symbol bounds
\eqref{eq:chart-symbol} and the fact that $v_\nu$ has a fixed sign on
the support, both of which are imposed on every level in
\cref{def:chart-ladder}.","status":"unverified"}

Conditional on R_1,...,R_{n-1}, assume their span is a hyperplane and choose a nonzero normal v measurable in these rows. Then P(det(R_1,...,R_n)=0 | R_1,...,R_{n-1})=P(R_n dot v=0 | R_1,...,R_{n-1}); the conditional law of R_n is its original law. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.424875+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e48d1c31ee50e160fa1e46d567717236adb315c63688f5abb4b567b9c82f86e6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Polish functor}] 
  We say that a functor $\tau$ is \textit{Polish} if there exist a functor $\tilde{\tau}$
  and, for each $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
  a sequence $(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S))_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of open subsets in $\tilde{\tau}(S)$
  satisfying the following conditions.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (P\arabic*), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
      The functor $\tilde{\tau}$ is complete, separable and continuous. 
    \item 
      The functor $\tau$ is a topological subfunctor of $\tilde{\tau}$.
    \item 
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
      it holds that $\tau(S) = \bigcap_{k \geq 1} \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S)$.
    \item 
      Let $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$ be a root-and-distance-preserving map
      between $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}) \in \mathfrak{M},\, i=1,2$.
      Then, $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{2})) = \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{1})$
      for each $k \geq 1$. 
      In particular,
      $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tau(S_{2})) = \tau(S_{1})$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We call $(\tilde{\tau}, (\tilde{\tau}_{k})_{k \geq 1})$ a \textit{Polish system} of $\tau$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:56.358067+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4b1211b343875f5b0a7fafc1532fce118c225bf3b06fa3cad002c4eea90951d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 13 (Equivalent formulations of strong convergence) of arXiv:2507.00346, 'The strong convergence phenomenon'] The following are equivalent.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:36:31.222978+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4bb4fe20e5e937d839408919319e0a8b80f27eb098ab2f1f65bfb0458c3bbff","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 10 (Exhaustive finite-time breakdown alternative) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,T_{\max})\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a maximal smooth

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.777908+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4c1242f69a232cc761b104feec96b3cc3fd100c4f2b1bcf410f2ecd17823e36","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(I_a=[1,a]\). Then \(N_a(L)/L\) satisfies a large deviations principle on \([0,\infty)\) with speed \(L\) and good rate function
\[
J_a(x):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}}\{\theta x-\Lambda_a(\theta)\},
\qquad x\geq0.
\]
That is, for every Borel set \(A\subset[0,\infty)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
-\inf_{x\in A^\circ}J_a(x)
&\le \liminf_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \\
&\le \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \le -\inf_{x\in \overline{A}}J_a(x),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(A^\circ\) and \(\overline A\) denote the interior and closure of \(A\) in the relative topology of \([0,\infty)\). Moreover, \(J_a\) is strictly convex on \((0,\infty)\) and vanishes only at \(\lambda_a=\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(1-\frac{1}{a}\right)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Any finite compatible real E m-by-p,B m-by-r,A r-by-p; arbitrary residual E","eta>0 and eta(||E||op+||B||op^2+||A||op^2)<=1/2","Exact simultaneous factor-GD residual map, including its positive quadratic term; no balance or commutation"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:57:31.217681+00:00","domain":"LoRA convergence and Julia operator dilation","id":"claim_e4c38b81ef8e61338829b6c6d6c408f8ccf4a6f6c4a14a4a03bf8cc3cf704c69","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; T419-C024 v2, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed. Let E be any real m-by-p matrix, B any m-by-r matrix and A any r-by-p matrix. Set e=||E||op and h=||B||op^2+||A||op^2. For any eta>0 with eta(e+h)<=1/2, put

 Phi(E,B,A)=E-eta(BB^T E+E A^T A)+eta^2 E A^T B^T E.

Then ||Phi(E,B,A)||op<=||E||op. In particular, when E=BA-Delta, Phi is exactly the residual after one simultaneous GD step for ||BA-Delta||F^2/2. No rank assumption, Gaussian assumption, balance or commutation is required. The lemma gives a sufficient small-step condition, not an optimal one. It does not claim spectral monotonicity at an arbitrary loss-decreasing step.

The hardest point is that orthogonal dilation commutes with this particular nonlinear update after compression. The proof explicitly checks the quadratic term. The algebraic dilation is the classical Julia/Halmos construction; its primary provenance is P. L. Robinson, "Julia operators and Halmos dilations", arXiv:1803.09329, Theorem0 p.1 and Theorem1 p.2. The rectangular block here is the Julia operator with its column blocks switched; Theorem2 concerns the square-space special case. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:05:09.627544+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4d170e19da90e73aac5fa058f2cba282166061e38fab6784a5223131b404e67","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $\phi: [1,\infty) \to (-\infty, 0]$ is a function
that satisfies the following conditions: \hfil\break
(a) $\phi$ is strictly decreasing and convex on $[1, \infty)$; and \hfil\break
(b) one has that
\begin{equation}

\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi(x)\ =\ -\infty 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac {\phi(x)} {x}\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}

   Let $\Gamma$ denote the set of all points $x \in (1, \infty)$ (the open half line) 
such that $\phi$ is {\rm not} differentiable at $x$.
Refer to Notations (nt6.4 of the paper)(A)(B).   
For each $y \in (1, \infty) - \Gamma$, let 
$L^{(y)}: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ denote the affine function whose graph is tangent to that 
of $\phi$ at the point $(y, \phi(y))$ --- that is, the affine function that satisfies
\begin{equation}

L^{(y)}(y)\ =\ \phi(y) \indent {\rm and} \indent 
L^{(y)}(x)\ \leq\ \phi(x)\ \ {\rm for\ all}\ x \in [1, \infty). 
\end{equation}
 
   Then the following statements (I) and (II) hold:
\medskip

   (I) The following statements hold: \hfil\break 
(i) For each $x \in (1, \infty)$, $\phi(x) < \phi(1) \leq 0$. \hfil\break 
(ii) For each $y \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$,  
$[{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}] = \phi'(y) < 0$. \hfil\break   
(iii) The function $x \mapsto \phi'(x)$ for $x \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$, 
is nondecreasing. \hfil\break  
(iv) One has that $\lim_{x \to \infty,\, x \notin \Gamma} \phi'(x) = 0$. 
\medskip

   (II) For any negative number $D$ and any positive number 
$s$, there exists a number    
$T = T(\phi, D, s) > 1$ with the following property:

   For each $y \in [T,\infty)  - \Gamma$, the affine function 
$L^{(y)}$ in (the entire sentence of) eq.\ ((eq6.502 of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}

-s\ \leq\ [{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}]\ =\ \phi'(y)\ <\ 0 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
L^{(y)}(0)\ \leq\ D. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:20:33.754498+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4ee7b1b0c19bb8b82285bdfeda4e24623277fdb17afbb02be376dc92a798f9b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df 34 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $E$ be a finite set.
    Let $E = E_0 \sqcup E_1 \sqcup E_2$ be a tripartition of $E$.
    Write $E_{01} = E_0 \cup E_1$ and $E_{12} = E_1 \cup E_2$.
    Suppose $M$ is a matroid on $E_{01}$ and $N$ is a matroid on $E_{12}$ such that
    $E_1$ is a modular flat of $M$ and
    $M|_{E_1} = N|_{E_1}$.
    
    One defines the \textbf{generalized parallel connection} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$---denoted $P_{E_1}(M, N)$---to be the unique matroid on $E$ whose flats are the subsets $F \subseteq E$ such that 
    $F \cap E_{01}$ is a flat of $M$ and 
    $F \cap E_{12}$ is a flat of $N$.
    The rank of this matroid is $\rk P_{E_1}(M, N) = \rk M + \rk N - \rk_M E_1$.
    When $E_1$ is modular in $N$ also, we say (following Ziegler) that $M$ is the \textbf{modular join} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$.
    In this case, $P_{E_1}(N, M)$ also exists and is equal to $P_{E_1}(M, N)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:58:44.385223+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4f9f5a8039e6fbcc819061673b9989353e90340c139f8fe372a30b2dc4bbbdb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 39 of arXiv:2609.02819, 'Adelic Points and Unramified Brauer Approximation for Classifying Stacks'] Let $q:Y\to\cX$ be a Brauer-detecting atlas, and suppose that $Y$ admits a
smooth proper compactification
\[
 j:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y.
\]

$\overline Y\setminus Y$, and let
\[
 \partial_{D_i}:\Br(Y)\longrightarrow
 H^1(k(D_i),\bQ/\bZ) 
\]
be the residue map.  Then
\begin{equation}
 q^*\Brun(\cX)
 =\operatorname{im}\bigl(\Br(\overline Y)\longrightarrow\Br(Y)\bigr)
\end{equation}

\begin{equation}
 q^*\Brun(\cX)

  \Br(Y)\xrightarrow{\oplus_i\partial_{D_i}}
  \bigoplus_{i=1}^m H^1(k(D_i),\bQ/\bZ)
 \right).
\end{equation}

\[
 0\longrightarrow\Br(\overline Y)

 \bigoplus_{i=1}^m H^1(k(D_i),\bQ/\bZ)
\]
is exact at its first two terms.","status":"unverified"}

 a+(h-1)+q\le m.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.693476+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e53b29e59e81738e45376b2c2bf7cd67a9e4cec7a398428857e3bc2fd0e42ba8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:two-vortex of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$ satisfy
$\kappa_1>0>\kappa_2$, and let
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\in\Lambda_2(D)$ be a strict local
minimum point of $W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$.  Choose $\rho>0$ such that
\[
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Subset\Lambda_2(D),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  &>W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\\
  &\quad\text{for every }(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})}
  \setminus\{(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\}.
  \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Fix $M_i,R_i>0$ for $i=1,2$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$,
such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$(\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})$, and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=|\kappa_i|,
  \qquad
  \|\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty
  \leq M_i\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R_i\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}),
  \quad i=1,2.
\]
Set
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
:=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,0}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,0}$.
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper), and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t}$ denote the transport of
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}$ by the associated Euler flow map.
If
\begin{equation}
  \eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0})
  +\Bigl[W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\Bigr]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})
  \times\mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})
  \subset B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2}),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
  &\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  \Bigl[
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Bigr] \leq C\eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:40.352891+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e54419eb49572f4b1a442ecc64684351e4ef3ec96a2e3c53ebcaf1a66b6e10cb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 27 (Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] In these definitions, we use the notation $N(A)$ to denote the \emph{set of neighbors} of $A$ in $\Q$, rather than
the number of neighbors.
Additionally, $\cH$ denotes either $\cE$ or $\cO$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item
    A subset $A \sse \cH$ is said to be \emph{2-linked} if there is no decomposition $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ into
    nonempty sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ which satisfy $N(A_1) \cap N(A_2) = \emptyset$.

    \item 
    For a subset $A \sse \cH$, we denote by $[A]$ the \emph{closure} of $A$,
    defined to be the largest subset of $\cH$ with the same neighborhood set as $A$.
    In other words, $[A] = \{ v \in \cH : N(v) \sse N(A) \}$.

    \item
    A 2-linked set $\fp \sse \cH$ with $|[\fp]| \leq \fr{3}{4} 2^{d-1}$ is called a \emph{polymer}.

    \item
    Polymers $\fp_1$ and $\fp_2$ are said to be \emph{compatible} if $\fp_1 \cup \fp_2$ is not 2-linked.

    \item
		We denote by $\Sep[\cH]$ the set of pairwise compatible collections of polymers.
    
    \item
    The \emph{weight} of a polymer $\fp$ is $\omega(\fp) = \E[\phi_\fp]$, where $\phi_\fp = 2^{-\N(\fp)}$.
    We remind the reader that $\N(\fp)$ denotes the (random) number of vertices neighboring $\fp$
    in the percolated graph $\Qp$.

    \item
    We define \emph{clusters} and their weights as in the previous section, which is a general construction that
    works for all polymer models.
    The set of clusters will be denoted by $\cC^\cH$.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["P is a set of partial computable functions","P is nontrivial: neither empty nor all partial computable functions"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.378848+00:00","domain":"computability theory","id":"claim_e566adf01a15158b9f7ce6ec58f8cd9ca5acbd8ecb4145e42d80266d80928187","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Every nontrivial semantic property of programs is undecidable. Precisely: let P be any set of partial computable functions that is nontrivial, meaning some partial computable function belongs to P and some does not. Then the index set {encodings of Turing machines M : the partial function computed by M belongs to P} is undecidable. 'Semantic' is essential: the property must depend only on the function computed, not on the machine's text (syntactic properties such as 'has fewer than 100 states' are decidable). Only the two trivial semantic properties (satisfied by all machines, or by none) have decidable index sets. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.711571+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e57978c10a981cc93d2afda45609cec34cf4c0498a9c2e886466955cdbe993b0","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 (Separated multiscale flows) of arXiv:2609.01143, 'The voter model on the hyperbolic graph'] Fix $\varphi<1$, $\epsilon_0>0$, a sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$ and a sufficiently large fixed $\ell$.  Let $v$ be a prescribed point with
\[
h(v):=R-r_v\geq\left(\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon_0\right)R,
\]
and write $\vartheta(v)$ for its angular coordinate.  Put
\[
J:=\left\lfloor\frac{R-h(v)}{\ell}\right\rfloor, \qquad u_i:=i\ell,\quad 0\leq i\leq J.
\]

For each $i$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$, the construction uses $K_i$ initial half-tiles, where
\begin{equation}
K_i\asymp e^{h(v)/2}e^{-u_i/2}.                              
\end{equation}
There is a fixed $c>0$ such that, uniformly over the choices above, under the Palm law obtained by adding $v$ the construction for $(i,b)$ fails with probability at most $e^{-cK_i}$.  On success, whenever $v\in V(\cG)$, it produces a probability measure $\lambda_i^b$ and a unit flow $g_i^b$ on $\cG$ such that
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{div}g_i^b=\mathbbm{1}_v-\lambda_i^b,\qquad \cE_{\cG}(g_i^b)\leq\frac{C}{P_i},\qquad I_\varphi(\lambda_i^b)\leq\frac{C}{V_i},                         
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
P_i\asymp e^{h(v)/2}e^{-(2\alpha-1)u_i/2}, \qquad V_i\asymp e^{h(v)/2}e^{u_i/2}.                                 
\end{equation}

Let $Q_i^b$ be the support of $\lambda_i^b$, and let $S_i^b$ consist of $v$ and the endpoints of edges carrying nonzero $g_i^b$-flow.  Then $Q_i^b\subset S_i^b\setminus\{v\}$, every vertex in $Q_i^b$ has height $O(1)$ uniformly in $i$ and $b$, and every $x\in S_i^b\setminus\{v\}$ satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb S^1}(\vartheta(x),\vartheta(v))\leq \epsilon,
\]
and
\[
S_i^b\cap S_j^{b'}=\{v\}\qquad\text{whenever }(i,b)\ne(j,b').
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:10:43.950157+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e59f56fdaafaee95edcaef05d9ded5885484bee5ec668b08ca6744e1d151f602","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem mainThem of arXiv:2412.04527, 'Critical Drift for Brownian Bees and a Reflected Brownian Motion Invariance Principle'] Let $X^{N,\mu}=(X^{N,\mu}(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a one dimensional $N$-Brownian bee system with drift $\mu\in \mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu_c^N=v_N$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \underline{Sub-Critical Case}: when $|\mu| < \mu_c^N$, then for any $t_0>0$, the process $(X^{N,\mu}(nt_0))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is positive Harris recurrent and therefore has a unique stationary probability measure $\pi^{N,\mu}$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$ so that for any $\chi\in \mathbb{R}^N$
    \begin{equation*}
        \lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{C}|\mathbb{P}_{\chi}(X^{N,\mu}(t)\in C)-\pi^{N,\mu}(C)|_{TV}=0.
    \end{equation*}    
    where $|\cdot|_{TV}$ represents the total variation norm, the supremum is taken over all measurable sets, and $\mathbb{P}_\chi(\cdot):=\mathbb{P}(\cdot|X^{N,\mu}(0)=\chi)$.
    \item \underline{Critical Case}: When $|\mu |=\mu_c^N$, there is an invariance principle
    $$  
    \left(m^{-1/2}X^{N,\mu}(mt)\right)_{t\geq 0} \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{d} \left(\frac{\mu}{|\mu|}\beta^{-1/2}\sigma |B(t)|\underline{1}\right)_{t\geq 0}.
    $$
    in the Skorokhod topology on $\mathcal{D}([0,\infty),\mathbb{R}^N)$, the space of cadlag functions $[0,\infty)\to \mathbb{R}$, where $B$ is a standard Brownian motion, $\underline{1}=(1,\ldots,1)\in \mathbb{R}^N$, and $\beta,\sigma$ are constants which we will define later. 
    \item \underline{Super-Critical Case}: When $|\mu|>\mu_c^N$, $X^{N,\mu}$ is transient in the sense that each particle $X_i^{N,\mu}$ diverges to $\frac{\mu}{|\mu|}\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, and further
    $$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{X^{N,\mu}_1(t)}{t}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{X^{N,\mu}_N(t)}{t} = \left(|\mu| - \mu_c^N\right)\frac{\mu}{|\mu|} \quad \text{a.s.}$$
    where $X_i^{N,\mu}$ denotes the $i$\textsuperscript{th} smallest particle of 
    $X^{N,\mu}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:09.927340+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e59ff678b2bc58a245e9f0d44e77da148099443d31c5ff09853596a7a3e1069c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 (Supermartingale $C$-monotonicity.) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] The Borel set $\Gamma \subset \R \times \Pc_1$ is supermartingale $C$-monotone if and only if there exists $M_0, M_1 \subset \R$, such that for any $N \in \N$, any collection $(x_1, p_1), \cdots, (x_N, p_N) \in \Gamma$ and $q_1, \cdots q_N \in \Pc_1$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i = \sum_{i=1}^{N} q_i$ and 
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy)= \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_1; \\
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy) \geq \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_0,
\end{aligned}
$$
 we have
 $$
 \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, p_i) \leq  \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, q_i).
 $$
where, $\mathcal{I}_0=\{i : x_i \in M_0 \}$, $\mathcal{I}_1=\{i : x_i \in M_1 \}$. In the following, we say a coupling $\pi \in \Pi_S(\mu, \nu)$ is Supermartingale $C$-monotone if there exists a Supermartingale $C$-monotone set $\Gamma$ with 
$$
(x, \pi_x) \in \Gamma \ \ \mbox{for } \mu(dx) \mbox{-almost every }x,
$$ 
with $M_0, M_1$ defined as the martingale region of $\pi$ to the left and right of $x^*$ (recall that $x^*$ is defined in Section \ref{sec:irreducible})  {In addition, a probability measure $\P \in \Pc(\R \times \Pc_1$, which is supported on a martingale $C$-monotone set, is called supermartingale $C$-monotone. }","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.096857+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e5ace840b7a802a63627f4607d2573244712aad61251eef12fdf70c6287c7bb4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:ribbon-majorant of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a ribbon record $\Gamma$, a circuit state $\tau$, and a designated
set $\mathcal E$ of factored endpoint or packet resources.  Expand every
remaining coefficient component in its circuit-anchored projective
presentation and insert every prescribed fixed gate before closing the
original circuit bases.  Define $\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\tau;\mathcal E}$
to be $|\omega_\Gamma|$ times the sum of the absolute scalar
coefficients multiplied by all remaining positive projective and
trace-class costs.  No endpoint weight or debit in $\mathcal E$ is
included.  In the monomer--dimer applications of (sec:moments of the paper), the
fixed recurrence scalar $(-\gamma)^a$ is also declared a factored
resource: it is not one of the ``scalar coefficients'' in this
definition and is restored exactly once by the resource ledger.

inside the majorant.  When $\tau$ and $\mathcal E$ are clear we write
$\mathfrak a_\Gamma$; subscripts such as
$\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}$ name the part of the record left open.

This is a positive presentation cost, not the possibly cancelling value
of an open contraction.  Consequently it dominates every compatible
partial trace-class contraction obtained from the same atoms.  The
operator-norm estimate needed for the Kac root-open specialization is the
separate, proved statement (lem:root-open-sinfty of the paper); it is not built
into this definition and no replica factorization is assumed.  The later
allocation argument specifies
which carriers are left bare and proves the corresponding Euler bound;
no second copy of this majorant is introduced there.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Conclusion is constancy on the closure of U x [0,t_0] only","U must be connected","The maximum must be attained at a point with x_0 in U and t_0 > 0"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.106923+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations","id":"claim_e5db45cf444dc11d943ed80dd9009a1a1904ce853e38b9031ae8a4e06c9b3559","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"If a solution of the heat equation attains its maximum over $\\overline{U_T}$ at an interior point $(x_0,t_0)\\in U_T$, the conclusion is that $u$ is constant on $\\overline U\\times[0,t_0]$ -- the past of $t_0$ -- and nothing at all is claimed for $t>t_0$. Heat is not time-reversible, and the mean value property over heat balls only looks backwards. Counterexample: on $U=(0,\\pi)$, $T=2$, let $h(t)=1$ for $t\\le1$ and $h(t)=1-e^{-1/(t-1)}$ for $t>1$ (smooth, $h\\le1$, $h<1$ for $t>1$), and let $u$ be the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}$ with $u(\\cdot,0)\\equiv1$ and $u(0,t)=u(\\pi,t)=h(t)$. On $[0,1]$, $u\\equiv1$ by uniqueness; the weak maximum principle gives $\\max_{\\overline{U_T}}u=1$, attained at the interior point $(\\pi/2,1)\\in U_T$; but for $t>1$, $u$ is not constant (its boundary values are $<1$ while, by continuity, $u$ stays near $1$ in the middle). So constancy holds exactly up to $t_0=1$ and fails afterwards. A second load-bearing hypothesis is connectedness of $U$: for $U=(0,1)\\cup(2,3)$ the solution equal to $1$ on the first component and to $e^{-\\lambda_1t}\\phi_1$ on the second attains its maximum at an interior point of the first component and is not constant on $U$. Finally, the interior maximum must be attained in $U_T$, i.e. at a point with $x_0\\in U$: a maximum on the lateral boundary says nothing about constancy (that is the Hopf lemma's domain, which asserts instead that the outward normal derivative is strictly positive there).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The counterexample uses H(p) = p^2 (smooth, uniformly convex) and zero data, so no exotic Hamiltonian is needed","'Solution a.e.' means Lipschitz plus the equation at points of differentiability","Uniqueness is restored by the viscosity property or, equivalently for convex superlinear H, by the semiconcavity bound of the Hopf-Lax solution"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.418105+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: Hamilton-Jacobi equations","id":"claim_e6002f2b1fb67f105d5effe237759fa92f79220ba532358144c459114f6ad305","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: in any uniqueness statement for u_t + H(Du) = 0 the solution must be a VISCOSITY solution (equivalently, for convex superlinear H, a Lipschitz a.e. solution satisfying the one-sided semiconcavity estimate). Satisfying the equation at almost every point plus the initial condition is far too weak. Counterexample (n = 1): H(p) = p^2, initial datum g ≡ 0. Both u ≡ 0 and v(x,t) := min(0, |x| - t) are Lipschitz on R × [0,∞), vanish at t = 0, and satisfy v_t + v_x^2 = 0 at every point of differentiability: for |x| < t one has v = |x| - t, v_t = -1, v_x = ±1; for |x| > t one has v ≡ 0. Only u ≡ 0 is the viscosity solution (it is also what the Hopf-Lax formula gives, since L(q) = q^2/4 and min_y ( |x-y|^2/(4t) ) = 0). Why v fails: at a point (0,t) with t > 0, v has a local minimum in x with a convex kink, so φ ≡ v(0,t) + c(t'-t) touches from below with φ_x = 0, φ_t = -1, and the supersolution inequality φ_t + φ_x^2 ≥ 0 reads -1 ≥ 0. Equivalently v violates semiconcavity: v(z,t) - 2v(0,t) + v(-z,t) = 2|z|, which is not O(|z|^2). Auditor's check: whenever a proof concludes 'u is the solution' from 'u is Lipschitz and solves the PDE a.e.', the argument is incomplete unless viscosity, semiconcavity, or a variational (Hopf-Lax) representation is verified.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:37:51.440284+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e601fdc2218ff22f2633ec3dc21aed26185ba1ca6b62b536720b81495874d3bf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 (Necessary Maximum Principle for Games) of arXiv:2604.02998, 'Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games for Controlled Convection-Diffusion SPDEs'] Let $(\hat u_1,\hat u_2)\in\mathcal U_1\times\mathcal U_2$

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:32:11.153410+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e6142a3f45c20d3df0e2acadb0566dc2b27b8c92aa0a7d38cb5b5103947e66ba","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:RBG of arXiv:2510.13733, 'Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation \\ with Critical Branching Random Walks'] Let $R_1 < R_2$ be two integer numbers,
set  $H = R_2 - R_1$. 
Let $\eta : \mathbb{Z}^d \to  \mathbb{N}$
be the initial particle configuration
with support in $\partial B_{R_1}$
and number of particles $N_1 = \sum_{z \in 
\partial B_{R_1}} \eta(z)$. 
Let further $Z_1, \ldots Z_{N_1}$ be i.i.d.\  random variables with distribution 
 supported in   $ \{1, \ldots,  H\} $  given by
\begin{equation}
P( Z_i = h) = \frac{ h^{d-1} }{\sum_{r =1 }^H  r^{d-1}},
\end{equation}
The $\{ Z_i\}$ represent the sequence of heights at which the BRWs will probe the space for settlement. 

The RBG consists of a discrete time
Markov chain  $(A_t)_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$
and a sequence of random variables 
$(  \tilde G_t,  \tilde R_t)_{  t \in \mathbb{N}_0  }$,
 defined as follows. 
We set $A_0 =  \emptyset$ 
and label the particles in $\eta$ with integers from $1$ to $N_1$ in some arbitrary order. 
At each step $t \in \{1, \ldots, N_1\}$, 
we start, from the $t$-th particle of $\eta$, an independent BRW
stopped on $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$ 
and let $\xi_t$ be the configuration of pioneers  on $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$.
We define the aggregate of the step $t$ as 
the union of the aggregate of the step $t-1$ and 
the support of the  pioneers configuration,  namely 
$$
A_t := A_{t-1} \cup \{ z \in \partial  B_{ R_1 + Z_t  } \, \, : \,   \xi_t(z) > 0     \}.
$$
After that we proceed as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
For each particle reaching $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$ within 
$A_{t-1}$ we start an independent critical branching random walk stopped on
$\partial B_{ R_2  }$  and call $\tilde{G}_t$ the total number of pioneers 
on $\partial B_{ R_2  }$, which we dub \textit{green particles}.
\item[(b)]  
For each vertex 
 $ x \in \partial  B_{ R_1 + Z_t  } \setminus A_{t-1}$
 with $\xi_t(x)>0$,
 we let exactly one of the $\xi_t(x)$ particles at $x$ settle
 and  start 
 $(\xi_t(x) - 1) \1_{ \{ \xi_t(x)>0 \}  }$
  independent critical branching random walks
 stopped on $ B_{ R_2  }$ from $x$, 
 namely one critical Branching Random Walk from each particle which has not settled at $x$. 
 We call $\tilde{R}_t$ 
 be the total number of pioneers on $\partial B_{ R_2  }$,
 which we dub \textit{red particles}.
\end{enumerate}
We then move to the step $t+1$ and iterate the procedure
up to reaching $t = N_1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:59.496248+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e6248aa0074ed65c0cb416759fb98cfbee64e1b86f405d7a62cdf77ef9f92b0d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 (First-break localization and tails) of arXiv:2605.09641, 'The Ballot Event for Two-Player Coupon Collection: A Renewal--Catalan Asymptotic'] Let $K_d$ be the extended first-break level defined by
\[
        \Prob(K_d=k)=\pi_{d,k}\quad(1\le k\le d-1),
        \qquad
        \Prob(K_d=d)=\rho_d,
\]
where
\[
        \rho_d:=\prod_{r=1}^{d-1}\frac{d-r}{d+r}
\]
is the probability that no one-sided tie-break occurs before simultaneous completion.  Thus the value $K_d=d$ records this exceptional terminal event.  Then
\[
        \frac{K_d}{\sqrt d}\Rightarrow X,
        \qquad
        \Prob(X\in \dd x)=2x e^{-x^2}\Ind_{\{x>0\}}\dd x .
\]
In particular,
\[
        K_d\to\infty,
        \qquad
        \frac{K_d}{d}\to0
\]
in probability.  More precisely, for $k=o(d)$,
\[
        \prod_{r=1}^{k-1}\frac{d-r}{d+r}
        =\exp\left(-\frac{k(k-1)}{d}+O\left(\frac{k^4}{d^3}\right)\right),
\]
and there are absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that, for every $R\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $d$,
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{k\ge R\sqrt{d\log d}}\pi_{d,k}
        \le C d^{-cR^2}+e^{-cd}.
\end{equation}
More generally, for every $M\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $d$,
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{k\ge M\sqrt d}\pi_{d,k}
        \le C e^{-cM^2}+e^{-cd}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $R$ large enough the tail in
\eqref{eq:first-break-tail} is $o(d^{-1})$.","status":"unverified"}

(1).    For $H\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, sample the walk  $W(t)$ in $\tilde{\mathcal{W}}(\cdot,H,L;N)$.

        View both $\ul\textup{Rep}^\oplus$ and $\ul\textup{Rep}^\amalg_\delta$ as functors $\text{Fin}_*\to\mathbb\Spc_{\textup{Glo}}$ satisfying the Segal condition. Then the map $\lim F_\oplus\to\lim{\textup{Hom}}\big(\textup{Rep}^\oplus(-),\textup{Rep}^\oplus(-)\big)\simeq{\textup{End}}(\ul\textup{Rep}^\oplus)$ induced by the inclusion is a monomorphism (as a limit of monomorphisms), and its image consists precisely of those natural transformations whose underlying functor is the identity.         \[
            \lim_{\alpha\colon\langle r\rangle\to\langle s\rangle}\hskip0pt minus 15ptF_\oplus(\alpha)\to
            \lim_{\alpha\colon\langle r\rangle\to\langle s\rangle}\hskip0pt minus 15pt{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\textup{Rep}^\amalg_\delta(\langle r\rangle),\ul\textup{Rep}^\oplus(\langle s\rangle))\gets

        \end{equation}
        are monomorphisms with the same image. 

        By construction, the image of the first map is the component of $\ul\textup{Rep}^\oplus(\alpha)\circ|{\cdot}|$, while the image of the second one is the component of $|{\cdot}|\circ\ul\textup{Rep}^\amalg_\delta(\alpha)$, and these maps are indeed homotopic.         \begin{align*}

            {\textup{Hom}}\big(\ul\textup{Rep}^\amalg_\delta(\langle r\rangle), \ul\textup{Rep}^\amalg_\delta(\langle s\rangle)\big)&\xrightarro","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.829831+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e6519770ff6242721d8351d347d9b989b931c291c91b2bcdc03248dd2cf970f0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 20 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01} and 
that the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}.  
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,   we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Fix $\wt b_0 \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b_0) \in \supp \nu$. 
Then, for every character $\chi$ of the group $M/M_0^{\mu}$, the operator $P_{\mu, \chi}$ 
has a unique eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi}$ of modulus one in the space $W_{\chi}^{0}$. 

Moreover, there exists a unique associated eigenvector $\varphi_{\chi} \in W_{\chi}^{0}$
such that $\varphi_{\chi}(\wt b_0) = 1$ and $\varphi_{\chi}$ is H\"older continuous on $\wt B$.  
Also, the generalized eigenspace associated with the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi}$ for the operator $P_{\mu, \chi}$ acting on the space $W_{\chi}^0$ 
is equal to $\bb C \varphi_{\chi}$, that is, this eigenvalue is multiplicity free. 

Finally, the restriction $\varphi_{\chi}|_{\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)}$ is the unique continuous function on $\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)$
such that $\varphi_{\chi}(\wt b_0) = 1$ and for every $m \in M$,  $g \in \supp \mu$ and $\wt b \in \eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)$, we have 
\begin{align}
\varphi_{\chi}(\wt b m) = \chi(m)^{-1} \varphi_{\chi}(\wt b)
\quad \mbox{and} \quad
\varphi_{\chi}(g \wt b) = \lambda_{\chi} \varphi_{\chi}(\wt b). 
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:07.026898+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e6527e14ca4bddf7fc28a6c130026b7a7a098d8dfc016137377a8de8c2a08911","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:poly_limit_scaled of arXiv:2607.27810, 'Perturbed Beta Corners Process'] Let $a_N=\frac{\beta}{2}\mathsf{a}_N$ with $\mathsf{a}_N\ne0$ fixed, let
$\boldsymbol{\mu}=(\mu_1>\cdots>\mu_{N-1})$ be fixed and not depend on $\beta$, and let random
$\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ be obtained from $\boldsymbol{\mu}$
through~(equation eq:random_poly_general of the paper). Then, as $\beta\to\infty$:
\begin{enumerate}[\normalfont(i)]
	\item $N-1$ of the roots stay bounded and converge in probability to the roots of
	\begin{equation}
		
		\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\frac{1}{x-\mu_i}=-\mathsf{a}_N,
		\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
		D_{\mathsf{a}_N}P_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}(x)
		= P_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}'(x)+\mathsf{a}_N P_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}(x)=0 .
	\end{equation}
	(prop:shifted_derivative of the paper), applied to $P_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$, locates
	these $N-1$ roots: exactly $N-2$ of them interlace with $\boldsymbol{\mu}$,
	one in each gap $(\mu_{i+1},\mu_i)$, and the last lies outside the range of
	$\boldsymbol{\mu}$ --- below $\mu_{N-1}$ if $\mathsf{a}_N>0$, above $\mu_1$
	if $\mathsf{a}_N<0$.
	\item The remaining root escapes on the scale of the perturbation:
	$\dfrac{2}{\beta}\max_j|\lambda_j|\to|\mathsf{a}_N|$,
	the unbounded root having the sign of $\mathsf{a}_N$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}
